mf-skill-d1d071c77fd998de.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-d1d071c77fd998de.Prerequisite Names: Inverse functions; Chain rule; Evaluating Expressions Containing Inverse Trigonometric Functions; The Chain Rule With Trigonometric Functions; Differentiating Inverse Functions
mf-skill-d1d071c77fd998de.Skill Description: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Differentiate arcsin, arccos, and arctan, and combine these formulas with the chain rule.

mf-skill-002e3f86a19d5000.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-002e3f86a19d5000.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Second-Degree Taylor Polynomials; Selecting Procedures for Calculating Derivatives
mf-skill-002e3f86a19d5000.Skill Description: Third-Degree Taylor Polynomials — Add the cubic term f'''(a)(x − a)³/6 to a quadratic approximation to capture how curvature changes near the center.

mf-skill-046c9bd3084d116b.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-046c9bd3084d116b.Skill Name: Using Differentiation to Calculate Critical Points
mf-skill-046c9bd3084d116b.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Global vs. Local Extrema and Critical Points; Selecting Procedures for Calculating Derivatives
mf-skill-046c9bd3084d116b.Skill Description: Using Differentiation to Calculate Critical Points — Differentiate a function and find where the derivative is zero or undefined within the domain to locate its critical points.

mf-skill-f33615ac69b1f837.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-f33615ac69b1f837.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-f33615ac69b1f837.Skill Description: Calculating Definite Integrals Using Substitution — Evaluate definite integrals by substitution, converting the limits to the new variable or returning to the original before evaluating.

mf-skill-70b5ea196ae53fad.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-70b5ea196ae53fad.Skill Name: Further Integration of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
mf-skill-70b5ea196ae53fad.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-70b5ea196ae53fad.Skill Description: Further Integration of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution — Use substitution on algebraic integrals where the leftover x must be rewritten in terms of the new variable.

mf-skill-b6676c71cac1cf39.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-b6676c71cac1cf39.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integrating Exponential Functions Using Linear Substitution; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-b6676c71cac1cf39.Skill Description: Integrating Exponential Functions Using Substitution — Integrate expressions containing e raised to a function of x by substituting for the exponent.

mf-skill-8732c4ffe2bb27e6.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-8732c4ffe2bb27e6.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial division; Completing the square; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Dividing Polynomials Using Long Division; Integrating Linear Rational Functions Using Substitution
mf-skill-8732c4ffe2bb27e6.Skill Description: Integrating Functions Using Polynomial Division — Divide polynomials first when a rational integrand's numerator degree is at least the denominator's, then integrate the pieces.

mf-skill-e4b987d67d586d04.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-e4b987d67d586d04.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integrating the Reciprocal Function; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-e4b987d67d586d04.Skill Description: Integrating Logarithmic Functions Using Substitution — Use substitution for integrands involving ln x or of the form f'(x)/f(x), producing logarithmic or power results.

mf-skill-6d7a9498c8e3d262.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-6d7a9498c8e3d262.Skill Name: Integrating Rational Functions Using Partial Fractions
mf-skill-6d7a9498c8e3d262.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial division; Rational expressions and restrictions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Expressing Rational Functions as Sums of Partial Fractions; Integrating Linear Rational Functions Using Substitution
mf-skill-6d7a9498c8e3d262.Skill Description: Integrating Rational Functions Using Partial Fractions — Split a proper rational function into simpler fractions over its linear denominator factors and integrate each one.

mf-skill-369c37b8c5cc9f86.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-369c37b8c5cc9f86.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integrating Trigonometric Functions; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-369c37b8c5cc9f86.Skill Description: Integrating Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution — Use u-substitution on integrals involving sine, cosine and other trig functions of an inner expression or with a matching derivative factor.

mf-skill-c6fe383cf4d91d6a.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-c6fe383cf4d91d6a.Prerequisite Names: Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Fundamental theorem of calculus; The Product Rule for Differentiation; Integration Using Substitution
mf-skill-c6fe383cf4d91d6a.Skill Description: Introduction to Integration by Parts — Integrate products of functions with ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du, derived from the product rule.

mf-skill-6cd7b6be5136d545.Subject: Limits & Continuity

mf-skill-6cd7b6be5136d545.Skill Description: L'Hopital's Rule — Evaluate limits of the indeterminate forms 0/0 or ∞/∞ by taking the limit of the ratio of derivatives instead.

mf-skill-165a77e028f51f13.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-165a77e028f51f13.Skill Name: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration
mf-skill-165a77e028f51f13.Prerequisite Names: Higher derivatives; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Calculating the Displacement of a Particle Using Integration; Finding the Area Between a Curve and the X-Axis When They Intersect
mf-skill-165a77e028f51f13.Skill Description: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration — Use integrals of velocity and acceleration to find an object's position, displacement, and total distance traveled along a line.

mf-skill-ec8cd2ab8be447d9.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-ec8cd2ab8be447d9.Skill Name: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration
mf-skill-ec8cd2ab8be447d9.Prerequisite Names: Parametric curves; Vector components and arithmetic; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Finding Velocity Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration; Calculating the Displacement of a Particle Using Integration
mf-skill-ec8cd2ab8be447d9.Skill Description: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration — Integrate each component of a two-dimensional velocity vector to find the net change in position over a time interval.

mf-skill-a7b04137d3579ffc.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-a7b04137d3579ffc.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; The Chain Rule for Differentiation; Rates of Change in Applied Contexts
mf-skill-a7b04137d3579ffc.Skill Description: Introduction to Related Rates — Find how fast one quantity changes by differentiating an equation that links it to another quantity whose rate is known.

mf-skill-511fdff48af56a7e.Subject: Definite Integrals

mf-skill-511fdff48af56a7e.Skill Description: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Function Given Its Graph — Evaluate a definite integral from a graph by adding areas of geometric shapes, counting regions below the axis as negative.

mf-skill-78acb7dc31dc38fd.Subject: Definite Integrals
mf-skill-78acb7dc31dc38fd.Prerequisite Names: Functions, domains, and ranges; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Limits of Piecewise Functions; Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration
mf-skill-78acb7dc31dc38fd.Skill Description: Definite Integrals of Piecewise Functions — Integrate a function defined by different formulas on different intervals by splitting the integral at each breakpoint.

mf-skill-76368ab232e2a5bb.Subject: Definite Integrals
mf-skill-76368ab232e2a5bb.Prerequisite Names: Functions, domains, and ranges; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Even and Odd Functions; Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration
mf-skill-76368ab232e2a5bb.Skill Description: Evaluating Definite Integrals Using Symmetry — Simplify definite integrals over intervals symmetric about zero by recognizing even and odd integrands.

mf-skill-d9e015be92fddd17.Subject: Definite Integrals
mf-skill-d9e015be92fddd17.Skill Name: The Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of X
mf-skill-d9e015be92fddd17.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Surface area and volume; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Finding the Area Between a Curve and the X-Axis When They Intersect
mf-skill-d9e015be92fddd17.Skill Description: The Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of X — Find the area between two curves y = f(x) and y = g(x) by integrating the top function minus the bottom function.

mf-skill-9108305965dccfea.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-9108305965dccfea.Prerequisite Names: Local linear approximation; Differential equations and initial values; Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization; Verifying Solutions of Differential Equations
mf-skill-9108305965dccfea.Skill Description: Euler's Method: Calculating One Step — Take a single Euler step, using the slope at the current point to estimate the next value of a solution.

mf-skill-749e027f201aac37.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-749e027f201aac37.Skill Name: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Direct Integration
mf-skill-749e027f201aac37.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Derivative as local rate; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integration Using Substitution; Verifying Solutions of Differential Equations
mf-skill-749e027f201aac37.Skill Description: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Direct Integration — Solve a differential equation of the form dy/dx = f(x) by integrating the right-hand side directly and adding a constant.

mf-skill-c70ce0f936349a80.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-c70ce0f936349a80.Skill Name: Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
mf-skill-c70ce0f936349a80.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Increasing and Decreasing Functions; Using Differentiation to Calculate Critical Points
mf-skill-c70ce0f936349a80.Skill Description: Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing — Use the sign of the first derivative to find the intervals where a function rises or falls.

mf-skill-db98ef613fa62b21.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-db98ef613fa62b21.Prerequisite Names: Inverse functions; Chain rule; Differentiating Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions; Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-db98ef613fa62b21.Skill Description: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions — Differentiate arcsec, arccsc, and arccot, including chain-rule versions and the range conventions they depend on.

mf-skill-5ae96b7220835593.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-5ae96b7220835593.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Sigma Notation; Third-Degree Taylor Polynomials
mf-skill-5ae96b7220835593.Skill Description: Higher-Degree Taylor Polynomials — Build Taylor polynomials of degree n and use the remainder estimate to choose a degree that meets an accuracy target.

mf-skill-ac89f0fec091eb0f.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-ac89f0fec091eb0f.Prerequisite Names: Inverse functions; Chain rule; The Sum Rule for Indefinite Integrals; Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-ac89f0fec091eb0f.Skill Description: Integration Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Evaluate integrals whose antiderivatives are arcsin, arctan, or arcsec, often after substitution or completing the square.

mf-skill-f4f1f97ab6ca234f.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-f4f1f97ab6ca234f.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; The Extreme Value Theorem; Using Differentiation to Calculate Critical Points
mf-skill-f4f1f97ab6ca234f.Skill Description: The Candidates Test — Find the absolute maximum and minimum of a continuous function on a closed interval by comparing values at critical points and endpoints.

mf-skill-f29a05ea25101665.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-f29a05ea25101665.Skill Name: Applying the Integration By Parts Twice
mf-skill-f29a05ea25101665.Prerequisite Names: Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Introduction to Integration by Parts
mf-skill-f29a05ea25101665.Skill Description: Applying the Integration By Parts Twice — Apply integration by parts a second time when the first application leaves an integral that still needs the same technique.

mf-skill-1e3d00e6b0a83143.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-1e3d00e6b0a83143.Prerequisite Names: Limits of functions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Limits of Exponential Functions; Calculating Definite Integrals Using Substitution
mf-skill-1e3d00e6b0a83143.Skill Description: Improper Integrals Involving Exponential Functions — Evaluate integrals of exponential functions over infinite intervals by taking limits, checking whether the exponential decays.

mf-skill-c81f4b5b461fcfa1.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-c81f4b5b461fcfa1.Skill Name: Integrating Rational Functions with Repeated Factors
mf-skill-c81f4b5b461fcfa1.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial division; Rational expressions and restrictions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Expressing Rational Functions with Repeated Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions; Integrating Rational Functions Using Partial Fractions
mf-skill-c81f4b5b461fcfa1.Skill Description: Integrating Rational Functions with Repeated Factors — Integrate rational functions with a repeated linear factor, using one partial fraction per power and integrating each to a logarithm or a power.

mf-skill-11e33b1c8fb9b862.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-11e33b1c8fb9b862.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric identities; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Simplifying Expressions Using Basic Trigonometric Identities; Integrating Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution
mf-skill-11e33b1c8fb9b862.Skill Description: Integration Using Basic Trigonometric Identities — Rewrite trig integrands with reciprocal and quotient identities so they match antiderivatives you already know.

mf-skill-3e17b73b7004f50f.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-3e17b73b7004f50f.Skill Name: Using Integration by Parts to Calculate Integrals With Logarithms
mf-skill-3e17b73b7004f50f.Prerequisite Names: Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Differentiating Logarithmic Functions; Introduction to Integration by Parts
mf-skill-3e17b73b7004f50f.Skill Description: Using Integration by Parts to Calculate Integrals With Logarithms — Integrate ln x and products involving logarithms by choosing u = ln x in integration by parts.

mf-skill-f08781364aab9457.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-f08781364aab9457.Prerequisite Names: Parametric curves; Vector components and arithmetic; Fundamental theorem of calculus; The Arc Length of a Planar Curve; Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration
mf-skill-f08781364aab9457.Skill Description: Calculating Displacement for Plane Motion — Find the net change in position of an object moving in a plane by integrating each velocity component.

mf-skill-b6a7b5fbd3d3ca23.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-b6a7b5fbd3d3ca23.Skill Name: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Differentiation
mf-skill-b6a7b5fbd3d3ca23.Prerequisite Names: Higher derivatives; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Calculating Acceleration for Straight-Line Motion Using Differentiation; Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
mf-skill-b6a7b5fbd3d3ca23.Skill Description: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Differentiation — Use velocity and acceleration found by differentiation to decide when an object is at rest, turns around, speeds up or slows down.

mf-skill-96bf1c3b9e8d970e.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-96bf1c3b9e8d970e.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; Calculating Slopes of Circles, Ellipses, and Parabolas; Introduction to Related Rates
mf-skill-96bf1c3b9e8d970e.Skill Description: Related Rates With Implicit Functions — Solve related rates problems where the linking equation is implicit, differentiating every variable with respect to time.

mf-skill-d3ce85346c610865.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-d3ce85346c610865.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; Rates of Change in Applied Contexts; The Candidates Test
mf-skill-d3ce85346c610865.Skill Description: Solving Optimization Problems Using Derivatives — Find the largest or smallest value of a quantity in a practical problem by modeling it as a function and using derivatives.

mf-skill-19c09c0d1c636c54.Subject: Definite Integrals
mf-skill-19c09c0d1c636c54.Skill Name: The Integral as an Accumulation Function
mf-skill-19c09c0d1c636c54.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Calculating the Definite Integral of a Function Given Its Graph
mf-skill-19c09c0d1c636c54.Skill Description: The Integral as an Accumulation Function — Treat an integral with a variable upper limit as a function that tracks accumulated quantity as the limit changes.

mf-skill-3a54a5e8065b13ad.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-3a54a5e8065b13ad.Prerequisite Names: Local linear approximation; Differential equations and initial values; Recursive Sequences; Euler's Method: Calculating One Step
mf-skill-3a54a5e8065b13ad.Skill Description: Euler's Method: Calculating Multiple Steps — Repeat Euler's method step by step to approximate a solution of a differential equation over a longer interval.

mf-skill-3b5afedbd7cf161c.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-3b5afedbd7cf161c.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Derivative as local rate; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Verifying Solutions of Differential Equations; Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
mf-skill-3b5afedbd7cf161c.Skill Description: Qualitative Analysis of First-Order ODEs — Describe how solutions of a first-order ODE behave using slope fields, equilibrium solutions, and sign analysis without solving it.

mf-skill-ec4491cd8166b3c7.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-ec4491cd8166b3c7.Skill Name: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Separation of Variables
mf-skill-ec4491cd8166b3c7.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Derivative as local rate; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integrating the Reciprocal Function; Solving First-Order ODEs Using Direct Integration
mf-skill-ec4491cd8166b3c7.Skill Description: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Separation of Variables — Solve first-order equations of the form dy/dx = g(x)h(y) by moving each variable to its own side and integrating.

mf-skill-e4d2473ebe130132.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-e4d2473ebe130132.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Second and Higher-Order Derivatives; Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
mf-skill-e4d2473ebe130132.Skill Description: Intervals of Concavity — Find where a graph is concave up or concave down by locating zeros of f'' and testing its sign on each interval.

mf-skill-27971e9da07f4251.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-27971e9da07f4251.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Convergent and Divergent Infinite Series; Higher-Degree Taylor Polynomials
mf-skill-27971e9da07f4251.Skill Description: Taylor Series — Extend Taylor polynomials to an infinite series and determine where that series converges to the function.

mf-skill-021834a57513b2ce.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-021834a57513b2ce.Skill Name: Using the First Derivative Test to Classify Local Extrema
mf-skill-021834a57513b2ce.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
mf-skill-021834a57513b2ce.Skill Description: Using the First Derivative Test to Classify Local Extrema — Classify a critical point as a local maximum, local minimum, or neither by checking how the sign of f' changes across it.

mf-skill-b03ab15b7fe27aab.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-b03ab15b7fe27aab.Prerequisite Names: Limits of functions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Improper Integrals Involving Exponential Functions; Integration Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-b03ab15b7fe27aab.Skill Description: Improper Integrals Involving Arctangent — Evaluate improper integrals whose antiderivative is an arctangent, using its limits of ±π/2 at infinity.

mf-skill-75a8fafa150b158b.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-75a8fafa150b158b.Skill Name: Integration by Parts in Cyclic Cases
mf-skill-75a8fafa150b158b.Prerequisite Names: Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Applying the Integration By Parts Twice
mf-skill-75a8fafa150b158b.Skill Description: Integration by Parts in Cyclic Cases — Apply integration by parts twice until the original integral reappears, then solve for it algebraically.

mf-skill-b62308928451ce34.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-b62308928451ce34.Skill Name: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-b62308928451ce34.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Integration Using Substitution; Integration Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-b62308928451ce34.Skill Description: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Recognize integrals that produce arcsin or arctan and use substitution to fit them to those standard forms.

mf-skill-758dc35e7d060276.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-758dc35e7d060276.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric identities; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Simplifying Expressions Using the Pythagorean Identity; Integration Using Basic Trigonometric Identities
mf-skill-758dc35e7d060276.Skill Description: Integration Using the Pythagorean Identities — Apply sin² x + cos² x = 1 and its variants to rewrite trig powers into integrable forms.

mf-skill-dd8f1856ab12c784.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-dd8f1856ab12c784.Skill Name: Calculating Related Rates Using the Pythagorean Theorem
mf-skill-dd8f1856ab12c784.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; The Pythagorean Theorem; Related Rates With Implicit Functions
mf-skill-dd8f1856ab12c784.Skill Description: Calculating Related Rates Using the Pythagorean Theorem — Solve related-rates problems in which lengths are tied by a² + b² = c², such as sliding ladders or separating cars.

mf-skill-e86900830c1cfbe0.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-e86900830c1cfbe0.Skill Name: Calculating Related Rates With Circles and Spheres
mf-skill-e86900830c1cfbe0.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; Volumes of Spheres; Related Rates With Implicit Functions
mf-skill-e86900830c1cfbe0.Skill Description: Calculating Related Rates With Circles and Spheres — Relate the changing radius of a circle or sphere to the rate of change of its area, circumference or volume.

mf-skill-9e9cb0356448a3da.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-9e9cb0356448a3da.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; Distances Between Points in the Coordinate Plane; Solving Optimization Problems Using Derivatives
mf-skill-9e9cb0356448a3da.Skill Description: Optimizing Distances — Minimize or maximize a distance, such as from a point to a line or between two moving objects, using derivatives.

mf-skill-fe0205a0b0673f7d.Subject: Definite Integrals
mf-skill-fe0205a0b0673f7d.Skill Name: The Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
mf-skill-fe0205a0b0673f7d.Prerequisite Names: Chain rule; Fundamental theorem of calculus; The Chain Rule for Differentiation; The Integral as an Accumulation Function
mf-skill-fe0205a0b0673f7d.Skill Description: The Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus — Differentiate an integral with a variable limit: the derivative equals the integrand at that limit, times the limit's derivative.

mf-skill-e2e28d2c7a28e1a1.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-e2e28d2c7a28e1a1.Skill Name: Solving First-Order IVPs Using Separation of Variables
mf-skill-e2e28d2c7a28e1a1.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Derivative as local rate; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Solving Equations Containing the Exponential Function; Solving First-Order ODEs Using Separation of Variables
mf-skill-e2e28d2c7a28e1a1.Skill Description: Solving First-Order IVPs Using Separation of Variables — Solve a separable first-order equation, then use the given initial condition to determine the constant and the particular solution.

mf-skill-017a6d1de86675b1.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-017a6d1de86675b1.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Taylor Series
mf-skill-017a6d1de86675b1.Skill Description: Maclaurin Series — Represent a function as a power series centred at x = 0, with coefficients built from its derivatives there.

mf-skill-210e26ae21804b91.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-210e26ae21804b91.Skill Name: Relating Concavity to the Second Derivative
mf-skill-210e26ae21804b91.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Intervals of Concavity
mf-skill-210e26ae21804b91.Skill Description: Relating Concavity to the Second Derivative — Interpret the second derivative as the rate of change of slope and use it to explain why a graph bends up or down.

mf-skill-fb7bf0f41f749ef2.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-fb7bf0f41f749ef2.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Finding the Sum of an Infinite Geometric Series; Taylor Series
mf-skill-fb7bf0f41f749ef2.Skill Description: Representing Functions as Power Series — Write functions as power series by adapting known series such as the geometric series, and state where they converge.

mf-skill-844ab65ef50c24e9.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-844ab65ef50c24e9.Skill Name: Improper Integrals Over the Real Line
mf-skill-844ab65ef50c24e9.Prerequisite Names: Limits of functions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Improper Integrals Involving Arctangent
mf-skill-844ab65ef50c24e9.Skill Description: Improper Integrals Over the Real Line — Evaluate integrals from −∞ to ∞ by splitting at a point and requiring both one-sided improper integrals to converge.

mf-skill-967fd4c265d73af2.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-967fd4c265d73af2.Skill Name: Integrating Functions by Completing the Square
mf-skill-967fd4c265d73af2.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial division; Completing the square; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Completing the Square With Leading Coefficients; Integration by Substitution With Inverse Trigonometric Functions
mf-skill-967fd4c265d73af2.Skill Description: Integrating Functions by Completing the Square — Rewrite a quadratic under a fraction or root as a shifted square so a standard integral such as arctan applies.

mf-skill-af0cba2e8c6a8dd2.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-af0cba2e8c6a8dd2.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric identities; Fundamental theorem of calculus; The Double-Angle Formula for Cosine; Integration Using the Pythagorean Identities
mf-skill-af0cba2e8c6a8dd2.Skill Description: Integration Using the Double-Angle Formulas — Use double-angle identities to lower powers such as sin² x and cos² x, or to simplify sin x cos x, before integrating.

mf-skill-3e6ca0981ed96934.Subject: Contextual Applications of Calculus
mf-skill-3e6ca0981ed96934.Prerequisite Names: Single-variable optimization; Implicit differentiation; Optimizing Distances
mf-skill-3e6ca0981ed96934.Skill Description: Optimizing Distances to Curves — Find the point on a curve nearest to or farthest from a given point by minimizing the squared distance.

mf-skill-8ba48f36315458ce.Subject: Differential Equations
mf-skill-8ba48f36315458ce.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Derivative as local rate; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Modeling Exponential Growth With Functions; Solving First-Order IVPs Using Separation of Variables
mf-skill-8ba48f36315458ce.Skill Description: Modeling With First-Order ODEs — Translate a verbal description of how a quantity changes into a first-order differential equation and interpret its solution.

mf-skill-7f66a6a979b2e708.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-7f66a6a979b2e708.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Intervals of Concavity; Relating Concavity to the Second Derivative
mf-skill-7f66a6a979b2e708.Skill Description: Points of Inflection — Locate points where a continuous graph changes concavity by finding where f'' is zero or undefined and confirming a sign change.

mf-skill-a1d77272241ec684.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-a1d77272241ec684.Prerequisite Names: Sequences and finite sums; Higher derivatives; Taylor Series; Maclaurin Series
mf-skill-a1d77272241ec684.Skill Description: Recognizing Standard Maclaurin Series — Know the common Maclaurin expansions by sight and adapt them by substitution instead of re-deriving each one.

mf-skill-e0528cc5dcf423c1.Subject: Differentiation
mf-skill-e0528cc5dcf423c1.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Continuity and discontinuities; Power, product, and quotient differentiation; Using the First Derivative Test to Classify Local Extrema; Relating Concavity to the Second Derivative
mf-skill-e0528cc5dcf423c1.Skill Description: The Second Derivative Test — Classify a critical point where f'(c) = 0 as a local maximum or minimum from the sign of f''(c).

mf-skill-05547b3b6f020b69.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-05547b3b6f020b69.Skill Name: Improper Integrals of the Second Kind
mf-skill-05547b3b6f020b69.Prerequisite Names: Limits of functions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Infinite Limits from Graphs; Improper Integrals Over the Real Line
mf-skill-05547b3b6f020b69.Skill Description: Improper Integrals of the Second Kind — Evaluate integrals whose integrand becomes unbounded at an endpoint or interior point, by replacing that point with a limit.

mf-skill-d46cedc0a2d46d7c.Subject: Integration Techniques
mf-skill-d46cedc0a2d46d7c.Skill Name: Integrating Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors
mf-skill-d46cedc0a2d46d7c.Prerequisite Codes: MTH-ALF-019, MTH-ALF-021, MTH-CAL-016, MTH-INT-002, MTH-INT-017, MTH-INT-025
mf-skill-d46cedc0a2d46d7c.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial division; Rational expressions and restrictions; Fundamental theorem of calculus; Expressing Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions; Integrating Rational Functions with Repeated Factors; Integrating Functions by Completing the Square
mf-skill-d46cedc0a2d46d7c.Skill Description: Integrating Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors — Integrate rational functions whose denominators contain quadratics with no real roots, using partial fractions with linear numerators and log or arctan results.

p-units.Subject: Measurement and modeling
p-units.Skill Description: Physical quantities and SI units — Express a physical quantity as a number together with a unit, using the SI system as the common standard.

px-accuracy.Subject: Measurement
px-accuracy.Skill Description: Distinguish accuracy from precision — Separate how close measurements are to the true value from how closely they agree with each other.

p-model.Subject: Measurement and modeling
p-model.Prerequisite Names: Describe an observable task and its limits; Physical quantities and SI units
p-model.Skill Description: Systems, assumptions, and models — Choose what to include in a system and state which effects a physical model deliberately ignores.

sss-phys-mass-weight.Subject: Force interpretation
sss-phys-mass-weight.Skill Name: Distinguish mass from gravitational weight and calculate weight using a stated g
sss-phys-mass-weight.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Multiplication and division
sss-phys-mass-weight.Skill Description: Distinguish mass from gravitational weight and calculate weight using a stated g — Mass is measured in kilograms; gravitational weight is a force measured in newtons with magnitude mg in the stated local gravitational field.

p-temperature.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-temperature.Skill Description: Temperature and thermal equilibrium — Distinguish temperature from thermal energy and identify thermal equilibrium.

p-charge.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-charge.Skill Description: Electric charge and conservation — Describe electric charge and its redistribution without treating charge as consumed by a circuit.

p-reflection.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-reflection.Skill Description: Reflection and ray diagrams — Trace light rays off mirrors and surfaces, measuring angles from the normal so the reflection angle equals the incidence angle.

px-randomerror.Subject: Measurement
px-randomerror.Skill Name: Distinguish random and systematic measurement errors
px-randomerror.Skill Description: Distinguish random and systematic measurement errors — Classify measurement errors as unpredictable scatter or as a consistent bias in one direction.

px-reflection-angle.Subject: Optics
px-reflection-angle.Skill Name: Apply the law of specular reflection
px-reflection-angle.Skill Description: Apply the law of specular reflection — Draw or calculate a reflected ray whose angle from the surface normal equals the angle of incidence.

px-kelvin.Subject: Thermal
px-kelvin.Skill Name: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin
px-kelvin.Prerequisite Names: Addition and subtraction; Temperature and thermal equilibrium
px-kelvin.Skill Description: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin — Convert Celsius readings to kelvin by adding 273.15, and recognize that temperature changes are the same size in both scales.

p-position.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-position.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Cartesian coordinates
p-position.Skill Description: Position and displacement — Describe an object's location and the signed change between two locations in a chosen frame.

hx-em-charge-density.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-charge-density.Skill Name: Linear, surface and volume charge density
hx-em-charge-density.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Electric charge and conservation; Surface area and volume
hx-em-charge-density.Skill Description: Linear, surface and volume charge density — Describe continuous charge with line, surface and volume densities and write the charge element dq for a rod, ring, disk or solid region.

px-distance.Subject: Kinematics
px-distance.Prerequisite Names: Absolute value and distance; Position and displacement
px-distance.Skill Description: Distinguish path distance from displacement — Tell apart the total path length traveled and the signed straight-line change in position.

p-precision.Subject: Measurement and modeling
p-precision.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Decimals and rounding
p-precision.Skill Description: Significant figures and resolution — Report measurements with digits that match the instrument's resolution, and keep resolution distinct from accuracy.

rob3:B-P01.Subject: Physics
rob3:B-P01.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Decimals and rounding
rob3:B-P01.Skill Description: Measure length, time and mass — Measure length, time and mass

hx-em-conductor-insulator.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-conductor-insulator.Skill Name: Conductors, insulators and free charge carriers
hx-em-conductor-insulator.Prerequisite Names: Electric charge and conservation; Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding
hx-em-conductor-insulator.Skill Description: Conductors, insulators and free charge carriers — Explain how mobile electrons in metals and bound electrons in insulators determine whether charge spreads through a material or stays where it was placed.

p-density.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-density.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Surface area and volume; Ratios and unit rates
p-density.Skill Description: Density and specific volume — Relate mass to occupied volume and distinguish density from total mass.

px-average-speed.Subject: Kinematics
px-average-speed.Skill Name: Compute average speed over a multistage trip
px-average-speed.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Distinguish path distance from displacement
px-average-speed.Skill Description: Compute average speed over a multistage trip — Divide the total distance traveled by the total elapsed time for a trip with several stages.

px-velocity-secant.Subject: Kinematics
px-velocity-secant.Skill Name: Find average velocity from two position readings
px-velocity-secant.Prerequisite Names: Position and displacement; Ratios and unit rates
px-velocity-secant.Skill Description: Find average velocity from two position readings — Compute signed displacement divided by elapsed time using position readings at two instants.

px-prefix.Subject: Measurement
px-prefix.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Integer powers; Ratios and unit rates
px-prefix.Skill Description: Convert SI prefixes in measurements — Convert measurements between SI prefixes such as kilo, milli, micro, and nano using powers of ten.

p-uncertainty.Subject: Measurement and modeling
p-uncertainty.Prerequisite Names: Absolute value and distance; Significant figures and resolution
p-uncertainty.Skill Description: Measurement uncertainty — Quantify the doubt in a measurement as a range and identify random and systematic contributions.

p-convert.Subject: Measurement and modeling
p-convert.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Ratios and unit rates
p-convert.Skill Description: Unit conversions — Change a quantity to different units by multiplying by conversion factors equal to one, including for squared and cubed units.

sss-phys-coordinate-convention.Subject: Motion interpretation

px-centripetal-force.Skill Description: Identify the net inward force in circular motion — Find which real forces combine to supply the net inward force m·v²/r that keeps an object moving in a circle.

px-thirdlaw-pairs.Subject: Forces
px-thirdlaw-pairs.Skill Name: Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair
px-thirdlaw-pairs.Prerequisite Names: Choose a system boundary for a free-body diagram; Interaction pairs and multiple bodies
px-thirdlaw-pairs.Skill Description: Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair — Match each force with its equal-and-opposite partner, which always acts on the other body in the interaction.

p-pressure.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-pressure.Prerequisite Names: Density and specific volume; Newton's second law in components
p-pressure.Skill Description: Pressure and hydrostatics — Relate normal force to area and model pressure changes with depth in a static fluid.

p-doppler.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-doppler.Prerequisite Names: Wave speed, frequency, and wavelength; Relative motion and reference frames
p-doppler.Skill Description: Doppler shifts — Relate relative source and observer motion to an observed frequency shift in an appropriate model.

p-electricfield.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-electricfield.Prerequisite Names: Electric charge and conservation; Newton's second law in components
p-electricfield.Skill Description: Electric force and field — Relate forces on charges to an electric field and use simple charge models.

p-magnetic.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-magnetic.Prerequisite Names: Electric charge and conservation; Cross products; Newton's second law in components
p-magnetic.Skill Description: Magnetic fields and forces — Relate moving charges and currents to magnetic forces using consistent directions.

p-lens.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-lens.Prerequisite Names: Similarity and scale drawings; Rational equations; Refraction and total internal reflection
p-lens.Skill Description: Thin-lens image formation — Relate object distance, image distance, and focal length with a stated sign convention.

hx-em-hall-effect.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-hall-effect.Prerequisite Names: Drift velocity of charge carriers; Determine magnetic force direction on a moving charge
hx-em-hall-effect.Skill Description: Hall effect physics — Derive the Hall voltage from the balance of magnetic and electric forces on drifting carriers, and use its sign and size to infer carrier type and density.

sss-phys-piecewise-handoff.Subject: Motion models
sss-phys-piecewise-handoff.Skill Name: Carry position and velocity between successive motion intervals
sss-phys-piecewise-handoff.Prerequisite Names: Calculate final position and velocity over a known constant-acceleration interval
sss-phys-piecewise-handoff.Skill Description: Carry position and velocity between successive motion intervals — Use the final position and velocity of one motion interval as the initial conditions of the next.

px-time-dilation.Subject: Modern physics
px-time-dilation.Skill Name: Calculate time dilation for inertial relative motion
px-time-dilation.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Ratios and unit rates; Roots and radicals; Relative motion and reference frames
px-time-dilation.Skill Description: Calculate time dilation for inertial relative motion — Use the Lorentz factor γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) to compare a proper time interval with the longer interval measured in another inertial frame.

px-uncertainty-principle.Subject: Modern physics
px-uncertainty-principle.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Sample variance and standard deviation; Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a particle
px-uncertainty-principle.Skill Description: Interpret the position-momentum uncertainty relation — Interpret Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 as a lower bound on the spreads of position and momentum in any quantum state.

hx-pmc-accelerating-frame.Subject: Non-inertial frames
hx-pmc-accelerating-frame.Skill Name: Inertial forces in a linearly accelerating frame
hx-pmc-accelerating-frame.Prerequisite Names: Infer constant velocity from zero net force in an inertial frame; Newton's second law in components; Relative motion and reference frames
hx-pmc-accelerating-frame.Skill Description: Inertial forces in a linearly accelerating frame — Analyze objects in an accelerating frame, such as a cup on a braking robot tray, by adding a fictitious force equal to minus mass times frame acceleration.

px-critical-angle.Subject: Optics
px-critical-angle.Skill Name: Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection
px-critical-angle.Prerequisite Names: Calculate a refraction angle with Snell's law
px-critical-angle.Skill Description: Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection — Find the incidence angle beyond which light in a higher-index medium is totally reflected at a boundary, using sin θc = n2/n1.

p-hooke.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-hooke.Prerequisite Names: Slope and intercept; Newton's second law in components
p-hooke.Skill Description: Ideal springs and restoring forces — Model a spring's restoring force as F = −kx, proportional to displacement, within the range where the spring behaves linearly.

p-torque.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-torque.Prerequisite Names: Right-triangle trigonometry; Cross products; Newton's second law in components
p-torque.Skill Description: Torque and lever arms — Describe and calculate the turning effect of a force about a point or axis using lever arms and τ = r × F.

p-coupled.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-coupled.Prerequisite Names: Two-variable linear systems; Newton's second law in components; Interaction pairs and multiple bodies
p-coupled.Skill Description: Coupled masses and pulleys — Use shared geometric constraints to solve interacting-body accelerations and forces.

p-incline.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-incline.Prerequisite Names: Right-triangle trigonometry; Newton's second law in components
p-incline.Skill Description: Inclined-plane dynamics — Resolve forces relative to a slope and solve for equilibrium or acceleration.

sss-phys-momentum-conditions.Subject: Translational mechanics
sss-phys-momentum-conditions.Prerequisite Names: Linear momentum; Choose a system boundary for a free-body diagram; Impulse and momentum change
sss-phys-momentum-conditions.Skill Description: Test when momentum conservation applies — Decide whether a system's total momentum, or one component of it, is conserved during an event by checking the net external impulse.

p-gravity.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-gravity.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Newton's second law in components
p-gravity.Skill Description: Universal gravitation — Model the inverse-square attraction between masses under the point-mass or spherical approximation.

p-weight.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-weight.Skill Description: Weight, normal force, and tension — Model common contact and support forces without assuming the normal force always equals weight.

p-work.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-work.Prerequisite Names: Dot products and projection; Newton's second law in components
p-work.Skill Description: Work by a constant force — Calculate energy transfer through the component of force along displacement.

px-wave-phase.Subject: Waves
px-wave-phase.Skill Name: Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave
px-wave-phase.Prerequisite Names: Radians and arc length; Convert among wave period, frequency, and wavelength; Periodic functions and phase
px-wave-phase.Skill Description: Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave — Convert a separation along a sinusoidal wave into a phase difference using Δφ = 2πΔx/λ.

hx-pth-doppler-echo.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-doppler-echo.Skill Name: Doppler shift of an echo from a moving target
hx-pth-doppler-echo.Prerequisite Names: Speed of sound and its temperature dependence; Doppler shifts
hx-pth-doppler-echo.Skill Description: Doppler shift of an echo from a moving target — Compute the two-way Doppler shift of sound reflected from a moving object and use it to infer the object's approach speed.

hx-pth-aberrations.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-aberrations.Prerequisite Names: Refraction and total internal reflection; Thin-lens image formation
hx-pth-aberrations.Skill Description: Chromatic and spherical aberrations — Explain physically how dispersion and spherical surfaces blur images, and why stopping down, achromatic doublets and aspheric elements reduce these errors.

hx-em-ring-field.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-ring-field.Skill Name: Electric field on the axis of a charged ring
hx-em-ring-field.Prerequisite Names: Linear, surface and volume charge density; Add electric fields from several point charges; Definite integrals and accumulation
hx-em-ring-field.Skill Description: Electric field on the axis of a charged ring — Derive the axial electric field of a uniformly charged ring by integration and locate where along the axis the field is strongest.

px-electric-flux.Subject: Electric fields
px-electric-flux.Skill Name: Calculate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field
px-electric-flux.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Dot products and projection; Electric force and field
px-electric-flux.Skill Description: Calculate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field — Evaluate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field as Φ = E · A = EA cos θ.

px-spring-energy.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-spring-energy.Skill Name: Calculate elastic energy stored in an ideal spring
px-spring-energy.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Ideal springs and restoring forces
px-spring-energy.Skill Description: Calculate elastic energy stored in an ideal spring — Use U = ½kx² to find the elastic potential energy of an ideal spring stretched or compressed by x.

px-power-force.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-power-force.Skill Name: Calculate instantaneous mechanical power from force and velocity
px-power-force.Prerequisite Names: Speed and average velocity; Dot products and projection; Work by a constant force
px-power-force.Skill Description: Calculate instantaneous mechanical power from force and velocity — Evaluate instantaneous power as the dot product of force and the velocity of its point of application.

px-work-sign.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-work-sign.Skill Name: Determine the sign of mechanical work
px-work-sign.Prerequisite Names: Angles and geometric relationships; Work by a constant force
px-work-sign.Skill Description: Determine the sign of mechanical work — Distinguish positive, negative, and zero work by the angle between force and displacement.

px-variable-work-graph.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-variable-work-graph.Skill Name: Find variable-force work from a force-position graph
px-variable-work-graph.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Interpreting physical graphs; Work by a constant force
px-variable-work-graph.Skill Description: Find variable-force work from a force-position graph — Sum signed geometric areas under a force-versus-position graph to find the work done by a varying force.

px-collision-inelastic.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-collision-inelastic.Skill Name: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly inelastic collision
px-collision-inelastic.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Linear momentum; Test when momentum conservation applies
px-collision-inelastic.Skill Description: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly inelastic collision — Find the common final velocity when two bodies stick together, using momentum conservation.

hx-pth-viscosity.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-viscosity.Prerequisite Names: Density and specific volume; Derivative as local rate; Normal and shear stress
hx-pth-viscosity.Skill Description: Dynamic and kinematic viscosity — Relate shear stress to velocity gradient through dynamic viscosity, convert to kinematic viscosity, and compare air, water and oils at different temperatures.

px-poiseuille.Subject: Fluids
px-poiseuille.Skill Name: Calculate pressure loss in ideal laminar pipe flow
px-poiseuille.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Convert area and mean flow speed to volume flow rate; Pressure and hydrostatics
px-poiseuille.Skill Description: Calculate pressure loss in ideal laminar pipe flow — Use Poiseuille's law to relate pressure drop and flow rate for steady laminar flow in a round pipe.

px-gauge-pressure.Subject: Fluids
px-gauge-pressure.Skill Name: Convert gauge pressure and absolute pressure
px-gauge-pressure.Prerequisite Names: Addition and subtraction; Pressure and hydrostatics
px-gauge-pressure.Skill Description: Convert gauge pressure and absolute pressure — Convert between gauge pressure, measured relative to the atmosphere, and absolute pressure, measured relative to vacuum.

px-manometer.Subject: Fluids
px-manometer.Skill Name: Infer pressure difference from a static liquid column
px-manometer.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Density and specific volume; Pressure and hydrostatics
px-manometer.Skill Description: Infer pressure difference from a static liquid column — Use the height difference of a liquid column in a manometer to calculate a pressure difference with ΔP = ρgh.

sss-phys-force-diagram-audit.Subject: Force equations
sss-phys-force-diagram-audit.Skill Name: Audit a free-body diagram for missing and double-counted interactions
sss-phys-force-diagram-audit.Prerequisite Names: Free-body diagrams; Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair
sss-phys-force-diagram-audit.Skill Description: Audit a free-body diagram for missing and double-counted interactions — Check a proposed diagram against the isolated body and its actual interactions.

sss-phys-internal-force-cancellation.Subject: Force equations
sss-phys-internal-force-cancellation.Skill Name: Identify which interaction forces cancel when two bodies form one system
sss-phys-internal-force-cancellation.Prerequisite Names: Choose a system boundary for a free-body diagram; Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair
sss-phys-internal-force-cancellation.Skill Description: Identify which interaction forces cancel when two bodies form one system — When two interacting bodies are included in one system, their mutual Newton third-law forces are internal and cancel in the vector sum for that combined system.

px-normal-elevator.Subject: Forces
px-normal-elevator.Skill Name: Calculate apparent weight in an accelerating elevator
px-normal-elevator.Prerequisite Names: Newton's second law in components; Weight, normal force, and tension
px-normal-elevator.Skill Description: Calculate apparent weight in an accelerating elevator — Find the scale reading, meaning the normal force, for a person in a vertically accelerating elevator.

px-terminal-speed.Subject: Forces
px-terminal-speed.Skill Name: Find terminal speed under a specified drag law
px-terminal-speed.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Roots and radicals; Newton's second law in components; Weight, normal force, and tension
px-terminal-speed.Skill Description: Find terminal speed under a specified drag law — Find the constant speed at which drag exactly balances gravity for a falling object under a given drag model.

p-buoyancy.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-buoyancy.Skill Description: Buoyancy — Relate buoyant force to the weight of displaced fluid.

p-pascal.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-pascal.Prerequisite Names: Direct and inverse proportion; Pressure and hydrostatics
p-pascal.Skill Description: Hydraulic force transmission — Use pressure transmission in an ideal confined fluid to relate piston forces and areas.

p-gas.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-gas.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Rearranging formulas; Pressure and hydrostatics
p-gas.Skill Description: Ideal-gas relationships — Relate pressure, volume, temperature, and amount under an ideal-gas approximation.

sss-phys-delay-phase.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
sss-phys-delay-phase.Skill Name: Convert between time delay and phase shift
sss-phys-delay-phase.Prerequisite Names: Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave
sss-phys-delay-phase.Skill Description: Convert between time delay and phase shift — Convert a time delay into a phase shift at a given frequency, and recognize that a fixed delay gives a phase shift that grows with frequency.

p-potentialelectric.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-potentialelectric.Prerequisite Names: Electric force and field; Work by a constant force
p-potentialelectric.Skill Description: Electric potential and voltage — Interpret potential difference as energy transfer per unit charge.

p-flux.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-flux.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Dot products and projection; Magnetic fields and forces
p-flux.Skill Description: Magnetic flux — Measure the component of magnetic field passing through an area.

px-wire-force.Subject: Magnetism
px-wire-force.Skill Name: Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire
px-wire-force.Prerequisite Names: Current and charge flow; Cross products; Magnetic fields and forces
px-wire-force.Skill Description: Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire — Use F = I L × B to find the force on a straight current-carrying wire in a uniform magnetic field.

px-charge-orbit.Subject: Magnetism
px-charge-orbit.Skill Name: Calculate the radius of a charged-particle orbit in a uniform field
px-charge-orbit.Prerequisite Names: Rearranging formulas; Magnetic fields and forces; Identify the net inward force in circular motion
px-charge-orbit.Skill Description: Calculate the radius of a charged-particle orbit in a uniform field — Find the circle radius of a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field using r = mv/(|q|B).

hx-em-biot-savart.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-biot-savart.Prerequisite Names: Current and charge flow; Cross products; Magnetic fields and forces
hx-em-biot-savart.Skill Description: Biot-Savart law — Write the magnetic field contribution of a current element using the Biot-Savart law and determine its direction with the cross product and right-hand rule.

px-calibrate.Subject: Measurement
px-calibrate.Prerequisite Names: Interpreting physical graphs; Regression and residual analysis
px-calibrate.Skill Description: Fit a straight-line measurement calibration — Fit a slope and offset relating an instrument's output to known reference values, then invert it to convert readings.

hx-pmc-moi-integral-setup.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-integral-setup.Skill Name: Moment of inertia as an integral
hx-pmc-moi-integral-setup.Prerequisite Names: Mass moment of inertia; Calculate rotational inertia for point masses; Definite integrals and accumulation
hx-pmc-moi-integral-setup.Skill Description: Moment of inertia as an integral — Set up the moment of inertia of a continuous body as the integral of squared distance times mass element, writing dm from linear, areal or volume density.

px-length-contraction.Subject: Modern physics
px-length-contraction.Skill Name: Calculate a moving object's longitudinal length
px-length-contraction.Prerequisite Names: Calculate time dilation for inertial relative motion
px-length-contraction.Skill Description: Calculate a moving object's longitudinal length — Find the length of a moving object along its direction of motion as L = L0/γ, with both endpoints located at the same instant.

hx-pmc-centrifugal-rotating-frame.Subject: Non-inertial frames
hx-pmc-centrifugal-rotating-frame.Skill Name: Centrifugal force in a rotating frame
hx-pmc-centrifugal-rotating-frame.Prerequisite Names: Inertial forces in a linearly accelerating frame; Identify the net inward force in circular motion
hx-pmc-centrifugal-rotating-frame.Skill Description: Centrifugal force in a rotating frame — Describe a body at rest in a rotating frame using centrifugal force and compare it with the centripetal description in the inertial frame.

px-lens-equation.Subject: Optics
px-lens-equation.Skill Name: Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation
px-lens-equation.Skill Description: Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation — Solve 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i for the image distance of a thin lens and decide whether the image is real or virtual.

hx-pmc-springs-series-parallel.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-springs-series-parallel.Skill Name: Equivalent stiffness of springs in series and parallel
hx-pmc-springs-series-parallel.Skill Description: Equivalent stiffness of springs in series and parallel — Combine linear and torsional springs in series and parallel into one equivalent stiffness and identify which arrangement a mechanism creates.

p-angularmomentum.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-angularmomentum.Prerequisite Names: Angular position, speed, and acceleration; Mass moment of inertia; Impulse and momentum change; Torque and lever arms
p-angularmomentum.Skill Description: Angular momentum conservation — Track angular momentum L = Iω, which stays constant when the net external torque is zero and otherwise changes at the rate of that torque.

p-equilibrium.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-equilibrium.Prerequisite Names: Two-variable linear systems; Torque and lever arms
p-equilibrium.Skill Description: Force and torque equilibrium — Require both net force and net torque to vanish for static equilibrium, and use those conditions to solve for unknown forces.

p-rotdynamics.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-rotdynamics.Skill Name: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis
p-rotdynamics.Prerequisite Names: Mass moment of inertia; Torque and lever arms
p-rotdynamics.Skill Description: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis — Relate net axial torque to angular acceleration, τ = Iα, for a rigid body with constant moment of inertia.

p-shm.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-shm.Prerequisite Names: Periodic functions and phase; Ideal springs and restoring forces
p-shm.Skill Description: Simple harmonic motion — Relate sinusoidal motion to a restoring force proportional to displacement, x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ).

p-orbit.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-orbit.Skill Description: Circular orbits — Balance the required inward acceleration with gravitational acceleration for a circular orbit.

p-potential.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-potential.Prerequisite Names: Ideal springs and restoring forces; Work by a constant force
p-potential.Skill Description: Gravitational and spring potential energy — Represent recoverable energy associated with height or ideal spring deformation.

p-kinetic.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-kinetic.Skill Description: Kinetic energy and work-energy balance — Relate net work to a change in translational kinetic energy.

p-friction.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-friction.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Weight, normal force, and tension
p-friction.Skill Description: Static and kinetic friction — Distinguish a variable static-friction force up to a limit from a simplified sliding-friction model.

px-interference-path.Subject: Waves
px-interference-path.Skill Name: Identify constructive and destructive two-wave path differences
px-interference-path.Prerequisite Names: Wave superposition and interference; Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave
px-interference-path.Skill Description: Identify constructive and destructive two-wave path differences — Decide whether two coherent waves reinforce or cancel at a point from their path difference in wavelengths.

hx-pth-wave-function.Subject: Waves
hx-pth-wave-function.Prerequisite Names: Functions of several variables; Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave
hx-pth-wave-function.Skill Description: Traveling sinusoidal wave functions — Write and evaluate a traveling wave as amplitude times sine of kx minus omega t, relating wave number and angular frequency to wavelength, period and speed.

hx-pth-f-number.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-f-number.Skill Name: f-number, aperture area and exposure stops
hx-pth-f-number.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation
hx-pth-f-number.Skill Description: f-number, aperture area and exposure stops — Relate f-number to aperture diameter and light gathering, showing each full stop halves image-plane irradiance and scales with f-number squared.

hx-pth-triangulation-geometry.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-triangulation-geometry.Skill Name: Laser and active triangulation range geometry
hx-pth-triangulation-geometry.Prerequisite Names: Similarity and scale drawings; Propagate uncertainty through products and quotients; Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation
hx-pth-triangulation-geometry.Skill Description: Laser and active triangulation range geometry — Derive range from the baseline, focal length and spot position in an active triangulation sensor, and show depth error grows with range squared.

hx-pth-distortion-physics.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-distortion-physics.Skill Name: Physical origin of barrel and pincushion distortion
hx-pth-distortion-physics.Prerequisite Names: Right-triangle trigonometry; Chromatic and spherical aberrations
hx-pth-distortion-physics.Skill Description: Physical origin of barrel and pincushion distortion — Explain how aperture stop position and wide-angle projection bend straight lines into barrel or pincushion shapes, and contrast rectilinear and fisheye mappings.

px-charge-potential.Subject: Electric fields
px-charge-potential.Skill Name: Calculate potential energy change of a test charge
px-charge-potential.Prerequisite Names: Multiplication and division; Electric charge and conservation; Electric potential and voltage
px-charge-potential.Skill Description: Calculate potential energy change of a test charge — Use ΔU = qΔV, keeping the sign of the charge, to find how a charge’s electric potential energy changes.

px-gauss.Subject: Electric fields
px-gauss.Skill Name: Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry
px-gauss.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Electric charge and conservation; Linear equations in one unknown; Calculate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field
px-gauss.Skill Description: Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry — Use a spherical Gaussian surface and Φ = Q_enc/ε₀ to find the field of spherically symmetric charge.

hx-em-point-potential.Subject: Electric potential
hx-em-point-potential.Skill Name: Potential of point charges by superposition
hx-em-point-potential.Prerequisite Names: Calculate the force between two point charges; Electric potential and voltage
hx-em-point-potential.Skill Description: Potential of point charges by superposition — Calculate the electric potential at a point from several point charges as a scalar sum, and compare its sign and falloff with the field.

px-collision-elastic.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-collision-elastic.Prerequisite Names: Two-variable linear systems; Linear momentum; Test when momentum conservation applies; Kinetic energy and work-energy balance
px-collision-elastic.Skill Description: Solve a one-dimensional elastic collision — Use momentum and kinetic-energy conservation together to find final velocities in a one-dimensional elastic collision.

hx-pth-darcy-weisbach.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-darcy-weisbach.Skill Name: Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop in tubes and ducts
hx-pth-darcy-weisbach.Prerequisite Names: Interpret Reynolds number for a stated flow geometry; Dynamic and kinematic viscosity; Calculate pressure loss in ideal laminar pipe flow
hx-pth-darcy-weisbach.Skill Description: Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop in tubes and ducts — Calculate friction pressure drop with Darcy-Weisbach, using hydraulic diameter for rectangular ducts and a laminar or turbulent friction factor from Reynolds number.

hx-pth-suction-force.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-suction-force.Skill Name: Holding force from a pressure difference
hx-pth-suction-force.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Convert gauge pressure and absolute pressure
hx-pth-suction-force.Skill Description: Holding force from a pressure difference — Compute the holding force of a suction cup or vacuum pad from absolute pressure difference and effective area, including the atmospheric ceiling on vacuum force.

sss-phys-one-axis-force-equation.Subject: Force equations
sss-phys-one-axis-force-equation.Skill Name: Translate a supplied collinear force diagram into a signed Newton equation
sss-phys-one-axis-force-equation.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Choose and consistently apply a one-dimensional coordinate convention; Audit a free-body diagram for missing and double-counted interactions
sss-phys-one-axis-force-equation.Skill Description: Translate a supplied collinear force diagram into a signed Newton equation — Choose a positive axis and translate a correct diagram of collinear forces into ΣF = ma for a constant-mass body in an inertial frame.

px-static-friction.Subject: Forces
px-static-friction.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Free-body diagrams; Static and kinetic friction
px-static-friction.Skill Description: Determine the required static-friction force — Solve for the static friction needed to prevent slipping and check it against the maximum μs N.

px-kinetic-friction.Subject: Forces
px-kinetic-friction.Skill Name: Set the direction and magnitude of sliding friction
px-kinetic-friction.Prerequisite Names: Free-body diagrams; Static and kinetic friction
px-kinetic-friction.Skill Description: Set the direction and magnitude of sliding friction — Apply kinetic friction with magnitude μk N, pointing opposite the relative sliding of the two surfaces.

hx-pmc-rolling-resistance.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-rolling-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Rolling without slipping; Force and torque equilibrium; Static and kinetic friction
hx-pmc-rolling-resistance.Skill Description: Rolling resistance of wheels — Model rolling resistance as a forward shift of the normal force or a coefficient times load, and compute the drive torque needed to overcome it.

p-induction.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-induction.Skill Description: Faraday and Lenz induction — Relate changing magnetic flux to induced voltage and its opposing tendency.

px-loop-torque.Subject: Magnetism
px-loop-torque.Skill Name: Calculate torque on a current loop in a magnetic field
px-loop-torque.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Torque and lever arms; Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire
px-loop-torque.Skill Description: Calculate torque on a current loop in a magnetic field — Find the twisting effect on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field using τ = N I A B sin θ.

hx-em-loop-axis-field.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-loop-axis-field.Skill Name: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular loop
hx-em-loop-axis-field.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; Biot-Savart law
hx-em-loop-axis-field.Skill Description: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular loop — Integrate the Biot-Savart law around a circular current loop to find the axial field, and evaluate it at the centre and far along the axis.

hx-pmc-moi-rod.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-rod.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of a slender rod
hx-pmc-moi-rod.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia as an integral
hx-pmc-moi-rod.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of a slender rod — Integrate to obtain the moment of inertia of a uniform slender rod about its center and about one end, and compare the two results.

hx-pmc-radius-of-gyration.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-radius-of-gyration.Prerequisite Names: Roots and radicals; Moment of inertia as an integral
hx-pmc-radius-of-gyration.Skill Description: Radius of gyration — Convert between moment of inertia and radius of gyration, and use tabulated radii of gyration to estimate inertia of irregular parts.

px-photon-energy.Subject: Modern physics
px-photon-energy.Skill Name: Convert photon wavelength into photon energy
px-photon-energy.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Electromagnetic spectrum; Kinetic energy and work-energy balance
px-photon-energy.Skill Description: Convert photon wavelength into photon energy — Convert a photon's vacuum wavelength into its energy using E = hc/λ, in joules or electronvolts.

px-probability-density.Subject: Modern physics
px-probability-density.Skill Name: Interpret a quantum position probability density
px-probability-density.Prerequisite Names: Complex-number arithmetic; Definite integrals and accumulation; Continuous probability densities
px-probability-density.Skill Description: Interpret a quantum position probability density — Find the probability of locating a particle in an interval by integrating |ψ(x)|² of a normalized wavefunction.

px-young-fringes.Subject: Optics
px-young-fringes.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Right-triangle trigonometry; Identify constructive and destructive two-wave path differences
px-young-fringes.Skill Description: Calculate double-slit fringe spacing — Estimate the spacing of bright double-slit interference fringes using Δy ≈ λL/d for a distant screen.

px-lens-magnification.Subject: Optics
px-lens-magnification.Skill Name: Calculate transverse magnification of a thin lens
px-lens-magnification.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation
px-lens-magnification.Skill Description: Calculate transverse magnification of a thin lens — Find a thin lens's magnification m = −d_i/d_o to get the image's relative size and whether it is upright or inverted.

hx-pmc-two-dof-equations.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-two-dof-equations.Skill Name: Equations of motion of a two-degree-of-freedom system
hx-pmc-two-dof-equations.Prerequisite Names: Matrix arithmetic; Coupled masses and pulleys; Equivalent stiffness of springs in series and parallel
hx-pmc-two-dof-equations.Skill Description: Equations of motion of a two-degree-of-freedom system — Write the coupled equations of two masses connected by springs in mass and stiffness matrix form, M x double-dot plus K x equals zero.

hx-pmc-angular-impulse.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-angular-impulse.Prerequisite Names: Calculate impulse from a force-time graph; Angular momentum conservation
hx-pmc-angular-impulse.Skill Description: Angular impulse and momentum change — Relate the time integral of torque to the change in angular momentum, and find spin-up time or final speed of a rotor under a given torque history.

px-spring-period.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
px-spring-period.Skill Name: Calculate the period of an ideal mass-spring oscillator
px-spring-period.Prerequisite Names: Roots and radicals; Ideal springs and restoring forces; Simple harmonic motion
px-spring-period.Skill Description: Calculate the period of an ideal mass-spring oscillator — Use T = 2π√(m/k) to find the oscillation period of an ideal undamped mass on a spring.

p-pendulum.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-pendulum.Prerequisite Names: Torque and lever arms; Simple harmonic motion
p-pendulum.Skill Description: Small-angle pendulum model — Approximate a pendulum as a harmonic oscillator when its angular excursion is small.

px-gas-absolute.Subject: Thermal
px-gas-absolute.Skill Name: Solve an ideal-gas state using absolute temperature and pressure
px-gas-absolute.Prerequisite Names: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin; Rearranging formulas; Ideal-gas relationships; Convert gauge pressure and absolute pressure
px-gas-absolute.Skill Description: Solve an ideal-gas state using absolute temperature and pressure — Apply PV = nRT with absolute pressure, kelvin temperature, and consistent units to find an unknown gas property.

sss-phys-energy-system.Subject: Translational mechanics
sss-phys-energy-system.Skill Name: Choose the system for an energy balance
sss-phys-energy-system.Prerequisite Names: Choose a system boundary for a free-body diagram; Gravitational and spring potential energy
sss-phys-energy-system.Skill Description: Choose the system for an energy balance — Decide which objects are inside the system before an energy balance, so each interaction is counted once, either as work or as stored potential energy.

hx-pth-depth-of-field.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-depth-of-field.Skill Name: Depth of field and circle of confusion
hx-pth-depth-of-field.Prerequisite Names: Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation; f-number, aperture area and exposure stops
hx-pth-depth-of-field.Skill Description: Depth of field and circle of confusion — Compute near and far limits of acceptable focus and the hyperfocal distance from focal length, f-number and an allowable circle of confusion.

hx-pth-diffraction-blur.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-diffraction-blur.Prerequisite Names: Estimate diffraction-limited angular resolution of a circular aperture; f-number, aperture area and exposure stops
hx-pth-diffraction-blur.Skill Description: Diffraction blur versus pixel size — Compute the Airy disk diameter from wavelength and f-number, compare it with pixel pitch, and find the aperture beyond which diffraction limits sharpness.

hx-pth-ifov-gsd.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-ifov-gsd.Skill Name: Instantaneous field of view and object-space pixel size
hx-pth-ifov-gsd.Prerequisite Names: Separate optical resolution and pixel sampling; Calculate transverse magnification of a thin lens
hx-pth-ifov-gsd.Skill Description: Instantaneous field of view and object-space pixel size — Compute the angle each pixel subtends from pixel pitch and focal length, and the millimeters per pixel at a working distance for manipulation tasks.

hx-pth-nir-silicon.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-nir-silicon.Skill Name: Near-infrared light and silicon sensor response
hx-pth-nir-silicon.Prerequisite Names: Electromagnetic spectrum; Convert photon wavelength into photon energy
hx-pth-nir-silicon.Skill Description: Near-infrared light and silicon sensor response — Explain why silicon sensors respond out to about 1000 nanometers, why color cameras use IR-cut filters, and trade-offs between 850 and 940 nanometer illumination.

hx-pth-shot-noise.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-shot-noise.Skill Name: Photon shot noise and signal-to-noise ratio
hx-pth-shot-noise.Prerequisite Names: Poisson event counts; f-number, aperture area and exposure stops; Convert photon wavelength into photon energy
hx-pth-shot-noise.Skill Description: Photon shot noise and signal-to-noise ratio — Estimate photons collected per pixel from exposure, f-number and quantum efficiency, model arrival as Poisson, and show SNR grows as the square root of photon count.

hx-em-conductor-equilibrium.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-conductor-equilibrium.Prerequisite Names: Conductors, insulators and free charge carriers; Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry
hx-em-conductor-equilibrium.Skill Description: Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium — Show with Gauss's law that a conductor in equilibrium has zero interior field, excess charge only on its surface, and a field normal to that surface.

hx-em-gauss-cylinder.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-gauss-cylinder.Prerequisite Names: Linear, surface and volume charge density; Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry
hx-em-gauss-cylinder.Skill Description: Gauss's law with cylindrical symmetry — Apply Gauss's law with a coaxial cylindrical surface to find the field of an infinite line charge or charged cylinder inside and outside.

hx-em-gauss-planar.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-gauss-planar.Prerequisite Names: Linear, surface and volume charge density; Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry
hx-em-gauss-planar.Skill Description: Gauss's law with planar symmetry — Use a pillbox Gaussian surface to find the field of an infinite charged sheet and of two oppositely charged parallel sheets.

hx-em-system-energy.Subject: Electric potential
hx-em-system-energy.Skill Name: Potential energy of a system of charges
hx-em-system-energy.Prerequisite Names: Potential of point charges by superposition; Calculate potential energy change of a test charge
hx-em-system-energy.Skill Description: Potential energy of a system of charges — Compute the total electrostatic potential energy of an assembly of point charges by summing pair energies, and relate it to the work needed to assemble them.

sss-phys-normal-balance.Subject: Force equations
sss-phys-normal-balance.Skill Name: Determine a normal force from a supplied perpendicular force balance
