sss-phys-normal-balance.Prerequisite Names: Distinguish mass from gravitational weight and calculate weight using a stated g; Identify the direction of a normal contact force; Translate a supplied collinear force diagram into a signed Newton equation
sss-phys-normal-balance.Skill Description: Determine a normal force from a supplied perpendicular force balance — Given a correct force diagram with components already resolved perpendicular to a support, use Newton’s second law in that direction to determine the normal reaction.

hx-pmc-friction-angle-cone.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-friction-angle-cone.Skill Name: Angle of friction and the friction cone
hx-pmc-friction-angle-cone.Prerequisite Names: Inverse trigonometry and quadrants; Determine the required static-friction force
hx-pmc-friction-angle-cone.Skill Description: Angle of friction and the friction cone — Express the static friction limit as an angle whose tangent is the coefficient, and test whether a total contact reaction lies inside the friction cone.

px-displacement-integral.Subject: Kinematics
px-displacement-integral.Skill Name: Integrate velocity to recover position change
px-displacement-integral.Prerequisite Names: Speed and average velocity; Definite integrals and accumulation; Antiderivatives
px-displacement-integral.Skill Description: Integrate velocity to recover position change — Use a definite integral of velocity over time to find displacement, and from it the position or distance traveled.

px-motional-emf.Subject: Magnetism
px-motional-emf.Skill Name: Calculate the emf across a rod moving through a magnetic field
px-motional-emf.Prerequisite Names: Multiplication and division; Magnetic fields and forces; Voltage references and ground
px-motional-emf.Skill Description: Calculate the emf across a rod moving through a magnetic field — Calculate the voltage produced across a conducting rod moving through a magnetic field with emf = B L v.

px-lenz-direction.Subject: Magnetism
px-lenz-direction.Skill Name: Determine the direction of an induced current
px-lenz-direction.Skill Description: Determine the direction of an induced current — Use Lenz's law to decide which way an induced current flows by opposing the change in magnetic flux.

hx-em-magnetic-dipole.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-magnetic-dipole.Skill Name: Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
hx-em-magnetic-dipole.Prerequisite Names: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular loop; Calculate torque on a current loop in a magnetic field
hx-em-magnetic-dipole.Skill Description: Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop — Calculate the magnetic moment N I A of a coil, assign its direction with the right-hand rule, and relate it to the far field of the loop.

hx-pmc-moi-ring-disk.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-ring-disk.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of a ring, disk and annulus
hx-pmc-moi-ring-disk.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a slender rod
hx-pmc-moi-ring-disk.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of a ring, disk and annulus — Derive the axial moment of inertia of a thin ring, a solid disk and an annular disk by integrating concentric rings, as for wheels and rotors.

px-infinite-well.Subject: Modern physics
px-infinite-well.Skill Name: Calculate energy levels in a one-dimensional infinite potential well
px-infinite-well.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Standing waves and modes; Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a particle; Interpret a quantum position probability density
px-infinite-well.Skill Description: Calculate energy levels in a one-dimensional infinite potential well — Compute the allowed energies E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) of a particle confined between two impenetrable walls a distance L apart.

px-photoelectric.Subject: Modern physics
px-photoelectric.Skill Name: Determine a photoelectric threshold and maximum electron energy
px-photoelectric.Prerequisite Names: Kinetic energy and work-energy balance; Convert photon wavelength into photon energy
px-photoelectric.Skill Description: Determine a photoelectric threshold and maximum electron energy — Use K_max = hf − φ to find the threshold frequency or wavelength and the kinetic energy of the fastest ejected electrons.

hx-pmc-normal-modes.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-normal-modes.Prerequisite Names: Determinants; Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Equations of motion of a two-degree-of-freedom system
hx-pmc-normal-modes.Skill Description: Natural frequencies and mode shapes — Find the natural frequencies and mode shapes of a two-degree-of-freedom system by solving det of K minus omega squared M equals zero.

hx-pmc-reaction-torque.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-reaction-torque.Skill Name: Reaction torque on the robot body
hx-pmc-reaction-torque.Prerequisite Names: Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair; Angular impulse and momentum change
hx-pmc-reaction-torque.Skill Description: Reaction torque on the robot body — Explain and calculate the equal and opposite torque a motor exerts on its mount when accelerating a load, as in reaction wheels and free-floating bases.

px-pendulum-period.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
px-pendulum-period.Prerequisite Names: Roots and radicals; Small-angle pendulum model
px-pendulum-period.Skill Description: Calculate the small-angle pendulum period — Use T = 2π√(L/g) to find a simple pendulum's period when its swings are small.

hx-pmc-frames-machines.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-frames-machines.Skill Name: Forces in multi-member frames and machines
hx-pmc-frames-machines.Prerequisite Names: Transfer a known joint force between separate member diagrams; Solve reactions of a stable pin-and-roller beam under point loads; Recognize the conditions for an ideal two-force member
hx-pmc-frames-machines.Skill Description: Forces in multi-member frames and machines — Disassemble a linkage, gripper or clamp into member free-body diagrams and solve pin forces and the mechanical advantage between input and output.

hx-pmc-virtual-work-statics.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-virtual-work-statics.Skill Name: Principle of virtual work for mechanism statics
hx-pmc-virtual-work-statics.Prerequisite Names: Derivative as local rate; Work by a constant force; Solve reactions of a stable pin-and-roller beam under point loads
hx-pmc-virtual-work-statics.Skill Description: Principle of virtual work for mechanism statics — Relate input torque to output force in a one-degree-of-freedom mechanism by setting total virtual work to zero for a compatible virtual displacement.

hx-pmc-distributed-load-resultant.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-distributed-load-resultant.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; Solve reactions of a stable pin-and-roller beam under point loads
hx-pmc-distributed-load-resultant.Skill Description: Resultant of a distributed load — Replace a distributed line load such as self-weight or pressure with an equivalent point force by integrating its intensity and locating its centroid.

hx-pth-air-tank-capacity.Subject: Thermodynamics essentials
hx-pth-air-tank-capacity.Skill Name: Air stored in a pneumatic reservoir
hx-pth-air-tank-capacity.Prerequisite Names: Solve an ideal-gas state using absolute temperature and pressure
hx-pth-air-tank-capacity.Skill Description: Air stored in a pneumatic reservoir — Use the ideal gas law with absolute pressures to compute the mass of stored air and the free-air volume a tank can deliver between two gauge pressures.

p-energy.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-energy.Prerequisite Names: Kinetic energy and work-energy balance; Gravitational and spring potential energy; Choose the system for an energy balance
p-energy.Skill Description: Mechanical energy accounting — Track energy transfers and losses across a chosen system boundary.

hx-pth-wave-equation.Subject: Waves
hx-pth-wave-equation.Prerequisite Names: Newton's second law in components; Traveling sinusoidal wave functions; Partial derivatives
hx-pth-wave-equation.Skill Description: The one-dimensional wave equation — Derive the wave equation for a taut string from Newton's second law, verify that traveling sinusoids solve it, and find speed as root of tension over linear density.

p-calcmotion.Subject: Advanced dynamic models
p-calcmotion.Prerequisite Names: Motion graphs and piecewise motion; Higher derivatives; Fundamental theorem of calculus
p-calcmotion.Skill Description: Motion through differentiation and integration — Relate position, velocity, and acceleration as continuous-time derivatives and integrals.

hx-em-capacitor-combinations.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-capacitor-combinations.Prerequisite Names: Adding unlike fractions; Capacitance and stored energy
hx-em-capacitor-combinations.Skill Description: Series and parallel capacitor combinations — Calculate equivalent capacitance, charge and voltage sharing for capacitors in series, parallel and simple mixed networks.

hx-pth-checkpoint-s6.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-pth-checkpoint-s6.Prerequisite Names: Air stored in a pneumatic reservoir
hx-pth-checkpoint-s6.Skill Description: Physics checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid) — Demonstrate the 1 end-of-branch physics skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 6 integration milestone.

hx-pth-motion-blur.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-motion-blur.Skill Name: Motion blur from exposure time and motion
hx-pth-motion-blur.Prerequisite Names: Angular position, speed, and acceleration; Instantaneous field of view and object-space pixel size
hx-pth-motion-blur.Skill Description: Motion blur from exposure time and motion — Compute blur length in pixels from object or head angular rate, exposure time and per-pixel angle, and set a maximum exposure for sharp images.

hx-pth-sensor-windows.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-sensor-windows.Prerequisite Names: Calculate a refraction angle with Snell's law; Near-infrared light and silicon sensor response
hx-pth-sensor-windows.Skill Description: Sensor windows and IR-transmissive covers — Estimate Fresnel reflection losses at a cover window, avoid internal reflections that blind depth sensors, and choose tinted plastics that pass near-infrared.

hx-em-resistivity.Subject: Current in materials
hx-em-resistivity.Skill Name: Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law
hx-em-resistivity.Prerequisite Names: Current density; Resistance and Ohm's law
hx-em-resistivity.Skill Description: Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law — State the microscopic Ohm's law J equals sigma E, convert between resistivity and conductivity, and compare copper, aluminium, steel and carbon values.

hx-em-faraday-cage.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-faraday-cage.Skill Name: Electrostatic shielding by a closed conductor
hx-em-faraday-cage.Skill Description: Electrostatic shielding by a closed conductor — Explain why a field-free cavity inside a closed conductor shields its contents from external static fields, and what happens when charge is placed inside the cavity.

hx-em-surface-field-conductor.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-surface-field-conductor.Skill Name: Field at a conductor surface and sharp points
hx-em-surface-field-conductor.Prerequisite Names: Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium; Gauss's law with planar symmetry
hx-em-surface-field-conductor.Skill Description: Field at a conductor surface and sharp points — Calculate the field just outside a charged conductor from its surface charge density and explain why charge and field concentrate at sharp edges and points.

px-parallel-capacitor.Subject: Electric fields
px-parallel-capacitor.Skill Name: Estimate the capacitance of parallel plates
px-parallel-capacitor.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Ratios and unit rates; Capacitance and stored energy
px-parallel-capacitor.Skill Description: Estimate the capacitance of parallel plates — Estimate parallel-plate capacitance with C = κε₀A/d when the gap is small compared with the plate size.

hx-em-faraday-quant.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-faraday-quant.Prerequisite Names: Derivative as local rate; Faraday and Lenz induction; Determine the direction of an induced current
hx-em-faraday-quant.Skill Description: Faraday's law calculations — Calculate induced emf from the rate of change of magnetic flux through an N-turn coil for changing field, area or orientation, with Lenz's law for sign.

hx-em-motional-loop.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-motional-loop.Skill Name: Sliding rod on rails: induced current and drag
hx-em-motional-loop.Prerequisite Names: Find terminal speed under a specified drag law; Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire; Calculate the emf across a rod moving through a magnetic field
hx-em-motional-loop.Skill Description: Sliding rod on rails: induced current and drag — Solve a conducting rod on rails in a magnetic field for induced current, retarding force, dissipated power and terminal speed under a constant applied force.

hx-em-field-from-potential.Subject: Electric potential
hx-em-field-from-potential.Skill Name: Electric field from the potential gradient
hx-em-field-from-potential.Prerequisite Names: Potential of point charges by superposition; Gradients and directional derivatives
hx-em-field-from-potential.Skill Description: Electric field from the potential gradient — Obtain the electric field as the negative gradient of a given potential function and interpret field direction as steepest potential decrease.

px-energy-loss.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-energy-loss.Prerequisite Names: Work by a constant force; Mechanical energy accounting
px-energy-loss.Skill Description: Account for dissipated mechanical energy — Include energy lost to friction or drag when kinetic plus potential energy is not conserved.

px-escape.Subject: Energy and momentum
px-escape.Skill Name: Calculate escape speed in a point-mass gravity model
px-escape.Prerequisite Names: Roots and radicals; Universal gravitation; Mechanical energy accounting
px-escape.Skill Description: Calculate escape speed in a point-mass gravity model — Find the minimum speed needed to coast away from a planet or star forever, using v = √(2GM/r).

hx-em-body-resistance.Subject: Electrical safety physics
hx-em-body-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Physiological effects of current through the body; Resistance and Ohm's law
hx-em-body-resistance.Skill Description: Body impedance and touch voltage — Estimate current through a person from touch voltage and body plus skin resistance, and explain why wet skin and broken skin raise hazard sharply.

sss-phys-contact-consistency.Subject: Force models
sss-phys-contact-consistency.Skill Name: Check whether a predicted normal reaction is compatible with nonadhesive contact
sss-phys-contact-consistency.Prerequisite Names: Linear inequalities and intervals; Determine a normal force from a supplied perpendicular force balance
sss-phys-contact-consistency.Skill Description: Check whether a predicted normal reaction is compatible with nonadhesive contact — An ordinary nonadhesive support can push on a body but cannot pull it toward the surface.

hx-pmc-wedge-screw-friction.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-wedge-screw-friction.Skill Name: Friction in wedges and power screws
hx-pmc-wedge-screw-friction.Prerequisite Names: Inclined-plane dynamics; Transfer a known joint force between separate member diagrams; Angle of friction and the friction cone
hx-pmc-wedge-screw-friction.Skill Description: Friction in wedges and power screws — Analyze a wedge with friction on several faces and treat a square-thread screw as a wrapped wedge to find raising, lowering and self-locking torques.

hx-pmc-pivot-journal-friction.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-pivot-journal-friction.Skill Name: Friction torque in pivots, collars and journals
hx-pmc-pivot-journal-friction.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; Torque and lever arms; Angle of friction and the friction cone
hx-pmc-pivot-journal-friction.Skill Description: Friction torque in pivots, collars and journals — Integrate friction over a flat collar or disk clutch and use the friction circle for a journal bearing to find the resisting torque in a joint.

p-bernoulli.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-bernoulli.Prerequisite Names: Fluid continuity; Pressure and hydrostatics; Mechanical energy accounting
p-bernoulli.Skill Description: Bernoulli energy relation — Relate pressure, speed, and elevation along a suitable ideal-flow streamline.

p-heat.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-heat.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Rearranging formulas; Mechanical energy accounting
p-heat.Skill Description: Heat capacity and phase-change energy — Calculate sensible or latent energy transfer using the appropriate material property.

sss-phys-flux-mechanisms.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
sss-phys-flux-mechanisms.Prerequisite Names: Faraday and Lenz induction; Calculate the emf across a rod moving through a magnetic field
sss-phys-flux-mechanisms.Skill Description: Compare flux change mechanisms — Identify whether an induced emf comes from a changing field, a changing area or a changing orientation, and estimate each contribution.

p-photon.Subject: Fields, waves, and light
p-photon.Skill Description: Photon energy and photoelectric response — Relate photon energy to frequency and distinguish quantum energy thresholds from intensity.

hx-pmc-generalized-coordinates.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-generalized-coordinates.Prerequisite Names: Count independent coordinates of an unconstrained serial joint chain; Partial derivatives; Mechanical energy accounting
hx-pmc-generalized-coordinates.Skill Description: Generalized coordinates and holonomic constraints — Count degrees of freedom of a constrained mechanical system, choose independent generalized coordinates and write holonomic constraint equations that eliminate dependent ones.

px-back-emf.Subject: Magnetism
px-back-emf.Skill Name: Explain speed-dependent back emf in a DC motor
px-back-emf.Prerequisite Names: Faraday and Lenz induction; Resistance and Ohm's law
px-back-emf.Skill Description: Explain speed-dependent back emf in a DC motor — Explain why a spinning DC motor generates a voltage opposing its supply, and how that limits current as speed rises.

hx-em-earth-field.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-earth-field.Prerequisite Names: Right-triangle trigonometry; Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
hx-em-earth-field.Skill Description: Earth's magnetic field — Describe Earth's field magnitude, declination and inclination, and resolve it into horizontal and vertical components at a given location for heading calculations.

hx-em-dipole-torque-energy.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-dipole-torque-energy.Skill Name: Torque and energy of a magnetic dipole
hx-em-dipole-torque-energy.Prerequisite Names: Dot products and projection; Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
hx-em-dipole-torque-energy.Skill Description: Torque and energy of a magnetic dipole — Calculate the torque m cross B and potential energy minus m dot B of a magnetic dipole, and predict stable and unstable alignment like a compass needle.

hx-pmc-perpendicular-axis.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-perpendicular-axis.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a ring, disk and annulus
hx-pmc-perpendicular-axis.Skill Description: Perpendicular-axis theorem for flat plates — Use the perpendicular-axis theorem to get the in-plane moments of inertia of a thin lamina, such as a disk about a diameter, from its polar moment.

hx-em-magnetization.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-magnetization.Prerequisite Names: Magnetic material response; Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
hx-em-magnetization.Skill Description: Magnetization of matter — Define magnetization as magnetic dipole moment per unit volume and explain how aligned atomic dipoles act like surface currents that add to an applied field.

px-rest-energy.Subject: Modern physics
px-rest-energy.Skill Description: Calculate mass-energy equivalence — Evaluate the rest energy E = mc² of a mass with consistent units, and relate changes in mass to changes in energy.

hx-pmc-physical-pendulum.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-physical-pendulum.Prerequisite Names: Parallel-axis theorem; Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Calculate the small-angle pendulum period
hx-pmc-physical-pendulum.Skill Description: Physical pendulum period — Calculate the small-oscillation period of a rigid body swinging about a pivot from its mass, center-of-mass distance and moment of inertia about the pivot.

hx-pmc-massive-pulley-system.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-massive-pulley-system.Skill Name: Hanging masses over a pulley with inertia
hx-pmc-massive-pulley-system.Prerequisite Names: Coupled masses and pulleys; Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Moment of inertia of a ring, disk and annulus
hx-pmc-massive-pulley-system.Skill Description: Hanging masses over a pulley with inertia — Solve accelerations and unequal rope tensions for masses connected over a pulley whose moment of inertia is not negligible.

p-rotenergy.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
p-rotenergy.Prerequisite Names: Mass moment of inertia; Mechanical energy accounting
p-rotenergy.Skill Description: Rotational kinetic energy and power — Track rotational kinetic energy ½Iω² and relate torque times angular speed to power.

hx-pth-copper-resistance-temp.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-copper-resistance-temp.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Percentages; Resistance and Ohm's law
hx-pth-copper-resistance-temp.Skill Description: Copper resistance rise with temperature — Use copper's temperature coefficient of about 0.39 percent per kelvin to predict winding resistance and copper loss at elevated temperature.

p-collision.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-collision.Prerequisite Names: Two-variable linear systems; Impulse and momentum change; Mechanical energy accounting
p-collision.Skill Description: Collision models — Combine momentum conservation with the appropriate energy or restitution assumptions.

p-power.Subject: Translational mechanics
p-power.Skill Description: Mechanical power and efficiency — Calculate energy transfer per time and compare useful output with input.

p-damping.Subject: Advanced dynamic models
p-damping.Prerequisite Names: Simple harmonic motion; Second-order linear equations
p-damping.Skill Description: Viscous damping and transient response — Model velocity-proportional resistance and distinguish underdamped, critical, and overdamped response.

p-variablework.Subject: Advanced dynamic models
p-variablework.Prerequisite Names: Work by a constant force; Line integrals
p-variablework.Skill Description: Work from a variable force — Find work as the integral of the force component along a path, W = ∫ F · dr, when force or direction varies.

hx-em-dielectric-constant.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-dielectric-constant.Prerequisite Names: Dielectric properties; Estimate the capacitance of parallel plates
hx-em-dielectric-constant.Skill Description: Dielectric constant and capacitance — Calculate how inserting a dielectric of relative permittivity changes capacitance, stored charge, field and energy at fixed voltage and at fixed charge.

hx-em-e-energy-density.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-e-energy-density.Skill Name: Energy density of the electric field
hx-em-e-energy-density.Prerequisite Names: Capacitance and stored energy; Estimate the capacitance of parallel plates
hx-em-e-energy-density.Skill Description: Energy density of the electric field — Show that a parallel-plate capacitor's stored energy equals one half epsilon zero E squared times its volume, and use field energy density in estimates.

hx-pmc-restitution.Subject: Collisions and impact
hx-pmc-restitution.Prerequisite Names: Solve a one-dimensional elastic collision; Collision models
hx-pmc-restitution.Skill Description: Coefficient of restitution — Define the coefficient of restitution from relative separation and approach speeds, solve partially elastic 1D impacts and measure it from bounce heights.

hx-em-temp-coefficient.Subject: Current in materials
hx-em-temp-coefficient.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Local linear approximation; Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law
hx-em-temp-coefficient.Skill Description: Temperature dependence of resistance — Apply the linear temperature coefficient of resistivity to predict how much a copper winding's resistance rises when it heats from room temperature to operating temperature.

hx-em-wire-resistance.Subject: Current in materials
hx-em-wire-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law
hx-em-wire-resistance.Skill Description: Wire resistance from geometry — Calculate a conductor's resistance from resistivity, length and cross-sectional area, and predict how resistance scales when wire gauge or length changes.

hx-em-torque-angle.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-torque-angle.Skill Name: Torque from interacting rotor and stator fields
hx-em-torque-angle.Prerequisite Names: Calculate torque on a current loop in a magnetic field; Torque and energy of a magnetic dipole
hx-em-torque-angle.Skill Description: Torque from interacting rotor and stator fields — Model machine torque as proportional to rotor and stator field strengths times the sine of the angle between them, and find the angle giving maximum torque per amp.

hx-em-line-charge-field.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-line-charge-field.Skill Name: Electric field of a finite line charge
hx-em-line-charge-field.Prerequisite Names: Linear, surface and volume charge density; Right-triangle trigonometry; Add electric fields from several point charges; Integration by substitution
hx-em-line-charge-field.Skill Description: Electric field of a finite line charge — Integrate Coulomb contributions along a uniformly charged rod to find the field at a point on its perpendicular bisector, using symmetry to cancel components.

hx-em-disk-field.Subject: Electrostatics
hx-em-disk-field.Skill Name: Electric field on the axis of a charged disk
hx-em-disk-field.Prerequisite Names: Limits of functions; Electric field on the axis of a charged ring; Integration by substitution
hx-em-disk-field.Skill Description: Electric field on the axis of a charged disk — Build a charged disk from concentric rings, integrate to find its axial field, and show the result approaches the infinite-sheet value close to the surface.

hx-em-rotating-coil-emf.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-rotating-coil-emf.Skill Name: Emf of a coil rotating in a uniform field
hx-em-rotating-coil-emf.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric and exponential derivatives; Faraday's law calculations
hx-em-rotating-coil-emf.Skill Description: Emf of a coil rotating in a uniform field — Derive the sinusoidal emf N B A omega sin omega t of a coil spinning in a uniform field and identify where in the rotation it peaks.

hx-em-flux-linkage.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-flux-linkage.Skill Description: Flux linkage — Define flux linkage as turns times flux, distinguish it from flux through one turn, and write induced voltage as its time derivative.

hx-em-induced-e-field.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-induced-e-field.Skill Description: Induced electric fields — Explain that a changing magnetic flux produces a circulating, non-conservative electric field, and calculate its magnitude around a symmetric changing flux region.

hx-em-equipotentials.Subject: Electric potential
hx-em-equipotentials.Prerequisite Names: Electric field line diagrams; Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium; Electric field from the potential gradient
hx-em-equipotentials.Skill Description: Equipotential surfaces — Sketch equipotential surfaces perpendicular to field lines, explain why a conductor is an equipotential, and why no work is done moving charge along one.

hx-em-potential-from-field.Subject: Electric potential
hx-em-potential-from-field.Skill Name: Potential difference from a line integral of the field
hx-em-potential-from-field.Prerequisite Names: Potential of point charges by superposition; Gauss's law with cylindrical symmetry; Line integrals
hx-em-potential-from-field.Skill Description: Potential difference from a line integral of the field — Integrate the electric field along a path to find potential differences for spheres, line charges and uniform fields, including the logarithmic potential of a line charge.

hx-em-current-path-hazard.Subject: Electrical safety physics
hx-em-current-path-hazard.Skill Name: Why shock hazard depends on current path
hx-em-current-path-hazard.Prerequisite Names: Voltage references and ground; Body impedance and touch voltage
hx-em-current-path-hazard.Skill Description: Why shock hazard depends on current path — Explain why hand-to-hand and hand-to-foot paths through the chest are most dangerous, why a single contact needs a return path, and how ground faults create one.

hx-pth-pressure-components.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-pressure-components.Skill Description: Static, dynamic and total pressure — Distinguish static, dynamic and total pressure, compute dynamic pressure from air speed, and read a pitot tube or fan static-pressure specification.

hx-pmc-tip-or-slip.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-tip-or-slip.Skill Name: Tipping versus slipping of a pushed body
hx-pmc-tip-or-slip.Prerequisite Names: Force and torque equilibrium; Determine the required static-friction force; Check whether a predicted normal reaction is compatible with nonadhesive contact
hx-pmc-tip-or-slip.Skill Description: Tipping versus slipping of a pushed body — Determine whether a block or robot pushed sideways will slide or tip first by comparing the friction limit with the moment balance about the edge.

sss-phys-bernoulli-assumptions.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
sss-phys-bernoulli-assumptions.Skill Name: Check assumptions before a Bernoulli calculation
sss-phys-bernoulli-assumptions.Skill Description: Check assumptions before a Bernoulli calculation — Decide whether a flow is steady, incompressible, effectively frictionless and free of pumps or turbines along the chosen streamline before using Bernoulli's equation.

p-firstlaw.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-firstlaw.Skill Description: First law of thermodynamics — Track internal-energy changes using a clearly stated heat and work sign convention.

hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-eom.Subject: Inverted pendulum and balance
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-eom.Skill Name: Equation of motion of an inverted pendulum
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-eom.Prerequisite Names: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Physical pendulum period
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-eom.Skill Description: Equation of motion of an inverted pendulum — Derive the nonlinear equation of a rigid inverted pendulum pivoted at its base with an applied pivot torque and identify its upright equilibrium.

hx-pmc-kinetic-energy-generalized.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-kinetic-energy-generalized.Prerequisite Names: Generalized coordinates and holonomic constraints; Multivariable chain rule; Rotational kinetic energy and power
hx-pmc-kinetic-energy-generalized.Skill Description: Kinetic energy in generalized coordinates — Express the kinetic energy of a system of particles and rigid bodies in terms of generalized coordinates and their rates using the chain rule.

hx-pth-radiometry-photometry.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-radiometry-photometry.Prerequisite Names: Electromagnetic spectrum; Mechanical power and efficiency
hx-pth-radiometry-photometry.Skill Description: Radiometric and photometric units — Distinguish watts from lumens using the eye's luminous efficiency curve, and compute luminous flux from radiant power at a given wavelength.

hx-em-straight-wire-field.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-straight-wire-field.Skill Name: Magnetic field of a long straight wire
hx-em-straight-wire-field.Skill Description: Magnetic field of a long straight wire — Derive and apply B equals mu zero I over two pi r for a long straight wire, including the circular field direction from the right-hand grip rule.

hx-pmc-moi-box-plate.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-box-plate.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of a rectangular plate and block
hx-pmc-moi-box-plate.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a slender rod; Perpendicular-axis theorem for flat plates
hx-pmc-moi-box-plate.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of a rectangular plate and block — Compute the centroidal moments of inertia of a rectangular plate and a rectangular block about each axis, the usual approximation for robot links and batteries.

hx-pmc-moi-cylinder.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-cylinder.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of solid and hollow cylinders
hx-pmc-moi-cylinder.Prerequisite Names: Parallel-axis theorem; Perpendicular-axis theorem for flat plates
hx-pmc-moi-cylinder.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of solid and hollow cylinders — Compute the moment of inertia of solid and thick-walled cylinders about their axis and about a transverse centroidal axis, as for motors and tubular links.

px-binding-energy.Subject: Modern physics
px-binding-energy.Skill Name: Calculate nuclear binding energy from a mass defect
px-binding-energy.Prerequisite Names: Addition and subtraction; Atoms, elements, and electron structure; Calculate mass-energy equivalence
px-binding-energy.Skill Description: Calculate nuclear binding energy from a mass defect — Convert the mass defect between separate nucleons and a bound nucleus into binding energy using E = Δm c².

hx-pmc-shm-solution.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-shm-solution.Skill Name: Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation
hx-pmc-shm-solution.Prerequisite Names: Simple harmonic motion; Second-order linear equations
hx-pmc-shm-solution.Skill Description: Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation — Solve x double-dot plus omega squared x equals zero and find amplitude and phase from initial position and velocity.

hx-pmc-rolling-energy.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-rolling-energy.Prerequisite Names: Apply the no-slip rolling constraint; Rotational kinetic energy and power
hx-pmc-rolling-energy.Skill Description: Energy of rolling bodies — Combine translational and rotational kinetic energy for a rolling wheel or cylinder and use energy conservation to find speed after descending a ramp.

hx-pmc-reflected-inertia-energy.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-reflected-inertia-energy.Skill Name: Equivalent inertia of a drive by energy equivalence
hx-pmc-reflected-inertia-energy.Prerequisite Names: Apply the no-slip rolling constraint; Refer inertia through a gearbox; Rotational kinetic energy and power
hx-pmc-reflected-inertia-energy.Skill Description: Equivalent inertia of a drive by energy equivalence — Derive the equivalent inertia at the motor shaft of a multi-stage gear train, belt or screw driving rotating and translating masses by equating kinetic energies.

hx-pth-composite-heat-capacity.Subject: Thermodynamics essentials
hx-pth-composite-heat-capacity.Skill Name: Heat capacity of a multi-material part
hx-pth-composite-heat-capacity.Prerequisite Names: Addition and subtraction; Heat capacity and phase-change energy
hx-pth-composite-heat-capacity.Skill Description: Heat capacity of a multi-material part — Sum mass times specific heat for copper, steel, aluminum and plastic parts to find the lumped heat capacity of a motor or electronics module.

hx-pth-winding-temp-by-resistance.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-winding-temp-by-resistance.Skill Name: Infer winding temperature from resistance change
hx-pth-winding-temp-by-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Multimeter measurement choices; Copper resistance rise with temperature
hx-pth-winding-temp-by-resistance.Skill Description: Infer winding temperature from resistance change — Measure cold and hot winding resistance and invert the copper temperature coefficient to estimate average winding temperature without an embedded sensor.

px-latent-heat.Subject: Thermal
px-latent-heat.Skill Name: Calculate energy required for a phase change
px-latent-heat.Prerequisite Names: Multiplication and division; Heat capacity and phase-change energy
px-latent-heat.Skill Description: Calculate energy required for a phase change — Use Q = mL to find the heat needed to melt, freeze, boil, or condense a mass at its transition temperature.

px-radiation.Subject: Thermal
px-radiation.Skill Name: Calculate net thermal radiation to a large surrounding enclosure
px-radiation.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin; Integer powers; Mechanical power and efficiency
px-radiation.Skill Description: Calculate net thermal radiation to a large surrounding enclosure — Find the net radiant heat flow between a surface and much larger surroundings using εσA(Ts⁴ − Tsur⁴).

px-conduction.Subject: Thermal
px-conduction.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Ratios and unit rates; Mechanical power and efficiency
px-conduction.Skill Description: Calculate steady one-dimensional heat conduction — Find the steady heat flow through a uniform slab using q = kAΔT/L.

px-calorimetry.Subject: Thermal
px-calorimetry.Skill Name: Solve a two-body thermal mixing problem
px-calorimetry.Prerequisite Names: Linear equations in one unknown; Heat capacity and phase-change energy
px-calorimetry.Skill Description: Solve a two-body thermal mixing problem — Find the final temperature when two bodies exchange heat in an insulated system with no phase change.

hx-pth-wave-intensity.Subject: Waves
hx-pth-wave-intensity.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Traveling sinusoidal wave functions; Mechanical power and efficiency
hx-pth-wave-intensity.Skill Description: Wave power and intensity — Define intensity as power per unit area, show that it scales with amplitude squared, and compute intensity from source power over a given area.

hx-pth-loudspeaker-principles.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-loudspeaker-principles.Prerequisite Names: Wave superposition and interference; Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire; Wave power and intensity
hx-pth-loudspeaker-principles.Skill Description: Moving-coil loudspeaker principles — Explain how voice-coil force on a cone radiates sound, why small drivers lose bass, and why front and rear waves cancel without a baffle.

p-resonance.Subject: Advanced dynamic models
p-resonance.Skill Description: Forced vibration and resonance — Analyze how forcing frequency interacts with natural dynamics and damping to produce large vibration near resonance.

p-lagrangian.Subject: Advanced dynamic models
p-lagrangian.Prerequisite Names: Differential equations and initial values; Partial derivatives; Mechanical energy accounting; Generalized coordinates and holonomic constraints; Kinetic energy in generalized coordinates
p-lagrangian.Skill Description: Lagrangian mechanics — Form equations of motion from kinetic and potential energy using generalized coordinates.

hx-em-cylindrical-capacitor.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-cylindrical-capacitor.Prerequisite Names: Capacitance and stored energy; Potential difference from a line integral of the field
hx-em-cylindrical-capacitor.Skill Description: Capacitance of coaxial cylinders — Derive the capacitance per unit length of a coaxial cable from the field between cylinders, and estimate the capacitance of a real cable run.

hx-em-dielectric-polarization.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-dielectric-polarization.Prerequisite Names: Conductors, insulators and free charge carriers; Dielectric constant and capacitance
hx-em-dielectric-polarization.Skill Description: Dielectric polarization and bound charge — Explain how induced and permanent molecular dipoles polarize a dielectric, creating bound surface charge that reduces the internal field and attracts neutral objects.

hx-em-dielectric-breakdown.Subject: Capacitance and dielectrics
hx-em-dielectric-breakdown.Skill Name: Dielectric strength, breakdown, clearance and creepage
hx-em-dielectric-breakdown.Prerequisite Names: Field at a conductor surface and sharp points; Dielectric constant and capacitance
hx-em-dielectric-breakdown.Skill Description: Dielectric strength, breakdown, clearance and creepage — Use dielectric strength to find the maximum voltage across a gap or insulator, and explain how air breakdown sets PCB clearance and surface contamination sets creepage.

hx-pth-air-heat-pickup.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-air-heat-pickup.Skill Name: Air temperature rise from absorbed heat
hx-pth-air-heat-pickup.Prerequisite Names: Convert volumetric flow rate to mass flow rate; Heat capacity and phase-change energy; First law of thermodynamics
hx-pth-air-heat-pickup.Skill Description: Air temperature rise from absorbed heat — Compute the outlet air temperature rise when a mass flow of air absorbs a known heat load, using heat equals mass flow times specific heat times temperature rise.

hx-pth-newton-cooling.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-newton-cooling.Skill Name: Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance
hx-pth-newton-cooling.Prerequisite Names: Calculate steady one-dimensional heat conduction; Convection and radiation concepts
hx-pth-newton-cooling.Skill Description: Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance — Apply heat flow equals h times area times temperature difference, convert it to a convection resistance, and recall typical h values for still air, fans and liquids.

hx-pmc-impact-force-contact-stiffness.Subject: Collisions and impact
hx-pmc-impact-force-contact-stiffness.Skill Name: Peak impact force from contact stiffness
hx-pmc-impact-force-contact-stiffness.Prerequisite Names: Impulse and momentum change; Calculate elastic energy stored in an ideal spring; Coefficient of restitution
hx-pmc-impact-force-contact-stiffness.Skill Description: Peak impact force from contact stiffness — Estimate peak contact force and duration of an impact by modeling the contact as a spring, giving force equal to speed times the square root of stiffness times mass.

hx-em-joule-microscopic.Subject: Current in materials
hx-em-joule-microscopic.Skill Name: Joule heating as microscopic power density
hx-em-joule-microscopic.Prerequisite Names: Dot products and projection; Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law; Electrical power and dissipation
hx-em-joule-microscopic.Skill Description: Joule heating as microscopic power density — Express resistive heating as power per volume J dot E, integrate it over a conductor, and locate hot spots where current crowds into narrow sections.

hx-em-eddy-currents.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-eddy-currents.Prerequisite Names: Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law; Induced electric fields
hx-em-eddy-currents.Skill Description: Eddy currents — Explain how changing flux drives circulating eddy currents in bulk conductors and how their loss scales with conductivity, frequency, field and conductor thickness.

hx-pth-minor-losses.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-minor-losses.Skill Name: Minor losses at bends, grilles and filters
hx-pth-minor-losses.Prerequisite Names: Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop in tubes and ducts; Static, dynamic and total pressure
hx-pth-minor-losses.Skill Description: Minor losses at bends, grilles and filters — Add loss coefficients for bends, sudden expansions, vent grilles and dust filters, each multiplying dynamic pressure, to total an air path's pressure drop.

hx-pth-quadratic-drag.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-quadratic-drag.Skill Name: Quadratic drag force and drag coefficient
hx-pth-quadratic-drag.Prerequisite Names: Newton's second law in components; Static, dynamic and total pressure
hx-pth-quadratic-drag.Skill Description: Quadratic drag force and drag coefficient — Calculate aerodynamic drag from dynamic pressure, frontal area and drag coefficient, and show it is negligible for a walking-speed robot but matters for fans and propellers.

p-entropy.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-entropy.Skill Description: Entropy and the second law — Describe the direction and limitations of energy conversion and entropy generation.

p-cycle.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
p-cycle.Prerequisite Names: Ideal-gas relationships; First law of thermodynamics
p-cycle.Skill Description: Thermodynamic cycles — Track a system through a cycle and interpret work on a pressure-volume diagram.

sss-phys-thermal-sign.Subject: Fluids and thermal physics
sss-phys-thermal-sign.Skill Name: Track sign conventions in a thermal energy balance
sss-phys-thermal-sign.Skill Description: Track sign conventions in a thermal energy balance — Carry one stated heat and work sign convention through a multi-step thermal balance, and convert results between the two common conventions.

hx-pth-slab-resistance.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-slab-resistance.Skill Name: Conduction thermal resistance of a slab
hx-pth-slab-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Calculate steady one-dimensional heat conduction; Thermal conductivity and conduction
hx-pth-slab-resistance.Skill Description: Conduction thermal resistance of a slab — Express steady conduction through a wall, pad or bracket as a thermal resistance equal to thickness over conductivity times area, in kelvin per watt.

hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-linear.Subject: Inverted pendulum and balance
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-linear.Skill Name: Linearize the inverted pendulum about upright
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-linear.Prerequisite Names: Local linear approximation; Phase portraits and equilibria; Equation of motion of an inverted pendulum
hx-pmc-inverted-pendulum-linear.Skill Description: Linearize the inverted pendulum about upright — Linearize the inverted pendulum for small tilt, find its real unstable root square root of g over l, and compute the time for a tilt to grow.

hx-pth-led-emission.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-led-emission.Skill Name: How LEDs emit light: bandgap and wavelength
hx-pth-led-emission.Prerequisite Names: Convert photon wavelength into photon energy; Carriers, doping, and junctions
hx-pth-led-emission.Skill Description: How LEDs emit light: bandgap and wavelength — Relate an LED's semiconductor bandgap to emission wavelength and forward voltage, and explain how white LEDs combine a blue die with phosphor.

hx-em-ampere-law.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-ampere-law.Prerequisite Names: Line integrals; Magnetic field of a long straight wire
hx-em-ampere-law.Skill Description: Ampere's law with symmetric currents — Apply Ampere's circuital law with an Amperian loop to find the field inside and outside a thick wire and recognise when symmetry makes it usable.

hx-em-parallel-wire-force.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-parallel-wire-force.Prerequisite Names: Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire; Magnetic field of a long straight wire
hx-em-parallel-wire-force.Skill Description: Force between parallel currents — Calculate the force per unit length between two parallel current-carrying conductors and determine whether they attract or repel from current directions.

hx-em-wire-superposition.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-wire-superposition.Prerequisite Names: Vector components and arithmetic; Magnetic field of a long straight wire
hx-em-wire-superposition.Skill Description: Superposing fields of several currents — Add the vector fields of multiple parallel wires to find net fields, and show why closely spaced go and return conductors largely cancel at a distance.

hx-em-gauss-magnetism.Subject: Maxwell's equations
hx-em-gauss-magnetism.Prerequisite Names: Magnetic flux; Surface integrals and flux
hx-em-gauss-magnetism.Skill Description: Gauss's law for magnetism — State that net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, explain the absence of magnetic monopoles, and use closed flux loops in magnetic reasoning.

hx-pmc-shm-energy.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-shm-energy.Prerequisite Names: Calculate elastic energy stored in an ideal spring; Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation
hx-pmc-shm-energy.Skill Description: Energy in simple harmonic motion — Track the exchange of kinetic and potential energy in an oscillator and find maximum speed and acceleration from amplitude and natural frequency.

hx-pmc-static-deflection-frequency.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-static-deflection-frequency.Prerequisite Names: Calculate the period of an ideal mass-spring oscillator; Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation
hx-pmc-static-deflection-frequency.Skill Description: Natural frequency from static deflection — Show that gravity shifts but does not change a vertical oscillator, and estimate natural frequency directly from static deflection under self-weight.

hx-pmc-torsional-oscillator.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-torsional-oscillator.Prerequisite Names: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Torsion of circular shafts; Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation
hx-pmc-torsional-oscillator.Skill Description: Torsional spring and inertia oscillator — Find the natural frequency of a rotor on a torsionally flexible shaft from torsional stiffness and moment of inertia.

hx-pmc-geared-drive-equation.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-geared-drive-equation.Skill Name: Equation of motion of a geared drive
hx-pmc-geared-drive-equation.Prerequisite Names: Calculate transmitted torque and losses; Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Equivalent inertia of a drive by energy equivalence
hx-pmc-geared-drive-equation.Skill Description: Equation of motion of a geared drive — Write the single-axis equation of motion of a motor driving a load through a gear ratio, referring load torque, friction and efficiency to the motor shaft.

hx-pmc-variable-torque-work.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-variable-torque-work.Skill Name: Work done by a variable torque
hx-pmc-variable-torque-work.Prerequisite Names: Rotational kinetic energy and power; Work from a variable force
hx-pmc-variable-torque-work.Skill Description: Work done by a variable torque — Compute rotational work as the integral of torque over angle, including spring and gravity torques, and relate it to the change in rotational kinetic energy.

px-damping-regimes.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
px-damping-regimes.Skill Name: Classify underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion
px-damping-regimes.Prerequisite Names: Second-order linear equations; Viscous damping and transient response
px-damping-regimes.Skill Description: Classify underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion — Classify a damped linear oscillator as underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped by comparing b² with 4mk.

hx-pth-losses-as-heat.Subject: Thermodynamics essentials
hx-pth-losses-as-heat.Prerequisite Names: Mechanical power and efficiency; Electrical power and dissipation; First law of thermodynamics
hx-pth-losses-as-heat.Skill Description: Efficiency losses appear as heat — Compute dissipated heat from input power and efficiency for motors, regulators and gearboxes, recognizing that every watt not delivered as useful work ends up warming the robot.

px-pv-work.Subject: Thermal
px-pv-work.Skill Name: Calculate boundary work from a pressure-volume diagram
px-pv-work.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Interpreting physical graphs; First law of thermodynamics
px-pv-work.Skill Description: Calculate boundary work from a pressure-volume diagram — Find the work done by a gas as the signed area under its path on a pressure-volume diagram.

hx-pth-emissivity.Subject: Thermal radiation
hx-pth-emissivity.Prerequisite Names: Calculate net thermal radiation to a large surrounding enclosure
hx-pth-emissivity.Skill Description: Emissivity of real surfaces — Compare emissivities of bare aluminum, anodized parts, paint and plastics, and explain why surface finish matters more than color for infrared radiation.

hx-pth-impedance-reflection.Subject: Waves
hx-pth-impedance-reflection.Skill Name: Reflection and transmission at an impedance boundary
hx-pth-impedance-reflection.Prerequisite Names: Speed of sound and its temperature dependence; Wave superposition and interference; Wave power and intensity
hx-pth-impedance-reflection.Skill Description: Reflection and transmission at an impedance boundary — Calculate reflected and transmitted fractions of a wave at a boundary between media of different characteristic impedance, such as air to solid or air to water.

hx-pth-speaker-enclosure.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-speaker-enclosure.Prerequisite Names: Standing waves in open and closed tubes; Moving-coil loudspeaker principles
hx-pth-speaker-enclosure.Skill Description: Loudspeaker enclosures and Helmholtz ports — Explain sealed and ported speaker enclosures, compute a Helmholtz port resonance, and judge how a head shell affects voice quality and echo.

hx-pth-reverberation-time.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-reverberation-time.Prerequisite Names: Surface area and volume; Calculate distance from round-trip echo time; Reflection and transmission at an impedance boundary
hx-pth-reverberation-time.Skill Description: Reverberation time with Sabine's formula — Total surface absorption from frequency-dependent absorption coefficients, estimate reverberation time with Sabine's formula, and explain how long reverberation smears speech.

hx-pth-spl.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-spl.Skill Name: Sound pressure level from RMS pressure
hx-pth-spl.Prerequisite Names: Convert an intensity ratio to a sound-level difference; AC amplitude, phase, and RMS
hx-pth-spl.Skill Description: Sound pressure level from RMS pressure — Convert RMS acoustic pressure to sound pressure level in decibels relative to 20 micropascals, using 20 log for pressure versus 10 log for intensity.

hx-pth-vibration-isolation.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-vibration-isolation.Prerequisite Names: Forced vibration and resonance; Classify underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion
hx-pth-vibration-isolation.Skill Description: Vibration isolation and structure-borne noise — Compute transmissibility of a spring-damper mount versus frequency ratio and choose isolators that keep motor and fan vibration from radiating through the shell.

hx-pth-checkpoint-s4.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-pth-checkpoint-s4.Prerequisite Names: Doppler shift of an echo from a moving target; Quadratic drag force and drag coefficient
hx-pth-checkpoint-s4.Skill Description: Physics checkpoint: stage 4 (wheeled base) — Demonstrate the 2 end-of-branch physics skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 4 integration milestone.

hx-pth-forced-convection.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-forced-convection.Skill Name: Forced convection and the Nusselt number
hx-pth-forced-convection.Prerequisite Names: Fractional exponents; Interpret Reynolds number for a stated flow geometry; Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance
hx-pth-forced-convection.Skill Description: Forced convection and the Nusselt number — Use a Nusselt-number correlation in Reynolds number to estimate the heat transfer coefficient for air blown over a plate or through a channel.

hx-pth-fin-basics.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-fin-basics.Skill Name: How heatsink fins add cooling area
hx-pth-fin-basics.Prerequisite Names: Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance
hx-pth-fin-basics.Skill Description: How heatsink fins add cooling area — Explain how fins raise convective area, why fins spaced too closely choke airflow, and why fins in still air need wider spacing than fins under a fan.

hx-pth-natural-convection.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-natural-convection.Skill Name: Natural convection from a heated plate
hx-pth-natural-convection.Prerequisite Names: Fractional exponents; Buoyancy; Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance
hx-pth-natural-convection.Skill Description: Natural convection from a heated plate — Estimate a natural-convection coefficient for a vertical heated surface from a simplified correlation, and explain how orientation and buoyant plumes affect cooling.

hx-pth-vent-airflow-sizing.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-vent-airflow-sizing.Skill Name: Size ventilation airflow for an enclosure
hx-pth-vent-airflow-sizing.Prerequisite Names: Unit conversions; Convert area and mean flow speed to volume flow rate; Air temperature rise from absorbed heat
hx-pth-vent-airflow-sizing.Skill Description: Size ventilation airflow for an enclosure — Find the volume flow in liters per second or CFM needed to hold enclosure air within an allowed rise, and place inlets and outlets so air sweeps hot parts.

hx-em-ac-generator.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-ac-generator.Prerequisite Names: Emf of a coil rotating in a uniform field; AC amplitude, phase, and RMS
hx-em-ac-generator.Skill Description: AC generator output — Calculate peak and RMS emf, frequency and delivered power for a simple AC generator driving a resistive load, and relate shaft torque to electrical load.

hx-em-eddy-braking.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-eddy-braking.Prerequisite Names: Sliding rod on rails: induced current and drag; Eddy currents
hx-em-eddy-braking.Skill Description: Eddy-current braking and damping — Show that eddy-current braking force is proportional to speed, model it as viscous damping, and predict the terminal speed of a magnet falling through a copper tube.

hx-em-stored-charge-hazard.Subject: Electrical safety physics
hx-em-stored-charge-hazard.Prerequisite Names: Body impedance and touch voltage; Series and parallel capacitor combinations; RC transient response
hx-em-stored-charge-hazard.Skill Description: Stored-charge hazard in bus capacitors — Calculate the energy and discharge time of a robot's bus capacitors through a bleed resistor, and decide when the bus is safe to touch after power-off.

hx-em-skin-effect.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-skin-effect.Prerequisite Names: Roots and radicals; Resistivity, conductivity and microscopic Ohm's law; Eddy currents
hx-em-skin-effect.Skill Description: Skin effect and skin depth — Calculate skin depth from resistivity, permeability and frequency, and explain why high-frequency current flows near a conductor's surface.

hx-pth-enclosure-impedance.Subject: Fluids for robots
hx-pth-enclosure-impedance.Prerequisite Names: Minor losses at bends, grilles and filters
hx-pth-enclosure-impedance.Skill Description: Enclosure airflow impedance curve — Build a system impedance curve for an enclosure, pressure drop proportional to flow squared, from component losses or a single measured point.

hx-pth-pcb-thermal-vias.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-pcb-thermal-vias.Skill Name: Heat spreading through PCB copper and thermal vias
hx-pth-pcb-thermal-vias.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Conduction thermal resistance of a slab; Thermal resistance networks
hx-pth-pcb-thermal-vias.Skill Description: Heat spreading through PCB copper and thermal vias — Calculate the conduction resistance of copper pours and arrays of plated thermal vias, and judge how much they lower a component's temperature.

hx-pth-junction-chain.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-junction-chain.Prerequisite Names: Conduction thermal resistance of a slab; Thermal resistance networks
hx-pth-junction-chain.Skill Description: Junction-to-ambient resistance chain from datasheets — Combine junction-to-case, case-to-sink and sink-to-ambient resistances from datasheets in series and compute junction temperature for a given dissipation.

hx-pth-contact-resistance.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-contact-resistance.Skill Name: Thermal contact resistance at clamped joints
hx-pth-contact-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Surface finish and contact behavior; Conduction thermal resistance of a slab
hx-pth-contact-resistance.Skill Description: Thermal contact resistance at clamped joints — Explain how surface roughness, flatness and clamping pressure create contact resistance at bolted interfaces, and estimate it from interface conductance data.

hx-pmc-lagrangian-pendulum.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-lagrangian-pendulum.Skill Name: Equation of motion of a pendulum by Lagrange
hx-pmc-lagrangian-pendulum.Prerequisite Names: Kinetic energy in generalized coordinates; Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-lagrangian-pendulum.Skill Description: Equation of motion of a pendulum by Lagrange — Form the Lagrangian of a simple and a physical pendulum, apply the Euler-Lagrange equation and recover the familiar nonlinear equation of motion.

hx-pth-led-efficacy-heat.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-led-efficacy-heat.Skill Name: LED efficacy, droop and junction heating
hx-pth-led-efficacy-heat.Prerequisite Names: Radiometric and photometric units; How LEDs emit light: bandgap and wavelength; Efficiency losses appear as heat
hx-pth-led-efficacy-heat.Skill Description: LED efficacy, droop and junction heating — Estimate the fraction of LED power converted to heat, explain efficiency droop at high current, and predict brightness and color shift as the junction warms.

hx-em-solenoid-field.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-solenoid-field.Skill Description: Magnetic field inside a solenoid — Use Ampere's law to show a long solenoid has a nearly uniform interior field of mu zero n I, and estimate field strength for a practical coil.

hx-em-toroid-field.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-toroid-field.Skill Description: Magnetic field inside a toroid — Use Ampere's law to find the field inside a toroidal coil, show it varies with radius and vanishes outside, and explain why toroids leak little flux.

hx-em-stray-field-estimate.Subject: Magnetostatics
hx-em-stray-field-estimate.Skill Name: Stray fields from robot wiring near a magnetometer
hx-em-stray-field-estimate.Prerequisite Names: Earth's magnetic field; Magnetic field of a long straight wire; Superposing fields of several currents
hx-em-stray-field-estimate.Skill Description: Stray fields from robot wiring near a magnetometer — Estimate the magnetic field a motor or battery cable produces at a magnetometer and compare it with Earth's field to set safe sensor placement distances.

hx-em-b-h-permeability.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-b-h-permeability.Prerequisite Names: Magnetization of matter; Ampere's law with symmetric currents
hx-em-b-h-permeability.Skill Description: B, H and permeability — Relate B, H and magnetization through B equals mu zero times H plus M, and use relative permeability and susceptibility for linear materials.

hx-em-displacement-current.Subject: Maxwell's equations
hx-em-displacement-current.Prerequisite Names: Capacitance and stored energy; Energy density of the electric field; Ampere's law with symmetric currents
hx-em-displacement-current.Skill Description: Displacement current — Explain why Ampere's law needs a displacement current term in a charging capacitor and calculate it from the rate of change of electric flux.

hx-pmc-damping-ratio.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-damping-ratio.Skill Name: Damping ratio and natural frequency from m, c and k
hx-pmc-damping-ratio.Prerequisite Names: Viscous damping and transient response; Classify underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion
hx-pmc-damping-ratio.Skill Description: Damping ratio and natural frequency from m, c and k — Compute undamped natural frequency, critical damping coefficient and damping ratio of a mass-spring-damper and relate them to its characteristic roots.

hx-pmc-energy-method-frequency.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-energy-method-frequency.Prerequisite Names: Rotational kinetic energy and power; Energy in simple harmonic motion
hx-pmc-energy-method-frequency.Skill Description: Energy method for natural frequency — Derive the natural frequency of a single-degree-of-freedom system from its kinetic and potential energy, including spring mass and lever arms.

hx-pmc-measure-inertia-pendulum.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-measure-inertia-pendulum.Skill Name: Measure moment of inertia by oscillation
hx-pmc-measure-inertia-pendulum.Prerequisite Names: Propagate uncertainty through products and quotients; Physical pendulum period; Torsional spring and inertia oscillator
hx-pmc-measure-inertia-pendulum.Skill Description: Measure moment of inertia by oscillation — Measure the moment of inertia of a robot link or rotor by timing compound-pendulum, bifilar or torsional oscillations and propagating timing uncertainty.

hx-pmc-two-inertia-torsional-modes.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-two-inertia-torsional-modes.Skill Name: Modes of a two-inertia torsional system
hx-pmc-two-inertia-torsional-modes.Prerequisite Names: Natural frequencies and mode shapes; Torsional spring and inertia oscillator
hx-pmc-two-inertia-torsional-modes.Skill Description: Modes of a two-inertia torsional system — Show that a motor and load joined by a flexible shaft have a zero-frequency rigid mode and one torsional mode, and compute that resonance frequency.

px-resonance-energy.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
px-resonance-energy.Skill Name: Explain energy transfer near a driven resonance
px-resonance-energy.Prerequisite Names: Mechanical power and efficiency; Forced vibration and resonance
px-resonance-energy.Skill Description: Explain energy transfer near a driven resonance — Explain how a periodic drive transfers energy into an oscillator most effectively near its natural frequency, with damping limiting the response.

hx-pth-thermal-time-constant.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-thermal-time-constant.Skill Name: Thermal time constant of a lumped body
hx-pth-thermal-time-constant.Prerequisite Names: Estimate temperature rise with a lumped model; Heat capacity of a multi-material part; Thermal resistance networks
hx-pth-thermal-time-constant.Skill Description: Thermal time constant of a lumped body — Compute a thermal time constant as thermal resistance times heat capacity and use it to judge how quickly a motor or heatsink approaches steady temperature.

px-entropy-transfer.Subject: Thermal
px-entropy-transfer.Skill Name: Calculate entropy transfer with reversible heat
px-entropy-transfer.Prerequisite Names: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin; Ratios and unit rates; Entropy and the second law
px-entropy-transfer.Skill Description: Calculate entropy transfer with reversible heat — Find the entropy change from heat transferred reversibly at constant absolute temperature using ΔS = Qrev/T.

px-carnot.Subject: Thermal
px-carnot.Skill Name: Calculate the reversible heat-engine efficiency bound
px-carnot.Prerequisite Names: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin; Ratios and unit rates; Thermodynamic cycles
px-carnot.Skill Description: Calculate the reversible heat-engine efficiency bound — Find the maximum possible efficiency of a heat engine between two reservoirs using 1 − Tcold/Thot.

px-isothermal.Subject: Thermal
px-isothermal.Skill Name: Calculate work for an ideal-gas isothermal expansion
px-isothermal.Prerequisite Names: Logarithms; Solve an ideal-gas state using absolute temperature and pressure; Calculate boundary work from a pressure-volume diagram
px-isothermal.Skill Description: Calculate work for an ideal-gas isothermal expansion — Find the work done by an ideal gas expanding reversibly at constant temperature using nRT ln(Vf/Vi).

hx-pth-ir-thermometry.Subject: Thermal radiation
hx-pth-ir-thermometry.Skill Name: Infrared thermometer and thermal camera readings
hx-pth-ir-thermometry.Prerequisite Names: Blackbody spectrum and Wien's displacement law; Emissivity of real surfaces
hx-pth-ir-thermometry.Skill Description: Infrared thermometer and thermal camera readings — Explain how infrared thermometers infer temperature, and correct or avoid errors from wrong emissivity settings and reflective metal surfaces when checking motors.

hx-pth-radiation-coefficient.Subject: Thermal radiation
hx-pth-radiation-coefficient.Prerequisite Names: Local linear approximation; Emissivity of real surfaces; Newton's law of cooling and convection resistance
hx-pth-radiation-coefficient.Skill Description: Linearized radiation heat transfer coefficient — Linearize net radiation into an equivalent coefficient proportional to emissivity times absolute temperature cubed, and add it in parallel with convection.

hx-pth-mic-transduction.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-mic-transduction.Prerequisite Names: Faraday and Lenz induction; Capacitance and stored energy; Sound pressure level from RMS pressure
hx-pth-mic-transduction.Skill Description: Microphone transduction principles — Explain how condenser, MEMS, dynamic and piezoelectric microphones convert pressure into voltage, and how pressure and pressure-gradient designs differ.

hx-pth-noise-spectra.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-noise-spectra.Skill Name: White, pink and tonal noise spectra
hx-pth-noise-spectra.Prerequisite Names: Fourier series; Sound pressure level from RMS pressure
hx-pth-noise-spectra.Skill Description: White, pink and tonal noise spectra — Distinguish white, pink and tonal noise by spectral shape, and identify motor whine, fan tones and broadband airflow noise on a spectrum plot.

hx-pth-fan-operating-point.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-fan-operating-point.Skill Name: Fan curve and system impedance operating point
hx-pth-fan-operating-point.Prerequisite Names: Enclosure airflow impedance curve; Size ventilation airflow for an enclosure
hx-pth-fan-operating-point.Skill Description: Fan curve and system impedance operating point — Intersect a fan's pressure-flow curve with an enclosure's quadratic impedance curve to find delivered airflow, and see why free-air ratings overstate real flow.

hx-pth-fin-efficiency.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-fin-efficiency.Skill Name: Fin efficiency of a straight fin
hx-pth-fin-efficiency.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Conduction thermal resistance of a slab; How heatsink fins add cooling area
hx-pth-fin-efficiency.Skill Description: Fin efficiency of a straight fin — Calculate the efficiency of a straight rectangular fin from its fin parameter and length, and explain why long thin fins add little cooling.

hx-pth-heatsink-curves.Subject: Convection and cooling
hx-pth-heatsink-curves.Skill Name: Read heatsink resistance versus airflow curves
hx-pth-heatsink-curves.Prerequisite Names: How heatsink fins add cooling area; Forced convection and the Nusselt number; Junction-to-ambient resistance chain from datasheets
hx-pth-heatsink-curves.Skill Description: Read heatsink resistance versus airflow curves — Read a heatsink's sink-to-ambient resistance at a given airflow or orientation from a datasheet curve and select a sink that meets a junction temperature limit.

hx-pth-dynamic-range.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-dynamic-range.Skill Name: Read noise, full-well capacity and dynamic range
hx-pth-dynamic-range.Prerequisite Names: Photon shot noise and signal-to-noise ratio; Decibel gain and frequency plots
hx-pth-dynamic-range.Skill Description: Read noise, full-well capacity and dynamic range — Compute sensor dynamic range in decibels and stops from full-well capacity and read noise, and predict when bright windows saturate a robot's view.

hx-em-solenoid-inductance.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-solenoid-inductance.Prerequisite Names: Inductance and stored energy; Flux linkage; Magnetic field inside a solenoid
hx-em-solenoid-inductance.Skill Description: Self-inductance of a solenoid — Derive L equals mu zero N squared A over length from flux linkage, and predict how turns, area and length change a coil's inductance.

hx-em-battery-short-hazard.Subject: Electrical safety physics
hx-em-battery-short-hazard.Skill Name: Low-voltage high-current burn and arc hazards
hx-em-battery-short-hazard.Prerequisite Names: Joule heating as microscopic power density; Battery capacity, energy, and internal resistance
hx-em-battery-short-hazard.Skill Description: Low-voltage high-current burn and arc hazards — Calculate short-circuit current and dissipated power from a battery's internal resistance, and explain why rings, tools and loose wires cause burns at low voltage.

hx-em-ac-resistance.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-ac-resistance.Skill Name: AC resistance, proximity effect and litz wire
hx-em-ac-resistance.Prerequisite Names: Wire resistance from geometry; Skin effect and skin depth
hx-em-ac-resistance.Skill Description: AC resistance, proximity effect and litz wire — Estimate a wire's AC resistance at a given frequency from skin depth, explain proximity effect between adjacent conductors, and when litz or flat conductors help.

hx-pth-tim-selection.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-tim-selection.Prerequisite Names: Thermal contact resistance at clamped joints
hx-pth-tim-selection.Skill Description: Choose a thermal interface material — Compare thermal paste, gap pads, phase-change films and adhesives by conductivity, bond-line thickness and compliance, and compute the resulting interface resistance.

hx-pmc-double-pendulum.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-double-pendulum.Skill Name: Equations of motion of a double pendulum
hx-pmc-double-pendulum.Prerequisite Names: Equation of motion of a pendulum by Lagrange
hx-pmc-double-pendulum.Skill Description: Equations of motion of a double pendulum — Derive the coupled equations of a planar double pendulum with Lagrange equations and identify mass-matrix, Coriolis and gravity terms.

hx-pmc-generalized-forces.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-generalized-forces.Skill Name: Generalized forces from applied forces and torques
hx-pmc-generalized-forces.Prerequisite Names: Principle of virtual work for mechanism statics; Equation of motion of a pendulum by Lagrange
hx-pmc-generalized-forces.Skill Description: Generalized forces from applied forces and torques — Compute the generalized force for each coordinate from applied joint torques, external forces and viscous friction using virtual work.

hx-em-dia-para.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-dia-para.Skill Description: Diamagnetism and paramagnetism — Distinguish diamagnetic and paramagnetic materials by the sign and tiny size of their susceptibility, and explain why neither matters for motor design.

hx-em-reluctance.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-reluctance.Prerequisite Names: B, H and permeability; Magnetic field inside a toroid
hx-em-reluctance.Skill Description: Magnetic circuits and reluctance — Model a magnetic core as a circuit with magnetomotive force N I, reluctance length over mu A and flux, by analogy with Ohm's law.

hx-em-maxwell-integral.Subject: Maxwell's equations
hx-em-maxwell-integral.Prerequisite Names: Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry; Induced electric fields; Gauss's law for magnetism; Displacement current
hx-em-maxwell-integral.Skill Description: Maxwell's equations in integral form — State the four Maxwell equations in integral form, identify the physical law and sources behind each, and choose the right one for a given field problem.

hx-pmc-cantilever-frequency.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-cantilever-frequency.Skill Name: First bending frequency of a cantilever
hx-pmc-cantilever-frequency.Prerequisite Names: Natural frequency from static deflection; Beam deflection; Energy method for natural frequency
hx-pmc-cantilever-frequency.Skill Description: First bending frequency of a cantilever — Estimate the first bending natural frequency of a cantilever beam with and without a tip mass using the standard mode constant and an equivalent spring.

hx-pmc-forced-steady-state.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-forced-steady-state.Prerequisite Names: Polar form and Euler's formula; Forced vibration and resonance; Damping ratio and natural frequency from m, c and k
hx-pmc-forced-steady-state.Skill Description: Steady-state response to harmonic forcing — Find the steady-state amplitude and phase lag of a damped oscillator driven by a sinusoidal force, and plot the magnification factor against frequency ratio.

hx-pth-derating-curve.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-derating-curve.Skill Name: Read and apply a thermal derating curve
hx-pth-derating-curve.Skill Description: Read and apply a thermal derating curve — Read a power or current derating curve versus ambient temperature, and compute allowed dissipation from maximum junction temperature and the thermal resistance chain.

hx-pth-polar-patterns.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-polar-patterns.Skill Description: Microphone polar patterns and directivity — Plot omnidirectional, cardioid and figure-eight polar patterns in polar coordinates and predict off-axis rejection of robot self-noise.

hx-pth-mic-sensitivity.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-mic-sensitivity.Prerequisite Names: Decibel gain and frequency plots; Microphone transduction principles
hx-pth-mic-sensitivity.Skill Description: Microphone sensitivity, self-noise and SNR — Convert sensitivity in dBV per pascal or dBFS to output level at a given SPL, and compute signal-to-noise ratio from equivalent self-noise.

hx-pth-checkpoint-s2.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-pth-checkpoint-s2.Prerequisite Names: Fin efficiency of a straight fin
hx-pth-checkpoint-s2.Skill Description: Physics checkpoint: stage 2 (controlled joint) — Demonstrate the 1 end-of-branch physics skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 2 integration milestone.

hx-em-rotating-field.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-rotating-field.Skill Name: Rotating magnetic field from three-phase currents
hx-em-rotating-field.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric identities; Magnetic field inside a solenoid; Three-phase systems
hx-em-rotating-field.Skill Description: Rotating magnetic field from three-phase currents — Show that three windings spaced 120 degrees and fed balanced three-phase currents produce a constant-magnitude field rotating at synchronous speed.

hx-em-b-energy-density.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-b-energy-density.Skill Name: Energy stored in a magnetic field
hx-em-b-energy-density.Skill Description: Energy stored in a magnetic field — Show that an inductor's energy equals B squared over two mu zero times its field volume, and use magnetic energy density to compare stored energies.

hx-em-mutual-inductance.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-mutual-inductance.Skill Description: Mutual inductance and coupling coefficient — Calculate mutual inductance between coaxial coils, use reciprocity, and relate the coupling coefficient to how much flux the two windings share.

hx-em-rl-time-constant.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-rl-time-constant.Skill Name: RL time constant from coil physics
hx-em-rl-time-constant.Prerequisite Names: RL transient response; Wire resistance from geometry; First-order linear equations; Self-inductance of a solenoid
hx-em-rl-time-constant.Skill Description: RL time constant from coil physics — Derive an RL current rise from Faraday's law as a first-order differential equation and compute L over R for a coil from its geometry and wire resistance.

hx-em-shielding-physics.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-shielding-physics.Skill Name: Shielding physics: reflection, absorption and magnetic shielding
hx-em-shielding-physics.Prerequisite Names: Electrostatic shielding by a closed conductor; Skin effect and skin depth; Magnetic circuits and reluctance
