hx-em-shielding-physics.Skill Description: Shielding physics: reflection, absorption and magnetic shielding — Explain shielding by reflection and absorption, estimate absorption loss from thickness in skin depths, and why low-frequency magnetic fields need high-permeability shields.

hx-pmc-lagrangian-cart-pole.Subject: Lagrangian mechanics
hx-pmc-lagrangian-cart-pole.Skill Name: Equations of motion of a cart-pole by Lagrange
hx-pmc-lagrangian-cart-pole.Prerequisite Names: Equation of motion of a pendulum by Lagrange; Generalized forces from applied forces and torques
hx-pmc-lagrangian-cart-pole.Skill Description: Equations of motion of a cart-pole by Lagrange — Derive the two coupled nonlinear equations of a pendulum on a horizontally driven cart using Lagrange equations with a generalized input force.

hx-em-air-gap.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-air-gap.Skill Description: Air gaps in magnetic circuits — Show that a small air gap dominates total reluctance, calculate gap flux density for a gapped core, and explain fringing and why gaps stabilize inductance.

hx-em-ferromagnetism.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-ferromagnetism.Skill Name: Ferromagnetism, domains and the Curie temperature
hx-em-ferromagnetism.Skill Description: Ferromagnetism, domains and the Curie temperature — Explain how exchange coupling aligns spins into domains, how domain walls move under applied field, and why ferromagnetism vanishes above the Curie temperature.

hx-em-maxwell-differential.Subject: Maxwell's equations
hx-em-maxwell-differential.Prerequisite Names: Green, Stokes, and divergence theorems; Maxwell's equations in integral form
hx-em-maxwell-differential.Skill Description: Maxwell's equations in differential form — Convert the integral Maxwell equations to divergence and curl form using the divergence and Stokes theorems, and interpret each as a local statement about fields.

hx-pmc-base-excitation.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-base-excitation.Skill Description: Base excitation and transmissibility — Compute displacement and force transmissibility for a mass on a spring and damper whose base vibrates, and find where transmissibility drops below one.

hx-pmc-msd-frequency-response.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-msd-frequency-response.Prerequisite Names: Laplace transforms; Decibel gain and frequency plots; Steady-state response to harmonic forcing
hx-pmc-msd-frequency-response.Skill Description: Frequency response of a mass-spring-damper — Derive the transfer function from force to displacement of a mass-spring-damper, draw its Bode magnitude and phase, and locate the resonant peak.

hx-em-coenergy-force.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-coenergy-force.Prerequisite Names: Derivative as local rate; Air gaps in magnetic circuits; Energy stored in a magnetic field
hx-em-coenergy-force.Skill Description: Force from magnetic field energy — Derive mechanical force from the change in stored magnetic energy or coenergy with position, including F equals one half i squared dL/dx at constant current.

hx-em-loop-area-pickup.Subject: Electromagnetic induction
hx-em-loop-area-pickup.Skill Name: Inductive noise pickup and loop area
hx-em-loop-area-pickup.Prerequisite Names: Magnetic field of a long straight wire; Mutual inductance and coupling coefficient
hx-em-loop-area-pickup.Skill Description: Inductive noise pickup and loop area — Estimate the voltage induced in a signal loop by a nearby switching current and show why reducing loop area and distance cuts magnetic coupling.

hx-em-wave-equation.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-wave-equation.Prerequisite Names: Partial derivatives; Maxwell's equations in differential form
hx-em-wave-equation.Skill Description: Wave equation from Maxwell's equations — Combine Faraday's and Ampere-Maxwell laws in empty space to derive a one-dimensional wave equation for the electric and magnetic fields.

hx-pmc-cart-pole-linear-model.Subject: Inverted pendulum and balance
hx-pmc-cart-pole-linear-model.Skill Name: Linear state-space model of a cart-pole
hx-pmc-cart-pole-linear-model.Prerequisite Names: Linearize the inverted pendulum about upright; Linear systems of ODEs; Equations of motion of a cart-pole by Lagrange
hx-pmc-cart-pole-linear-model.Skill Description: Linear state-space model of a cart-pole — Linearize the cart-pole equations about the upright equilibrium and write the four-state linear model with cart force as input.

hx-pmc-products-of-inertia.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-products-of-inertia.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a rectangular plate and block; Three-Dimensional Vectors in Component Form
hx-pmc-products-of-inertia.Skill Description: Products of inertia — Compute products of inertia by integration or from symmetry, and state when they vanish for bodies with planes of symmetry.

hx-em-bh-curve.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-bh-curve.Prerequisite Names: Interpreting physical graphs; Ferromagnetism, domains and the Curie temperature
hx-em-bh-curve.Skill Description: Magnetization curves and saturation — Read a B-H magnetization curve to extract initial permeability and saturation flux density, and explain why permeability falls as the core approaches saturation.

hx-pmc-vibration-isolation.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-vibration-isolation.Prerequisite Names: Natural frequency from static deflection; Base excitation and transmissibility
hx-pmc-vibration-isolation.Skill Description: Vibration isolation design — Choose isolator stiffness and damping so the excitation frequency exceeds the square root of two times natural frequency, for camera, IMU and motor mounts.

hx-pmc-angular-velocity-vector.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-angular-velocity-vector.Skill Name: Angular velocity and acceleration as vectors
hx-pmc-angular-velocity-vector.Prerequisite Names: Angular position, speed, and acceleration; Cross products; Three-Dimensional Vectors in Component Form
hx-pmc-angular-velocity-vector.Skill Description: Angular velocity and acceleration as vectors — Represent angular velocity and angular acceleration as vectors along the rotation axis by the right-hand rule and add angular velocities of nested rotations.

hx-em-reluctance-force.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-reluctance-force.Skill Name: Reluctance force of a solenoid actuator
hx-em-reluctance-force.Skill Description: Reluctance force of a solenoid actuator — Calculate the pull force across an air gap from B squared A over two mu zero, and explain why solenoid and brake force rises sharply as the gap closes.

hx-em-reluctance-torque.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-reluctance-torque.Skill Description: Reluctance torque — Derive torque from the change of inductance with rotor angle and explain how reluctance torque drives switched-reluctance and hybrid stepper motors.

hx-em-speed-of-light.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-speed-of-light.Prerequisite Names: Convert among wave period, frequency, and wavelength; Wave equation from Maxwell's equations
hx-em-speed-of-light.Skill Description: Speed of electromagnetic waves — Compute the speed of light from mu zero and epsilon zero, and find wave speed and wavelength in a dielectric such as cable insulation or PCB substrate.

hx-pmc-inertia-about-arbitrary-axis.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-inertia-about-arbitrary-axis.Skill Name: Moment of inertia about an arbitrary axis
hx-pmc-inertia-about-arbitrary-axis.Prerequisite Names: Matrix arithmetic; Symmetric matrices and quadratic forms; Products of inertia
hx-pmc-inertia-about-arbitrary-axis.Skill Description: Moment of inertia about an arbitrary axis — Assemble the 3 by 3 inertia matrix from moments and products, and compute the inertia about any unit axis as the quadratic form n transpose I n.

hx-em-eddy-core-loss.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-eddy-core-loss.Prerequisite Names: Eddy currents; Magnetization curves and saturation
hx-em-eddy-core-loss.Skill Description: Eddy-current core loss and laminations — Estimate eddy-current loss in a magnetic core as proportional to sheet thickness squared and frequency squared, and justify laminations, ferrites and powdered cores.

hx-em-hysteresis-loop.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-hysteresis-loop.Skill Description: Hysteresis loops, remanence and coercivity — Trace a hysteresis loop through a magnetizing cycle and read remanent flux density and coercive field strength from it.

hx-em-inductor-saturation.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-inductor-saturation.Prerequisite Names: Self-inductance of a solenoid; Air gaps in magnetic circuits; Magnetization curves and saturation
hx-em-inductor-saturation.Skill Description: Inductor core saturation — Predict the current at which a cored inductor saturates from its geometry and saturation flux density, and explain the resulting collapse of inductance and current spike.

hx-pth-inverse-square-sound.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-inverse-square-sound.Prerequisite Names: Wave power and intensity; Sound pressure level from RMS pressure; Surface Areas of Spheres
hx-pth-inverse-square-sound.Skill Description: Inverse-square spreading of sound — Predict sound level at a new distance from a point source using spherical spreading, losing about six decibels per doubling of distance in free field.

hx-em-wave-e-b.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-wave-e-b.Skill Name: E and B fields in a plane wave
hx-em-wave-e-b.Prerequisite Names: Cross products; Speed of electromagnetic waves
hx-em-wave-e-b.Skill Description: E and B fields in a plane wave — Describe a plane electromagnetic wave with perpendicular, in-phase E and B fields transverse to propagation, and use E equals c B to relate their amplitudes.

px-force-components.Subject: Forces
px-force-components.Skill Name: Resolve a force vector along chosen axes
px-force-components.Prerequisite Names: Vector components and arithmetic; Mass, inertia, and net force; Calculating Side Lengths of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
px-force-components.Skill Description: Resolve a force vector along chosen axes — Project a known force onto two perpendicular axes.

px-projectile-components.Subject: Kinematics
px-projectile-components.Prerequisite Names: Two-dimensional motion components; Calculating Side Lengths of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
px-projectile-components.Skill Description: Resolve a projectile launch velocity — Split a projectile's launch speed and angle into horizontal and vertical velocity components.

hx-pth-illuminance.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-illuminance.Skill Name: Luminous intensity, solid angle and illuminance
hx-pth-illuminance.Prerequisite Names: Radiometric and photometric units; Surface Areas of Spheres
hx-pth-illuminance.Skill Description: Luminous intensity, solid angle and illuminance — Relate candela, lumens per steradian and lux, use solid angle to convert a beam's intensity to flux, and apply the inverse-square law for illuminance.

hx-pmc-principal-axes.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-principal-axes.Skill Name: Principal moments and axes of inertia
hx-pmc-principal-axes.Prerequisite Names: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Moment of inertia about an arbitrary axis
hx-pmc-principal-axes.Skill Description: Principal moments and axes of inertia — Find principal moments and axes of a rigid body as eigenvalues and eigenvectors of its symmetric inertia matrix, and explain why principal axes are orthogonal.

hx-em-hysteresis-loss.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-hysteresis-loss.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; Hysteresis loops, remanence and coercivity
hx-em-hysteresis-loss.Skill Description: Hysteresis core loss — Calculate hysteresis energy loss per cycle from loop area and core volume, and scale it to power loss with frequency using a Steinmetz-type relation.

hx-em-soft-hard.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-soft-hard.Skill Description: Soft versus hard magnetic materials — Classify silicon steel, ferrite, powdered iron, NdFeB, SmCo and AlNiCo as soft or hard from loop shape, and match each to cores or permanent magnets.

px-torque-sign.Subject: Rotation and oscillation
px-torque-sign.Skill Name: Calculate a planar torque with a signed lever arm
px-torque-sign.Prerequisite Names: Angles and geometric relationships; Mass, inertia, and net force; Calculating Side Lengths of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
px-torque-sign.Skill Description: Calculate a planar torque with a signed lever arm — Compute a torque in a plane as force times perpendicular lever arm, and give it a clockwise or counterclockwise sign.

hx-pth-room-acoustics.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-room-acoustics.Skill Name: Room modes, early reflections and critical distance
hx-pth-room-acoustics.Prerequisite Names: Standing waves in open and closed tubes; Reverberation time with Sabine's formula; Inverse-square spreading of sound
hx-pth-room-acoustics.Skill Description: Room modes, early reflections and critical distance — Describe low-frequency room modes, early reflections and the critical distance where direct and reverberant sound are equal, and their effect on robot hearing.

hx-pth-diffuse-return.Subject: Camera and sensor optics
hx-pth-diffuse-return.Skill Name: Diffuse versus specular returns in active sensing
hx-pth-diffuse-return.Prerequisite Names: Apply the law of specular reflection; Luminous intensity, solid angle and illuminance
hx-pth-diffuse-return.Skill Description: Diffuse versus specular returns in active sensing — Explain Lambertian diffuse reflection, specular mirrors and retroreflectors, and predict weak or false returns from dark, shiny or glass targets.

hx-em-motor-loss-split.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-motor-loss-split.Skill Name: Copper, core and mechanical loss in motors
hx-em-motor-loss-split.Prerequisite Names: Joule heating as microscopic power density; Eddy-current core loss and laminations; Hysteresis core loss
hx-em-motor-loss-split.Skill Description: Copper, core and mechanical loss in motors — Separate motor losses into copper loss scaling with current squared, core loss scaling with speed and flux, and friction, and predict how each varies across operating points.

hx-em-poynting.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-poynting.Prerequisite Names: Energy density of the electric field; Energy stored in a magnetic field; E and B fields in a plane wave
hx-em-poynting.Skill Description: Poynting vector and intensity — Calculate the Poynting vector and time-averaged intensity of an electromagnetic wave, and estimate field amplitude at a distance from an isotropic transmitter's power.

hx-em-antenna-basics.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-antenna-basics.Skill Name: Radiation from accelerated charge and dipole antennas
hx-em-antenna-basics.Prerequisite Names: Convert among wave period, frequency, and wavelength; E and B fields in a plane wave
hx-em-antenna-basics.Skill Description: Radiation from accelerated charge and dipole antennas — Explain that oscillating charges radiate, size a half-wave dipole for a given frequency, and sketch its doughnut-shaped radiation pattern.

px-projectile-time.Subject: Kinematics
px-projectile-time.Skill Name: Calculate projectile flight time to a specified height
px-projectile-time.Prerequisite Names: Constant-acceleration motion; Solving quadratic equations; Resolve a projectile launch velocity
px-projectile-time.Skill Description: Calculate projectile flight time to a specified height — Solve the vertical motion equation, usually a quadratic in time, for when a projectile reaches a given height.

hx-pth-luminance.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-luminance.Prerequisite Names: Luminous intensity, solid angle and illuminance
hx-pth-luminance.Skill Description: Luminance of displays and surfaces — Define luminance in candela per square meter, compute it for a diffuse lit surface, and compare a face display's nits with indoor and daylight conditions.

hx-em-hard-soft-iron.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-hard-soft-iron.Prerequisite Names: Earth's magnetic field; Soft versus hard magnetic materials
hx-em-hard-soft-iron.Skill Description: Hard-iron and soft-iron distortion physics — Explain how nearby magnets add a constant offset field and nearby steel bends the local field, producing the hard-iron and soft-iron distortions seen by magnetometers.

hx-em-demag-curve.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-demag-curve.Skill Name: Permanent magnet demagnetization curve and grades
hx-em-demag-curve.Skill Description: Permanent magnet demagnetization curve and grades — Read the second-quadrant demagnetization curve, maximum energy product and N-grade ratings of permanent magnets to compare remanence and coercivity across grades.

hx-pmc-force-3d-components.Subject: Vector mechanics in 3D
hx-pmc-force-3d-components.Skill Name: Resolve a force along a line in 3D
hx-pmc-force-3d-components.Prerequisite Names: Three-Dimensional Vectors in Component Form; Unit Vectors; Addition and Scalar Multiplication of Cartesian Vectors in 3D; Resolve a force vector along chosen axes
hx-pmc-force-3d-components.Skill Description: Resolve a force along a line in 3D — Write a force acting along a cable or link as magnitude times a unit vector built from two point coordinates, and add concurrent 3D forces by components.

hx-em-near-far-field.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-near-far-field.Prerequisite Names: Radiation from accelerated charge and dipole antennas
hx-em-near-far-field.Skill Description: Near field versus far field — Estimate the boundary between reactive near field and radiating far field from wavelength, and explain why near-field coupling is mostly electric or magnetic.

hx-em-radiation-pressure.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-radiation-pressure.Prerequisite Names: Linear momentum; Poynting vector and intensity
hx-em-radiation-pressure.Skill Description: Radiation pressure — Calculate radiation pressure for absorbed and reflected waves from intensity and speed of light, and judge when it is negligible compared with other forces.

px-projectile-range.Subject: Kinematics
px-projectile-range.Prerequisite Names: Calculate projectile flight time to a specified height
px-projectile-range.Skill Description: Calculate horizontal projectile displacement — Multiply the constant horizontal velocity by the flight time to find how far a projectile travels sideways.

hx-pth-light-diffusion.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-light-diffusion.Skill Name: Diffusing LED light without hot spots
hx-pth-light-diffusion.Prerequisite Names: Diffuse versus specular returns in active sensing; Luminance of displays and surfaces
hx-pth-light-diffusion.Skill Description: Diffusing LED light without hot spots — Choose diffuser material, thickness and LED-to-diffuser spacing so discrete LEDs blend into an even glowing surface for eyes or a face panel.

hx-pth-dimming-perception.Subject: Light sources and displays
hx-pth-dimming-perception.Skill Name: PWM dimming, flicker and perceived brightness
hx-pth-dimming-perception.Prerequisite Names: Fractional exponents; Interpret PWM duty and period; Luminance of displays and surfaces
hx-pth-dimming-perception.Skill Description: PWM dimming, flicker and perceived brightness — Explain why perceived brightness is nonlinear in duty cycle, apply gamma correction, and choose PWM frequencies that avoid visible flicker and camera banding.

hx-em-magnet-temperature.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-magnet-temperature.Skill Name: Magnet temperature effects and irreversible demagnetization
hx-em-magnet-temperature.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Permanent magnet demagnetization curve and grades
hx-em-magnet-temperature.Skill Description: Magnet temperature effects and irreversible demagnetization — Use temperature coefficients and temperature-grade suffixes to predict remanence loss with heat and identify the operating point where irreversible demagnetization begins.

hx-em-magnet-in-circuit.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-magnet-in-circuit.Skill Name: Permanent magnet operating point with an air gap
hx-em-magnet-in-circuit.Prerequisite Names: Air gaps in magnetic circuits; Permanent magnet demagnetization curve and grades
hx-em-magnet-in-circuit.Skill Description: Permanent magnet operating point with an air gap — Combine a magnet's demagnetization curve with the load line of an iron path and air gap to find the magnet's operating point and gap flux density.

hx-em-back-emf-waveform.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-back-emf-waveform.Prerequisite Names: Emf of a coil rotating in a uniform field; Permanent magnet operating point with an air gap
hx-em-back-emf-waveform.Skill Description: Back-EMF waveform shape — Relate a motor's back-EMF waveform to its air-gap flux distribution and winding layout, distinguishing trapezoidal from sinusoidal back-EMF machines.

hx-em-cogging-torque.Subject: Electromechanical energy conversion
hx-em-cogging-torque.Prerequisite Names: Reluctance torque; Permanent magnet operating point with an air gap
hx-em-cogging-torque.Skill Description: Cogging torque — Explain how magnets seeking minimum-reluctance positions against stator slots create cogging torque, and how slot-pole combinations and skew reduce it.

hx-em-antenna-placement.Subject: EM waves, skin effect and shielding
hx-em-antenna-placement.Skill Name: Antenna placement in a metal robot body
hx-em-antenna-placement.Prerequisite Names: Electrostatic shielding by a closed conductor; Near field versus far field
hx-em-antenna-placement.Skill Description: Antenna placement in a metal robot body — Judge how metal frames, batteries, cables and the human body detune or block a robot's Wi-Fi and radio antennas, and choose placements that keep links reliable.

hx-em-flux-concentration.Subject: Magnetic materials and circuits
hx-em-flux-concentration.Skill Name: Back iron, flux concentration and Halbach arrays
hx-em-flux-concentration.Prerequisite Names: Permanent magnet operating point with an air gap
hx-em-flux-concentration.Skill Description: Back iron, flux concentration and Halbach arrays — Explain how back iron, pole pieces and Halbach magnet arrangements steer and concentrate flux into the working gap while limiting leakage and saturation.

hx-pmc-damped-free-response.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-damped-free-response.Prerequisite Names: Solve the simple harmonic oscillator equation; Damping ratio and natural frequency from m, c and k; Euler's Formula
hx-pmc-damped-free-response.Skill Description: Underdamped free response — Write the underdamped free response as a decaying sinusoid, compute the damped natural frequency and the exponential envelope from initial conditions.

hx-pmc-log-decrement.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-log-decrement.Skill Description: Logarithmic decrement — Estimate damping ratio from the ratio of successive peaks in measured ring-down data using the logarithmic decrement.

hx-pmc-quality-factor.Subject: Oscillations and vibration
hx-pmc-quality-factor.Skill Name: Quality factor and energy loss per cycle
hx-pmc-quality-factor.Prerequisite Names: Explain energy transfer near a driven resonance; Underdamped free response
hx-pmc-quality-factor.Skill Description: Quality factor and energy loss per cycle — Relate quality factor to damping ratio, energy dissipated per cycle and resonance bandwidth for a lightly damped oscillator.

hx-pmc-velocity-omega-cross-r.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-velocity-omega-cross-r.Skill Name: Point velocity from omega cross r
hx-pmc-velocity-omega-cross-r.Prerequisite Names: Convert angular velocity to tangential speed; Angular velocity and acceleration as vectors; Calculating the Cross Product Using Determinants
hx-pmc-velocity-omega-cross-r.Skill Description: Point velocity from omega cross r — Compute the velocity of any point on a body rotating about a fixed axis in 3D as the cross product of angular velocity with the position vector.

hx-pth-arrhenius-lifetime.Subject: Thermodynamics essentials
hx-pth-arrhenius-lifetime.Prerequisite Names: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin; Solving Exponential Decay Problems
hx-pth-arrhenius-lifetime.Skill Description: Temperature and component lifetime — Apply an Arrhenius acceleration factor and the rule of thumb that lifetime halves per ten-degree rise to estimate capacitor, battery and lubricant life at operating temperature.

hx-pmc-moment-cross-product.Subject: Vector mechanics in 3D
hx-pmc-moment-cross-product.Skill Name: Moment of a force as a cross product
hx-pmc-moment-cross-product.Prerequisite Names: Torque and lever arms; Resolve a force along a line in 3D; Calculating the Cross Product Using Determinants
hx-pmc-moment-cross-product.Skill Description: Moment of a force as a cross product — Compute the moment of a 3D force about a point as r cross F using the determinant form, and interpret its direction with the right-hand rule.

hx-pth-cylinder-conduction.Subject: Heat conduction
hx-pth-cylinder-conduction.Skill Name: Radial conduction through a cylindrical shell
hx-pth-cylinder-conduction.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; Conduction thermal resistance of a slab; The Natural Logarithm
hx-pth-cylinder-conduction.Skill Description: Radial conduction through a cylindrical shell — Derive and apply the logarithmic thermal resistance of a cylindrical shell for heat flowing outward through motor housings, winding insulation and pipe walls.

hx-pmc-rigid-relative-velocity.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-velocity.Skill Name: Relative velocity of two points on a rigid body
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-velocity.Prerequisite Names: Relative motion and reference frames; Point velocity from omega cross r
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-velocity.Skill Description: Relative velocity of two points on a rigid body — Relate velocities of two points on a body in planar motion with v_B equals v_A plus omega cross r_B/A, and solve simple linkage velocities.

hx-pmc-rotating-point-acceleration.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-rotating-point-acceleration.Skill Name: Tangential and centripetal acceleration of a rotating point
hx-pmc-rotating-point-acceleration.Prerequisite Names: Uniform circular motion; Point velocity from omega cross r
hx-pmc-rotating-point-acceleration.Skill Description: Tangential and centripetal acceleration of a rotating point — Split the acceleration of a point on a rotating body into alpha cross r and omega cross omega cross r, and evaluate both for an accelerating link.

hx-pmc-angular-momentum-vector.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-angular-momentum-vector.Skill Name: Angular momentum of particles and rigid bodies
hx-pmc-angular-momentum-vector.Prerequisite Names: Angular momentum conservation; Moment of inertia about an arbitrary axis; Moment of a force as a cross product
hx-pmc-angular-momentum-vector.Skill Description: Angular momentum of particles and rigid bodies — Compute angular momentum as r cross p for particles and as the inertia matrix times angular velocity for a rigid body, noting when L is not parallel to omega.

hx-pmc-couple-moment-3d.Subject: Vector mechanics in 3D
hx-pmc-couple-moment-3d.Skill Name: Couple moments as free vectors in 3D
hx-pmc-couple-moment-3d.Prerequisite Names: Replace an equal-and-opposite force couple with its signed moment; Moment of a force as a cross product
hx-pmc-couple-moment-3d.Skill Description: Couple moments as free vectors in 3D — Represent a couple as a free moment vector independent of reference point, and add several couples acting in different planes by vector components.

hx-pmc-moment-about-axis.Subject: Vector mechanics in 3D
hx-pmc-moment-about-axis.Skill Name: Moment of a force about a specified axis
hx-pmc-moment-about-axis.Prerequisite Names: Moment of a force as a cross product; The Scalar Triple Product
hx-pmc-moment-about-axis.Skill Description: Moment of a force about a specified axis — Find the component of a moment along a given axis, such as a joint axis, using the scalar triple product with the axis unit vector.

hx-pmc-pivoted-body-impact.Subject: Collisions and impact
hx-pmc-pivoted-body-impact.Skill Name: Impact on a pivoted rigid body
hx-pmc-pivoted-body-impact.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a slender rod; Coefficient of restitution; Angular momentum of particles and rigid bodies
hx-pmc-pivoted-body-impact.Skill Description: Impact on a pivoted rigid body — Solve an impact between a particle and a pivoted link, using conservation of angular momentum about the pivot together with the restitution condition.

hx-pmc-accelerometer-specific-force.Subject: Non-inertial frames
hx-pmc-accelerometer-specific-force.Prerequisite Names: Inertial forces in a linearly accelerating frame; Inertial measurement units; Tangential and centripetal acceleration of a rotating point
hx-pmc-accelerometer-specific-force.Skill Description: What an accelerometer measures — Explain that an accelerometer reads specific force, acceleration minus gravity, and compute extra centripetal and tangential readings from an off-center mounting.

hx-pmc-rigid-relative-acceleration.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-acceleration.Skill Name: Relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-acceleration.Prerequisite Names: Relative velocity of two points on a rigid body; Tangential and centripetal acceleration of a rotating point
hx-pmc-rigid-relative-acceleration.Skill Description: Relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body — Relate accelerations of two points on a body in general planar motion, including tangential and centripetal relative terms, to analyze links and wheels.

hx-pmc-gyroscopic-precession.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-gyroscopic-precession.Prerequisite Names: Angular impulse and momentum change; Angular momentum of particles and rigid bodies
hx-pmc-gyroscopic-precession.Skill Description: Gyroscopic precession and gyroscopic torque — Calculate the steady precession rate of a spinning rotor under gravity and the gyroscopic torque on bearings when a spinning rotor is turned about another axis.

hx-pmc-rotating-frame-derivative.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-rotating-frame-derivative.Skill Name: Time derivative of a vector in a rotating frame
hx-pmc-rotating-frame-derivative.Prerequisite Names: Point velocity from omega cross r; Differentiating Vector-Valued Functions
hx-pmc-rotating-frame-derivative.Skill Description: Time derivative of a vector in a rotating frame — Apply the transport theorem, inertial derivative equals body-frame derivative plus omega cross the vector, to velocities, momentum and angular momentum.

hx-pmc-supports-3d.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-supports-3d.Prerequisite Names: Replace ideal planar supports with their allowed reaction components; Couple moments as free vectors in 3D
hx-pmc-supports-3d.Skill Description: Reactions of 3D supports and connections — Identify the force and couple reactions supplied by ball-and-socket joints, hinges, journal bearings, thrust bearings and fixed supports in three dimensions.

hx-pmc-force-couple-3d.Subject: Vector mechanics in 3D
hx-pmc-force-couple-3d.Skill Name: Reduce a 3D force system to a force and couple
hx-pmc-force-couple-3d.Prerequisite Names: Move a force to another point using an equivalent force-and-couple system; Couple moments as free vectors in 3D
hx-pmc-force-couple-3d.Skill Description: Reduce a 3D force system to a force and couple — Replace any set of forces and couples with one resultant force and one resultant couple at a chosen point, the basis of wrench representation.

hx-pmc-effective-mass-at-contact.Subject: Collisions and impact
hx-pmc-effective-mass-at-contact.Skill Name: Effective mass of an arm at a contact point
hx-pmc-effective-mass-at-contact.Prerequisite Names: Equivalent inertia of a drive by energy equivalence; Peak impact force from contact stiffness; Impact on a pivoted rigid body
hx-pmc-effective-mass-at-contact.Skill Description: Effective mass of an arm at a contact point — Compute the effective mass a geared robot link presents at a contact point from its total reflected inertia and lever arm, and its effect on impact force.

hx-pmc-coriolis-acceleration.Subject: Non-inertial frames
hx-pmc-coriolis-acceleration.Skill Name: Coriolis acceleration in a rotating frame
hx-pmc-coriolis-acceleration.Prerequisite Names: Centrifugal force in a rotating frame; Time derivative of a vector in a rotating frame
hx-pmc-coriolis-acceleration.Skill Description: Coriolis acceleration in a rotating frame — Compute the Coriolis term minus two omega cross v for a body moving within a rotating frame, such as a gripper sliding along a turning arm.

hx-pmc-rolling-accelerations.Subject: Rigid-body rotational kinematics
hx-pmc-rolling-accelerations.Prerequisite Names: Apply the no-slip rolling constraint; Relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body
hx-pmc-rolling-accelerations.Skill Description: Accelerations of a rolling wheel — Apply the no-slip constraint to relate center acceleration and angular acceleration of a wheel, and show the contact point accelerates toward the center.

hx-pmc-planar-rigid-dynamics.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-planar-rigid-dynamics.Skill Name: Equations of general planar rigid-body motion
hx-pmc-planar-rigid-dynamics.Prerequisite Names: Newton's second law in components; Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body
hx-pmc-planar-rigid-dynamics.Skill Description: Equations of general planar rigid-body motion — Write sum of forces equals mass times center-of-mass acceleration and sum of moments about the center equals I alpha for a body in general planar motion.

hx-pmc-equilibrium-3d.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-equilibrium-3d.Skill Name: Equilibrium of a rigid body in 3D
hx-pmc-equilibrium-3d.Prerequisite Names: Force and torque equilibrium; Resolve a force along a line in 3D; Moment of a force about a specified axis; Reactions of 3D supports and connections
hx-pmc-equilibrium-3d.Skill Description: Equilibrium of a rigid body in 3D — Write and solve the six scalar equilibrium equations for a rigid body, choosing moment axes that eliminate unknown reactions, for shafts and brackets.

hx-pmc-rolling-force-dynamics.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-rolling-force-dynamics.Skill Name: Forces on an accelerating rolling wheel
hx-pmc-rolling-force-dynamics.Prerequisite Names: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis; Determine the required static-friction force; Accelerations of a rolling wheel
hx-pmc-rolling-force-dynamics.Skill Description: Forces on an accelerating rolling wheel — Apply force and moment equations to a driven or braked wheel, find the friction force required for rolling, and check it against the slip limit.

hx-pmc-linked-bodies-fbd.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-linked-bodies-fbd.Skill Name: Free-body diagrams for linked rigid bodies
hx-pmc-linked-bodies-fbd.Prerequisite Names: Transfer a known joint force between separate member diagrams; Identify which interaction forces cancel when two bodies form one system; Equations of general planar rigid-body motion
hx-pmc-linked-bodies-fbd.Skill Description: Free-body diagrams for linked rigid bodies — Draw separate dynamic free-body diagrams for connected bodies, such as a cart with a pendulum or a two-link arm, and solve joint forces with accelerations.

hx-pmc-pivot-reaction-forces.Subject: Rotational dynamics
hx-pmc-pivot-reaction-forces.Skill Name: Pivot reactions on a swinging link
hx-pmc-pivot-reaction-forces.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a slender rod; Equations of general planar rigid-body motion
hx-pmc-pivot-reaction-forces.Skill Description: Pivot reactions on a swinging link — Find the pivot reaction forces on a link rotating about a fixed joint, such as a rod released from horizontal, using tangential and normal center-of-mass acceleration.

hx-pth-db-addition.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-db-addition.Prerequisite Names: Sound pressure level from RMS pressure; Combining the Laws of Logarithms
hx-pth-db-addition.Skill Description: Adding incoherent sources in decibels — Combine the levels of independent noise sources by summing their intensities, and show that doubling identical sources adds about three decibels.

hx-pth-speaker-spl.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-speaker-spl.Skill Name: Loudspeaker sensitivity and required amplifier power
hx-pth-speaker-spl.Prerequisite Names: Moving-coil loudspeaker principles; Inverse-square spreading of sound; Combining the Laws of Logarithms
hx-pth-speaker-spl.Skill Description: Loudspeaker sensitivity and required amplifier power — Use speaker sensitivity in dB at 1 W and 1 m with distance loss to find the amplifier power needed for a target speech level at a listener.

hx-pmc-center-of-percussion.Subject: Collisions and impact
hx-pmc-center-of-percussion.Prerequisite Names: Impact on a pivoted rigid body; Pivot reactions on a swinging link
hx-pmc-center-of-percussion.Skill Description: Center of percussion — Locate the point on a pivoted link where an impact produces no impulsive pivot reaction, and use it to reduce shock loads on joints.

hx-pmc-pivot-acceleration-balance.Subject: Inverted pendulum and balance
hx-pmc-pivot-acceleration-balance.Prerequisite Names: Linearize the inverted pendulum about upright; Free-body diagrams for linked rigid bodies
hx-pmc-pivot-acceleration-balance.Skill Description: Balancing by accelerating the support — Calculate the horizontal support acceleration needed to hold a tall body at a given lean angle, the physics behind wheeled balancing and leaning while braking.

hx-pth-frequency-weighting.Subject: Acoustics
hx-pth-frequency-weighting.Skill Name: A-weighting and C-weighting of sound levels
hx-pth-frequency-weighting.Prerequisite Names: White, pink and tonal noise spectra; Adding incoherent sources in decibels
hx-pth-frequency-weighting.Skill Description: A-weighting and C-weighting of sound levels — Group a spectrum into octave bands, apply A and C weighting corrections to report dBA and dBC, and explain why A-weighting approximates human hearing.

px-velocity-derivative.Subject: Kinematics
px-velocity-derivative.Prerequisite Names: Find average velocity from two position readings; Derivative as local rate; The Power Rule for Differentiation
px-velocity-derivative.Skill Description: Differentiate position to obtain velocity — Differentiate a position function with respect to time to get instantaneous velocity at any moment.

px-acceleration-derivative.Subject: Kinematics
px-acceleration-derivative.Prerequisite Names: Acceleration; Differentiate position to obtain velocity
px-acceleration-derivative.Skill Description: Differentiate velocity to obtain acceleration — Differentiate a velocity function with respect to time to find acceleration and interpret its sign.

hx-pmc-moi-sphere.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-sphere.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of a sphere and spherical shell
hx-pmc-moi-sphere.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a ring, disk and annulus; Integration Using Substitution
hx-pmc-moi-sphere.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of a sphere and spherical shell — Integrate thin disks or shells to obtain the moment of inertia of a solid sphere and a thin spherical shell about a diameter.

hx-pth-checkpoint-s1.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-pth-checkpoint-s1.Prerequisite Codes: PHY-MIN-003, PHY-ELP-002, PHY-WAV-008, PHY-ELE-012, PHY-ELP-004, PHY-ELE-011, PHY-ROD-004, PHY-CAD-004, PHY-CAD-005, PHY-MAN-009, PHY-ROD-007, PHY-EWS-010, PHY-OSV-020, PHY-COI-005, PHY-MIN-011
hx-pth-checkpoint-s1.Prerequisite Names: Radius of gyration; Potential energy of a system of charges; The one-dimensional wave equation; Electric field on the axis of a charged disk; Equipotential surfaces; Electric field of a finite line charge; Energy of rolling bodies; Capacitance of coaxial cylinders; Dielectric polarization and bound charge; Force between parallel currents; Work done by a variable torque; Radiation pressure; Quality factor and energy loss per cycle; Center of percussion; Moment of inertia of a sphere and spherical shell
hx-pth-checkpoint-s1.Skill Description: Physics checkpoint: stage 1 (foundations) — Demonstrate the 15 end-of-branch physics skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 1 integration milestone.

hx-pmc-centroid-integration.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-centroid-integration.Skill Name: Centroid of an area by integration
hx-pmc-centroid-integration.Prerequisite Names: Calculate center of mass for a set of point masses; The Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of X
hx-pmc-centroid-integration.Skill Description: Centroid of an area by integration — Locate the centroid of a planar shape bounded by curves by integrating first moments of area over vertical or horizontal strips.

hx-pmc-belt-friction-derivation.Subject: Friction in mechanisms
hx-pmc-belt-friction-derivation.Skill Name: Derive belt friction from a differential element
hx-pmc-belt-friction-derivation.Prerequisite Names: Exponential models; Static and kinetic friction; Solving First-Order ODEs Using Separation of Variables
hx-pmc-belt-friction-derivation.Skill Description: Derive belt friction from a differential element — Derive the exponential tension ratio for a flat belt or rope wrapped on a drum by balancing forces on a small arc element and separating variables.

hx-pmc-com-composite.Subject: Statics of rigid bodies in 3D
hx-pmc-com-composite.Skill Name: Center of mass of a composite body
hx-pmc-com-composite.Prerequisite Names: Center of mass; Three-Dimensional Vectors in Component Form; Centroid of an area by integration
hx-pmc-com-composite.Skill Description: Center of mass of a composite body — Compute the 3D center of mass of an assembly of standard shapes, treating holes and cutouts as negative mass, and check it against CAD values.

hx-pmc-com-ground-reaction.Subject: Inverted pendulum and balance
hx-pmc-com-ground-reaction.Prerequisite Names: Equations of general planar rigid-body motion; Center of mass of a composite body
hx-pmc-com-ground-reaction.Skill Description: Center-of-mass acceleration and ground reaction — Relate total ground reaction force to center-of-mass acceleration and the moment balance about the center of mass to the location of the center of pressure.

hx-pmc-moi-composite.Subject: Moment of inertia
hx-pmc-moi-composite.Skill Name: Moment of inertia of a composite body
hx-pmc-moi-composite.Prerequisite Names: Moment of inertia of a rectangular plate and block; Moment of inertia of solid and hollow cylinders; Center of mass of a composite body
hx-pmc-moi-composite.Skill Description: Moment of inertia of a composite body — Combine standard-shape inertias with the parallel-axis theorem, subtracting holes, to find the inertia of a link with motor and payload about a joint axis.

hx-pth-exponential-heating.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-exponential-heating.Prerequisite Names: Thermal time constant of a lumped body; Modeling With First-Order ODEs
hx-pth-exponential-heating.Skill Description: Exponential heating and cooling curves — Solve the first-order lumped thermal model for a step in power and predict temperature at any time during heating and after the load is removed.

hx-pth-short-duty-averaging.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-short-duty-averaging.Skill Name: Average heating under fast duty cycles
hx-pth-short-duty-averaging.Prerequisite Names: Definite integrals and accumulation; AC amplitude, phase, and RMS; Exponential heating and cooling curves
hx-pth-short-duty-averaging.Skill Description: Average heating under fast duty cycles — Explain why a duty cycle much shorter than the thermal time constant heats a winding according to mean squared current, and compute that average dissipation.

hx-pth-time-to-limit.Subject: Transient heating and duty
hx-pth-time-to-limit.Skill Name: Time to reach a temperature limit under overload
hx-pth-time-to-limit.Prerequisite Names: Solving Logarithmic Equations Containing the Natural Logarithm; Exponential heating and cooling curves
hx-pth-time-to-limit.Skill Description: Time to reach a temperature limit under overload — Solve the exponential heating curve with a natural logarithm to find how long an overloaded joint can run before reaching its winding limit.

s-atom.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-atom.Skill Description: Atoms, elements, and electron structure — Distinguish atomic number, isotopes, and electron arrangement, and see how outer electrons shape chemical and material behaviour.

s-bond.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-bond.Skill Description: Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding — Compare ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding as electron transfer, sharing, and delocalization, and link each to material properties.

s-strain.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-strain.Prerequisite Names: Angles and geometric relationships; Ratios and unit rates
s-strain.Skill Description: Normal and shear strain — Measure deformation as relative change in length or change in angle, independent of an object's overall size.

s-crystal.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-crystal.Prerequisite Names: Cartesian coordinates; Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding
s-crystal.Skill Description: Crystalline and amorphous structure — Distinguish crystalline solids with long-range periodic atomic order from amorphous solids that lack it, and compare their behaviour.

s-secondary.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-secondary.Skill Description: Secondary bonding and intermolecular forces — Distinguish weak intermolecular forces such as van der Waals and hydrogen bonds from the primary bonds inside molecules.

sss-mat-engineering-strain.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-engineering-strain.Skill Name: Calculate engineering strain from a stated gauge length
sss-mat-engineering-strain.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Unit conversions
sss-mat-engineering-strain.Skill Description: Calculate engineering strain from a stated gauge length — Calculate engineering strain as the change in gauge length divided by its original length.
sss-mat-engineering-strain.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-engineering-stress.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-engineering-stress.Skill Name: Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area
sss-mat-engineering-stress.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Unit conversions
sss-mat-engineering-stress.Skill Description: Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area — Convert a tensile force measurement into engineering stress by dividing it by the original cross-sectional area.
sss-mat-engineering-stress.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

s-thermalexpand.Subject: Material families and processing
s-thermalexpand.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Normal and shear strain
s-thermalexpand.Skill Description: Thermal expansion and mismatch — Relate temperature change to dimensional change and predict the effects of joining materials that expand differently.

s-polymer.Subject: Material families and processing
s-polymer.Prerequisite Names: Crystalline and amorphous structure; Secondary bonding and intermolecular forces
s-polymer.Skill Description: Thermoplastics and thermosets — Distinguish polymers that soften and can be remelted from those that cure into a permanently crosslinked network.

s-grains.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-grains.Skill Description: Grains and grain boundaries — Describe polycrystalline materials as many crystal grains of different orientation and explain how grain boundaries affect properties.

s-defects.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-defects.Skill Description: Point defects and dislocations — Distinguish point defects such as vacancies and substitutional atoms from line defects called dislocations, and explain their effects.

s-unitcell.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-unitcell.Prerequisite Names: Surface area and volume; Crystalline and amorphous structure
s-unitcell.Skill Description: Unit cells and lattice geometry — Describe a crystal by its repeating unit cell, count atoms per cell, and connect cell geometry to density and packing.

sss-mat-current-area-stress.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-current-area-stress.Skill Name: Compare nominal and current-area average stress using measured areas
sss-mat-current-area-stress.Prerequisite Names: Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area
sss-mat-current-area-stress.Skill Description: Compare nominal and current-area average stress using measured areas — At a given tensile load, calculate nominal stress with the original area and current-area average stress with the measured current section.
sss-mat-current-area-stress.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-elastic-versus-linear.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-elastic-versus-linear.Skill Name: Distinguish recoverable deformation from linear stress-strain response
sss-mat-elastic-versus-linear.Prerequisite Names: Normal and shear strain; Interpreting physical graphs
sss-mat-elastic-versus-linear.Skill Description: Distinguish recoverable deformation from linear stress-strain response — Elastic response concerns recovery after unloading, while linear response concerns the shape of a stress-strain relationship.
sss-mat-elastic-versus-linear.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-modulus-slope.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-modulus-slope.Skill Name: Extract Young’s modulus from a specified linear stress-strain interval
sss-mat-modulus-slope.Prerequisite Names: Slope and intercept; Calculate engineering strain from a stated gauge length; Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area
sss-mat-modulus-slope.Skill Description: Extract Young’s modulus from a specified linear stress-strain interval — Find Young’s modulus from the stress change divided by the strain change over a stated linear elastic interval.
sss-mat-modulus-slope.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-engineering-uts.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-engineering-uts.Skill Name: Find ultimate tensile strength from peak load and original area
sss-mat-engineering-uts.Prerequisite Names: Interpreting physical graphs; Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area
sss-mat-engineering-uts.Skill Description: Find ultimate tensile strength from peak load and original area — Locate the maximum recorded tensile load and divide it by the original specimen area to obtain ultimate tensile strength.
sss-mat-engineering-uts.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-differential-expansion.Subject: Material families and processing
sss-mat-differential-expansion.Skill Name: Calculate differential expansion between joined parts
sss-mat-differential-expansion.Skill Description: Calculate differential expansion between joined parts — Calculate how much two joined parts of different materials change length relative to each other over a temperature range, and its effect on a fit or a fastened joint.

s-metal.Subject: Material families and processing
s-metal.Skill Description: Engineering metals and alloy families — Compare metallic material families through density, stiffness, strength, corrosion behavior, and ease of processing.

s-symmetry.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-symmetry.Prerequisite Names: Vector components and arithmetic; Unit cells and lattice geometry
s-symmetry.Skill Description: Crystal symmetry and directional properties — Relate a crystal's symmetry to whether its physical properties can vary with direction, and recognize anisotropic materials.

s-additive.Subject: Material families and processing
s-additive.Prerequisite Names: Thermoplastics and thermosets; Engineering metals and alloy families; Crystal symmetry and directional properties
s-additive.Skill Description: Additive manufacturing and build direction — Distinguish 3D printing process families and recognize how build orientation, porosity, supports, and postprocessing affect parts.

s-aluminum.Subject: Material families and processing
s-aluminum.Skill Description: Aluminum alloys — Weigh aluminum alloys' low density and easy machining against their lower stiffness, temperature limits, joining issues, and corrosion.

s-titanium.Subject: Material families and processing
s-titanium.Skill Description: Titanium and specialty alloys — Compare titanium and other specialty alloys by specific performance, temperature and corrosion capability, and fabrication cost.

s-load.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-load.Skill Description: Load paths and structural idealization — Trace how external loads travel through a structure to its supports and choose a suitably simplified model for analysis.

sss-mat-process-dimensions.Subject: Material families and processing
sss-mat-process-dimensions.Skill Name: Relate processing choices to dimensional change
sss-mat-process-dimensions.Skill Description: Relate processing choices to dimensional change — Predict how a manufacturing process will change a part's dimensions, such as shrinkage, warping, quench distortion or stress-relief movement, and plan an allowance for it.

s-diffraction.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-diffraction.Prerequisite Names: Unit cells and lattice geometry; Diffraction and resolution
s-diffraction.Skill Description: Diffraction for structure identification — Use Bragg's law and diffraction peak positions to identify crystal structures, lattice spacings, and phases in a material.

s-stress.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-stress.Prerequisite Names: Perimeter and planar area; Newton's second law in components
s-stress.Skill Description: Normal and shear stress — Relate internal force components to the area resisting them, and distinguish normal stress from shear stress.

s-fits.Subject: Material families and processing
s-fits.Prerequisite Names: Significant figures and resolution; Linear inequalities and intervals; Load paths and structural idealization
s-fits.Skill Description: Fits, tolerances, and datum references — Specify allowed size and geometric variation and reference it to datum features that reflect how parts function and assemble.

s-machining.Subject: Material families and processing
s-machining.Prerequisite Names: Engineering metals and alloy families; Load paths and structural idealization
s-machining.Skill Description: Machining fundamentals — Relate cutting forces, tool access, workholding, and material behavior to the geometry and accuracy a machined part can achieve.

s-section.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-section.Skill Description: Area moments of inertia — Calculate a cross section's second moment of area about a stated axis to predict its resistance to bending and buckling.

s-elastic.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-elastic.Prerequisite Names: Slope and intercept; Normal and shear strain; Normal and shear stress
s-elastic.Skill Description: Elastic modulus and linear elasticity — Relate small elastic stress and strain with an elastic modulus, and separate stiffness from strength.

s-concentration.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-concentration.Prerequisite Names: Load paths and structural idealization; Normal and shear stress
s-concentration.Skill Description: Stress concentrations — Recognize and estimate the local rise in stress near holes, notches, and sharp corners.

s-stressstate.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-stressstate.Prerequisite Names: Trigonometric identities; Normal and shear stress
s-stressstate.Skill Description: Stress transformations and principal stress — Find the stresses acting on planes at any orientation and identify the principal stresses and their directions.

s-adhesive.Subject: Material families and processing
s-adhesive.Prerequisite Names: Thermoplastics and thermosets; Normal and shear stress
s-adhesive.Skill Description: Adhesive joints — Relate surface preparation, bond geometry, and loading mode to the strength and durability of bonded joints.

sss-mech-datum-scheme.Subject: Material families and processing
sss-mech-datum-scheme.Prerequisite Names: Produce a manufacturing drawing; Fits, tolerances, and datum references
sss-mech-datum-scheme.Skill Description: Build a functional datum scheme — Choose a part's primary, secondary and tertiary datums from how it mounts and works, and dimension its critical features from them.

s-stack.Subject: Material families and processing
s-stack.Prerequisite Names: Absolute value and distance; Fits, tolerances, and datum references
s-stack.Skill Description: Tolerance stack analysis — Combine dimensional variations along a chain of parts using a clearly chosen worst-case or statistical model.

s-dielectric.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-dielectric.Prerequisite Names: Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding; Electric force and field
s-dielectric.Skill Description: Dielectric properties — Explain dielectric polarization and distinguish relative permittivity, dielectric loss, and breakdown strength in insulating materials.

s-magnetic.Subject: Materials structure and bonding
s-magnetic.Prerequisite Names: Atoms, elements, and electron structure; Magnetic fields and forces
s-magnetic.Skill Description: Magnetic material response — Distinguish diamagnetic, paramagnetic, and ferromagnetic behaviour, and interpret domains, hysteresis, and soft versus hard magnetic materials.

s-axial.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-axial.Prerequisite Names: Load paths and structural idealization; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-axial.Skill Description: Axial deformation of bars — Calculate how much a bar stretches or shortens under axial load from its length, area, and elastic modulus.

s-fracture.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-fracture.Prerequisite Names: Stress concentrations; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-fracture.Skill Description: Cracks and fracture toughness — Explain why a crack can cause failure far below a material's nominal strength and how fracture toughness quantifies crack resistance.

sss-mat-nominal-peak.Subject: Materials mechanics
sss-mat-nominal-peak.Prerequisite Names: Compare nominal and current-area average stress using measured areas; Stress concentrations
sss-mat-nominal-peak.Skill Description: Distinguish nominal and peak stress — Compute both the nominal stress on a net section and the peak stress at a notch, and decide which one a given check should use.

s-buckling.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-buckling.Prerequisite Names: Force and torque equilibrium; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity; Area moments of inertia
s-buckling.Skill Description: Elastic buckling of columns — Recognize sudden sideways instability in slender compressed members and estimate the critical load from stiffness, length, and end restraints.

s-composite.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-composite.Prerequisite Names: Direct and inverse proportion; Crystal symmetry and directional properties; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-composite.Skill Description: Fiber composites and load sharing — Estimate how fibers and matrix share load in a composite and why its stiffness and strength depend strongly on direction.

s-fea.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-fea.Prerequisite Names: Matrix arithmetic; Load paths and structural idealization; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-fea.Skill Description: Finite-element model concepts — Understand how finite-element analysis approximates a structure with elements, material laws, loads, and boundary conditions solved as a matrix system.

s-poisson.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-poisson.Skill Description: Poisson effect and shear modulus — Describe how materials contract sideways when stretched, and relate Poisson's ratio, Young's modulus, and shear modulus.

sss-mech-distributed-resultant.Subject: Materials mechanics
sss-mech-distributed-resultant.Skill Name: Replace a distributed load with an equivalent resultant
sss-mech-distributed-resultant.Prerequisite Names: Load paths and structural idealization; Force and torque equilibrium
sss-mech-distributed-resultant.Skill Description: Replace a distributed load with an equivalent resultant — Replace a load spread along a beam with a single force equal to its total, acting at its centroid, for use in external equilibrium.

s-torsion.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-torsion.Prerequisite Names: Torque and lever arms; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-torsion.Skill Description: Torsion of circular shafts — Relate transmitted torque to shear stress and angle of twist in solid and hollow circular shafts.

s-viscoelastic.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-viscoelastic.Prerequisite Names: Temperature and thermal equilibrium; Differential equations and initial values; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
s-viscoelastic.Skill Description: Viscoelastic response — Describe materials whose response depends on loading time and rate, combining spring-like and fluid-like behaviour.

s-plastic.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-plastic.Skill Description: Yielding and plastic deformation — Distinguish recoverable elastic strain from permanent plastic deformation and explain the role of yield strength and yield criteria.

sss-mat-axial-stiffness.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-axial-stiffness.Skill Name: Compare axial part stiffness after changing length, area, or modulus
sss-mat-axial-stiffness.Prerequisite Names: Ratios and unit rates; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity
sss-mat-axial-stiffness.Skill Description: Compare axial part stiffness after changing length, area, or modulus — For a uniform straight bar under small, linear elastic axial deformation, use k=EA/L to compare force-per-extension stiffness.
sss-mat-axial-stiffness.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

s-finish.Subject: Material families and processing
s-finish.Prerequisite Names: Fits, tolerances, and datum references; Static and kinetic friction
s-finish.Skill Description: Surface finish and contact behavior — Distinguish overall geometric form from waviness and fine surface texture, and understand how each affects contact.

sss-mech-effective-length.Subject: Materials mechanics
sss-mech-effective-length.Skill Name: Check effective-length assumptions in a buckling model
sss-mech-effective-length.Skill Description: Check effective-length assumptions in a buckling model — Choose the effective-length factor from how a column's ends are really held, and check how much the buckling load depends on that choice.

s-creep.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-creep.Skill Description: Creep and stress relaxation — Distinguish creep, where strain grows under constant stress, from stress relaxation, where stress falls under constant strain.

sss-mat-fiber-direction.Subject: Materials mechanics
sss-mat-fiber-direction.Skill Name: Distinguish fibre-direction effects from isotropic response
sss-mat-fiber-direction.Skill Description: Distinguish fibre-direction effects from isotropic response — Compute a fibre composite's stiffness along and across its fibres and recognize when an isotropic formula would mislead.

sss-mat-yield-vs-crack.Subject: Materials mechanics
sss-mat-yield-vs-crack.Prerequisite Names: Cracks and fracture toughness; Yielding and plastic deformation
sss-mat-yield-vs-crack.Skill Description: Distinguish yielding from crack-driven failure — For a part with a known crack, compare the stress that would cause yielding with the stress that would cause fast fracture, and say which comes first.

s-failurecriterion.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-failurecriterion.Prerequisite Names: Stress transformations and principal stress; Yielding and plastic deformation
s-failurecriterion.Skill Description: Ductile and brittle failure criteria — Choose a failure criterion suited to ductile yielding or brittle fracture and apply it to combined stress states.

s-fatigue.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-fatigue.Skill Description: Fatigue under repeated loading — Explain how repeated load cycles can grow cracks and cause failure at stresses well below a material's static strength.

s-tensile.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-tensile.Prerequisite Names: Interpreting physical graphs; Yielding and plastic deformation
s-tensile.Skill Description: Interpreting tensile-test curves — Read modulus, yield strength, ultimate strength, ductility, and fracture from a stress-strain curve, including engineering versus true values.

s-laminate.Subject: Materials mechanics
s-laminate.Prerequisite Names: Matrix arithmetic; Fiber composites and load sharing
s-laminate.Skill Description: Laminates and anisotropic stiffness — Describe how stacked plies at different angles set a laminate's stiffness and create coupling between stretching, bending, and twisting.

sss-mat-proof-stress.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-proof-stress.Skill Name: Determine 0.2 percent offset proof stress from a tensile curve
sss-mat-proof-stress.Prerequisite Names: Extract Young’s modulus from a specified linear stress-strain interval; Yielding and plastic deformation
sss-mat-proof-stress.Skill Description: Determine 0.2 percent offset proof stress from a tensile curve — Draw a line with the measured elastic slope starting at strain 0.002, and read the stress where it intersects the tensile curve.
sss-mat-proof-stress.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-property-selection.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-property-selection.Skill Name: Distinguish modulus, yield strength, and tensile strength in property data
sss-mat-property-selection.Prerequisite Names: Find ultimate tensile strength from peak load and original area; Elastic modulus and linear elasticity; Yielding and plastic deformation
sss-mat-property-selection.Skill Description: Distinguish modulus, yield strength, and tensile strength in property data — Choose the property column that answers the question being asked: modulus describes elastic stress-to-strain response, yield strength describes a stated yielding criterion, and tensile strength identifies a peak engineering tensile stress..
sss-mat-property-selection.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

sss-mat-permanent-set.Subject: Material behavior and tensile testing
sss-mat-permanent-set.Skill Name: Estimate residual strain using a stated linear elastic unloading model
sss-mat-permanent-set.Prerequisite Names: Extract Young’s modulus from a specified linear stress-strain interval; Yielding and plastic deformation
sss-mat-permanent-set.Skill Description: Estimate residual strain using a stated linear elastic unloading model — For a specified uniaxial state with total strain epsilon and tensile stress sigma, subtract the recoverable strain sigma/E to estimate residual strain.
sss-mat-permanent-set.Atlas Domain / Subdomain: Mechanics / Material behavior and tensile testing

s-fastener.Subject: Material families and processing
s-fastener.Prerequisite Names: Force and torque equilibrium; Static and kinetic friction; Axial deformation of bars
s-fastener.Skill Description: Bolted joints and preload — Distinguish bolt preload from service load and use joint stiffness to see how added load is shared, and when joints slip or separate.

s-carbonfiber.Subject: Material families and processing
s-carbonfiber.Prerequisite Names: Thermoplastics and thermosets; Fiber composites and load sharing
s-carbonfiber.Skill Description: Carbon-fiber reinforced structures — Relate fiber orientation, resin, joints, and damage sensitivity to how carbon-fiber composite structures carry load.

s-ceramic.Subject: Material families and processing
s-ceramic.Prerequisite Names: Crystalline and amorphous structure; Cracks and fracture toughness
s-ceramic.Skill Description: Ceramics and glasses — Compare hard, often brittle ceramics and glasses and their uses as wear surfaces, insulators, and high-temperature materials.

s-elastomer.Subject: Material families and processing

hx-mec-bearing-life.Subject: Shafts, bearings and couplings
hx-mec-bearing-life.Prerequisite Names: Integer powers; Bearing types and their load directions
hx-mec-bearing-life.Skill Description: Bearing rating life calculation — Compute equivalent dynamic load and L10 rating life from catalog ratings, and check static load capacity for shock and holding loads.

hx-mec-bearing-fits-mounting.Subject: Shafts, bearings and couplings

hx-mec-bearing-fits-mounting.Skill Description: Bearing seat fits and mounting practice — Pick shaft and housing tolerances for rotating and stationary rings, design shoulder heights, and press bearings in without loading through the balls.

hx-mec-coupling-types.Skill Description: Select a shaft coupling — Distinguish parallel, angular and axial misalignment and select rigid, jaw, beam, Oldham or bellows couplings by torque, torsional stiffness and backlash.

hx-mec-motor-shaft-interface.Subject: Shafts, bearings and couplings

hx-mec-motor-shaft-interface.Skill Description: Attach gears and pulleys to shafts — Transmit torque to hubs with keys, D-flats, set screws or clamp hubs, sizing a key for shear while avoiding radial overload of motor bearings.

hx-mec-bearing-preload.Skill Description: Bearing preload methods — Apply bearing preload with wave springs, shims or ground spacers, and explain the trade between joint stiffness, play and friction torque.

hx-mec-shaft-sizing.Skill Description: Size a shaft for combined loading and stiffness — Combine bending and torsional stress with von Mises, then choose a shaft diameter meeting deflection limits and fatigue life at shoulders and keyways.

hx-mec-base-chassis.Skill Description: Design a wheeled base chassis — Design a mobile base chassis with drive wheels supported on their own bearings, casters, low centre of mass, battery bay, bumpers and a stiff deck.

hx-mec-crossed-roller-bearing.Subject: Shafts, bearings and couplings
hx-mec-crossed-roller-bearing.Prerequisite Names: Bearing preload methods; Select and mount bearings for a rotating joint

hx-mec-checkpoint-s6.Skill Description: Mechanical Design & Fabrication checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid) — Demonstrate the 3 end-of-branch mechanical design & fabrication skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 6 integration milestone.

hx-mec-cad-mass-properties.Skill Description: Mass properties from a CAD model — Assign materials and densities, then read mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor about a chosen frame and check them against hand estimates.

hx-mec-cad-to-urdf.Skill Description: Export a CAD assembly to a robot description — Export link meshes, joint frames, masses and inertias from a CAD assembly into a URDF and check frames and inertias against the model.

hx-mec-arm-mass-distribution.Subject: Robot mechanical design
hx-mec-arm-mass-distribution.Skill Name: Arm mass distribution and joint torque

hx-mec-torso-frame.Skill Description: Design a humanoid torso frame — Design a torso frame that carries both shoulders and the neck, houses electronics and transfers arm loads into the base with adequate stiffness.

hx-mec-hip-pelvis-structure.Skill Description: Design a hip and pelvis structure — Design a pelvis and three-axis hip that carries body weight and walking moments through large bearings into stiff, compact leg mounts.

hx-mec-leg-structure.Skill Description: Design legs for walking loads — Design thigh and shank structures with knee actuator placement and low distal mass, sized for repeated impacts and fatigue during walking.
