hx-ai-vla-finetune.Skill Description: Fine-tune a VLA on robot demonstrations — Collect teleoperated demonstrations and fine-tune a vision-language-action model with LoRA on a multi-GPU server, then evaluate success on held-out tasks.

hx-ai-latency-budget.Subject: Dialogue and translation
hx-ai-latency-budget.Prerequisite Names: Low-latency streaming speech synthesis; Streaming speech recognition and endpointing; Choose between local and cloud language models; Mass, power, compute and latency budgets
hx-ai-latency-budget.Skill Description: Conversational latency budget — Break response latency into VAD, ASR, LLM first token, TTS first audio and playback stages, measure each, and meet a target turn gap.

hx-ai-dialogue-manager.Subject: Dialogue and translation
hx-ai-dialogue-manager.Prerequisite Names: Barge-in handling; Dialogue state tracking and slot filling; Conversation memory; LLM tool calling to robot skills; Conversational latency budget
hx-ai-dialogue-manager.Skill Description: Dialogue management and turn-taking — Integrate dialogue state, memory, tool calls, turn-taking and barge-in into one manager that runs a natural spoken conversation with a robot.

hx-ai-compute-partition.Subject: Evaluation and deployment
hx-ai-compute-partition.Skill Name: Partition AI workloads across robot, server and cloud
hx-ai-compute-partition.Prerequisite Names: Deploy models on edge hardware; Choose between local and cloud language models; Conversational latency budget
hx-ai-compute-partition.Skill Description: Partition AI workloads across robot, server and cloud — Allocate speech, language, vision and policy models between onboard computers, a local GPU server and cloud services to meet latency, privacy and outage needs.

hx-ai-realtime-interpretation.Subject: Dialogue and translation
hx-ai-realtime-interpretation.Prerequisite Names: Multilingual conversation; Dialogue management and turn-taking
hx-ai-realtime-interpretation.Skill Description: Real-time interpretation between two people — Act as a live interpreter between two speakers of different languages, managing turns, latency and uncertain phrases while keeping both parties informed.

hx-ai-action-confirmation.Subject: AI safety and governance
hx-ai-action-confirmation.Prerequisite Names: Dialogue state tracking and slot filling; Validate AI-proposed robot actions; Robot risk assessment
hx-ai-action-confirmation.Skill Description: Confirm before consequential physical actions — Assign actions to risk tiers and require spoken read-back and explicit confirmation before higher-risk motions, handing objects or touching people.

hx-ai-unsafe-command-refusal.Subject: AI safety and governance
hx-ai-unsafe-command-refusal.Prerequisite Names: Prompt and configure a large language model; Validate AI-proposed robot actions; Robot risk assessment
hx-ai-unsafe-command-refusal.Skill Description: Refuse unsafe or out-of-scope commands — Detect commands that could harm people, property or the robot, refuse them politely with a reason, and offer a safe alternative when one exists.

hx-ai-action-guardrails.Subject: AI safety and governance
hx-ai-action-guardrails.Prerequisite Names: Spoken stop and human override; Prompt injection and untrusted inputs; Confirm before consequential physical actions; Refuse unsafe or out-of-scope commands
hx-ai-action-guardrails.Skill Description: Guardrails on AI-commanded robot actions — Layer validation, refusal, confirmation, injection defenses and hardware stops so no single model error can cause an unsafe robot action.

hx-ai-voice-task-pipeline.Subject: AI safety and governance
hx-ai-voice-task-pipeline.Skill Name: Command a robot task safely by voice
hx-ai-voice-task-pipeline.Prerequisite Names: Ground language references in the scene; Log and audit AI decisions; Execution monitoring and replanning; Dialogue management and turn-taking; Guardrails on AI-commanded robot actions
hx-ai-voice-task-pipeline.Skill Description: Command a robot task safely by voice — Integrate speech, dialogue, grounded planning and guardrails so a spoken request becomes a verified, confirmed and logged robot task.

hx-ai-checkpoint-s6.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-ai-checkpoint-s6.Skill Name: AI, Learning & Language checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid)
hx-ai-checkpoint-s6.Prerequisite Codes: AIL-SPA-008, AIL-LAM-015, AIL-EVD-008, AIL-VLA-005, AIL-EVD-009, AIL-DIT-009, AIL-ASG-009
hx-ai-checkpoint-s6.Prerequisite Names: Speaker identification with consent; Etiquette and protocol knowledge base; Red-team AI behavior; Fine-tune a VLA on robot demonstrations; Partition AI workloads across robot, server and cloud; Real-time interpretation between two people; Command a robot task safely by voice
hx-ai-checkpoint-s6.Skill Description: AI, Learning & Language checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid) — Demonstrate the 7 end-of-branch ai, learning & language skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 6 integration milestone.

hx-hri-scope-of-hri.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-scope-of-hri.Prerequisite Names: Describe an observable task and its limits
hx-hri-scope-of-hri.Skill Description: Scope of human-robot interaction — Explain what human-robot interaction studies, why social robots differ from industrial ones, and which factors (usefulness, ease, social fit) drive whether people accept a robot.

hx-hri-mental-models.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-mental-models.Skill Description: Users' mental models of robots — Explain how people form mental models of what a robot perceives, knows and can do, and predict misunderstandings when the robot's behavior contradicts those models.

hx-hri-anthropomorphism.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-anthropomorphism.Skill Description: Anthropomorphism and social attribution — Describe how humanlike form, voice and motion lead people to attribute intentions, emotions and agency to a robot, and when this helps or misleads interaction.

hx-hri-facial-action-units.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-facial-action-units.Skill Name: Facial action units and basic expressions
hx-hri-facial-action-units.Skill Description: Facial action units and basic expressions — Describe expressions in terms of facial action units for brows, lids and mouth, and identify which few features carry most of the emotional signal for a simplified robot face.

hx-hri-gaze-functions.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-gaze-functions.Skill Description: Functions of gaze in interaction — Explain how gaze signals attention, regulates turn-taking, expresses intimacy through mutual gaze, and uses aversion while thinking, with typical durations from human studies.

hx-hri-uncanny-valley.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-uncanny-valley.Skill Description: Uncanny valley effect — Explain the uncanny valley hypothesis, the evidence for and against it, and how mismatched realism between face, motion and voice produces discomfort.

hx-hri-proxemic-zones.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-proxemic-zones.Skill Description: Proxemic zones and personal space — Describe intimate, personal, social and public distance zones, how culture, age and context shift them, and why a robot should treat them as soft constraints.

hx-hri-emotion-models.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-emotion-models.Prerequisite Names: Facial action units and basic expressions
hx-hri-emotion-models.Skill Description: Emotion models for robot expression — Compare categorical emotion sets with dimensional models such as valence-arousal and pleasure-arousal-dominance, and choose one suited to driving robot expression.

hx-hri-gesture-taxonomy.Subject: Gestures and nonverbal behavior
hx-hri-gesture-taxonomy.Skill Description: Types of nonverbal gestures — Classify gestures as deictic, iconic, metaphoric, beat or emblem, and describe what each contributes to spoken communication and how culture changes emblem meanings.

hx-hri-stylized-design.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-stylized-design.Skill Description: Stylized versus realistic humanoid design — Choose a stylized or realistic appearance for a humanoid head and body, justifying the choice by cost, uncanny risk, expressiveness and the robot's intended role.

hx-hri-trust-calibration.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-trust-calibration.Prerequisite Names: Users' mental models of robots; Identify hazards and protective functions
hx-hri-trust-calibration.Skill Description: Trust and trust calibration — Distinguish overtrust, undertrust and calibrated trust, list the robot behaviors and failures that shift trust, and propose measures that keep user trust matched to reliability.

hx-hri-height-posture.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-height-posture.Skill Name: Robot height, posture and perceived dominance
hx-hri-height-posture.Skill Description: Robot height, posture and perceived dominance — Explain how robot height and posture affect perceived dominance and comfort, and adjust torso height or lean to meet seated people and children at eye level.

hx-hri-expectation-setting.Subject: HRI foundations
hx-hri-expectation-setting.Skill Description: Matching appearance to capability — Identify the expectation gap created when a robot looks or sounds more capable than it is, and adjust form, voice and wording to keep expectations accurate.

hx-hri-character-bible.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-character-bible.Skill Description: Write a robot character bible — Write a character specification for the robot covering role, traits, values, speech style, humor limits and taboo topics, consistent with its capabilities and appearance.

hx-hri-politeness-strategies.Subject: Etiquette and protocol
hx-hri-politeness-strategies.Skill Description: Politeness strategies for robots — Apply politeness theory to phrase robot requests, refusals and corrections with suitable directness, hedging and deference for the relationship and situation.

hx-hri-affect-state.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-affect-state.Skill Name: Implement an affect state with decay
hx-hri-affect-state.Prerequisite Names: Emotion models for robot expression; Finite-state machines for robot behaviour; Exponential models
hx-hri-affect-state.Skill Description: Implement an affect state with decay — Implement an internal affect state that events push in valence-arousal space and that decays exponentially toward a neutral baseline, with bounded and testable outputs.

hx-hri-forms-of-address.Subject: Etiquette and protocol
hx-hri-forms-of-address.Skill Description: Formal address, titles and honorifics — Address people with correct titles, honorifics and name order across languages, ask for preferred names, and switch formality appropriately as a relationship develops.

hx-hri-greetings-across-cultures.Subject: Etiquette and protocol
hx-hri-greetings-across-cultures.Prerequisite Names: Types of nonverbal gestures; Politeness strategies for robots
hx-hri-greetings-across-cultures.Skill Description: Greetings and gestures across cultures — Describe greeting customs (bow, wave, handshake, verbal forms) and gesture meanings across major cultures, and choose robot greetings that avoid offense or unwanted touch.

hx-hri-study-design.Subject: Evaluation and user studies
hx-hri-study-design.Prerequisite Names: Scope of human-robot interaction; Sampling and bias; Hypothesis tests and error types
hx-hri-study-design.Skill Description: Design an HRI user study — Design a within- or between-subjects study with a hypothesis, conditions, counterbalancing, sample size reasoning and informed-consent procedure for testing a robot behavior.

hx-hri-data-minimization.Subject: Privacy and consent
hx-hri-data-minimization.Prerequisite Names: Scope of human-robot interaction; Logging and recorded data
hx-hri-data-minimization.Skill Description: Interaction data handling and minimization — Decide what audio, video, transcripts and face data to keep, process on-device where possible, set retention limits, and document who can access stored data.

hx-hri-introductions.Subject: Etiquette and protocol
hx-hri-introductions.Skill Description: Perform introductions between people — Introduce people to each other following protocol on order, names, titles and context, and introduce the robot itself with an honest statement of its role.

hx-hri-ab-test-behavior.Subject: Evaluation and user studies
hx-hri-ab-test-behavior.Prerequisite Names: Logging and recorded data; Hypothesis tests and error types; Design an HRI user study
hx-hri-ab-test-behavior.Skill Description: A/B test an interaction behavior — Run an A/B comparison of two robot behaviors on a logged outcome such as task success or engagement time, and test whether the difference is statistically meaningful.

hx-hri-godspeed-scoring.Subject: Evaluation and user studies
hx-hri-godspeed-scoring.Prerequisite Names: Mean, median, and mode; Sample variance and standard deviation; Design an HRI user study
hx-hri-godspeed-scoring.Skill Description: Score the Godspeed questionnaire — Administer the Godspeed series (anthropomorphism, animacy, likeability, intelligence, safety), compute subscale scores and internal consistency, and compare conditions.

hx-hri-animation-principles.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-animation-principles.Prerequisite Names: Anthropomorphism and social attribution; Generate bounded joint trajectories
hx-hri-animation-principles.Skill Description: Animation principles for robots — Explain the classic animation principles (timing, anticipation, slow-in and slow-out, follow-through, arcs, exaggeration) and how each applies to a physical robot with joint limits.

hx-hri-easing-curves.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-easing-curves.Prerequisite Names: Polynomial arithmetic; Animation principles for robots; Derivative as local rate
hx-hri-easing-curves.Skill Description: Easing curves and slow-in/slow-out — Implement ease-in, ease-out and minimum-jerk easing functions for a joint move, and compare their velocity and acceleration profiles against a linear interpolation.

hx-hri-legible-motion.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-legible-motion.Prerequisite Names: Users' mental models of robots; Generate smooth joint trajectories
hx-hri-legible-motion.Skill Description: Legible and predictable robot motion — Distinguish predictable motion from legible motion, and shape arm and base trajectories so observers can infer the robot's goal early, trading efficiency against readability.

hx-hri-motion-timing.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-motion-timing.Skill Name: Timing and speed to convey intent
hx-hri-motion-timing.Skill Description: Timing and speed to convey intent — Choose motion speed, pauses and hold times so a gesture reads as calm, urgent, hesitant or confident, and verify the intended impression with observers.

hx-hri-anticipation.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-anticipation.Prerequisite Names: Legible and predictable robot motion; Timing and speed to convey intent
hx-hri-anticipation.Skill Description: Anticipation before robot actions — Add a short preparatory motion or gaze shift before a main action so observers can foresee what the robot will do, without violating workspace or safety limits.

hx-hri-follow-through-secondary.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-follow-through-secondary.Prerequisite Names: Timing and speed to convey intent
hx-hri-follow-through-secondary.Skill Description: Follow-through and secondary motion — Add follow-through, overlapping action and subtle secondary or idle motion (settling, breathing sway) so a robot appears alive without distracting jitter.

hx-hri-approach-direction.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-approach-direction.Prerequisite Names: Proxemic zones and personal space; Legible and predictable robot motion
hx-hri-approach-direction.Skill Description: Approach direction and speed — Choose an approach path that keeps the robot visible, arrives from a front-oblique angle, and slows smoothly when entering a person's social zone.

hx-hri-checkpoint-s3.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-hri-checkpoint-s3.Skill Description: Human-Robot Interaction checkpoint: stage 3 (robot arm) — Demonstrate the 1 end-of-branch human-robot interaction skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 3 integration milestone.

hx-hri-keyframe-animation.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-keyframe-animation.Prerequisite Names: Generate smooth joint trajectories; Easing curves and slow-in/slow-out; Write a URDF robot description
hx-hri-keyframe-animation.Skill Description: Keyframe a robot joint animation — Define keyframes for several joints, interpolate between them with easing, and play the result back as a time-stamped joint trajectory on a simulated robot.

hx-hri-wizard-of-oz.Subject: Evaluation and user studies
hx-hri-wizard-of-oz.Prerequisite Names: Design an HRI user study; Write a ROS 2 publisher and subscriber
hx-hri-wizard-of-oz.Skill Description: Wizard-of-Oz prototyping — Run a Wizard-of-Oz session where a hidden operator drives robot speech or motion, so interaction designs can be tested before autonomy exists, and disclose it appropriately.

hx-hri-animation-tool-export.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-animation-tool-export.Skill Name: Author robot animations in a 3D tool
hx-hri-animation-tool-export.Skill Description: Author robot animations in a 3D tool — Rig a robot model from its URDF in a 3D animation tool such as Blender, keyframe a gesture, and export it as joint trajectories the robot can play.

hx-hri-gesture-library.Subject: Gestures and nonverbal behavior
hx-hri-gesture-library.Prerequisite Names: Types of nonverbal gestures; Author robot animations in a 3D tool
hx-hri-gesture-library.Skill Description: Build a parameterized gesture library — Author a set of reusable gestures (wave, bow, shrug, open palm, nod) with parameters for amplitude, speed and handedness that can be triggered by name.

hx-hri-observation-coding.Subject: Evaluation and user studies
hx-hri-observation-coding.Prerequisite Names: Conditional probability and independence; Design an HRI user study; Record and replay robot data with rosbag
hx-hri-observation-coding.Skill Description: Code observed interactions from video — Build a coding scheme for observed interaction events, annotate recorded sessions with two raters, and compute inter-rater agreement such as Cohen's kappa.

hx-hri-status-signals.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-status-signals.Skill Name: Signal robot state with light and sound
hx-hri-status-signals.Prerequisite Names: Users' mental models of robots; LED current limiting
hx-hri-status-signals.Skill Description: Signal robot state with light and sound — Design consistent light, sound and on-screen cues for states such as idle, listening, thinking, moving and fault, so users can read the robot's state at a glance.

hx-hri-accessibility-principles.Subject: Accessibility
hx-hri-accessibility-principles.Prerequisite Names: Signal robot state with light and sound
hx-hri-accessibility-principles.Skill Description: Accessible interaction design principles — Apply inclusive design for hearing, vision, motor and cognitive differences, providing redundant output channels and alternative inputs such as touch or buttons.

hx-hri-privacy-indicators.Subject: Privacy and consent
hx-hri-privacy-indicators.Prerequisite Names: Configure microcontroller GPIO; Signal robot state with light and sound
hx-hri-privacy-indicators.Skill Description: Hardware camera and microphone indicators — Wire camera and microphone status lights so they are driven by sensor power and cannot be disabled in software, and add physical mute switches or shutters.

hx-hri-animatronic-eyes.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-animatronic-eyes.Prerequisite Names: Stylized versus realistic humanoid design; Design and print functional parts with tolerances; Command and read a smart serial bus servo
hx-hri-animatronic-eyes.Skill Description: Build an animatronic eye mechanism — Design and assemble a servo-driven eye mechanism with pan, tilt and eyelids, choosing linkages and servos for range, speed and quiet operation.

hx-hri-screen-face.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-screen-face.Skill Name: Design and render an animated screen face
hx-hri-screen-face.Prerequisite Names: Facial action units and basic expressions; Stylized versus realistic humanoid design; Easing curves and slow-in/slow-out; Luminance of displays and surfaces; PWM dimming, flicker and perceived brightness
hx-hri-screen-face.Skill Description: Design and render an animated screen face — Design a stylized screen face with parameterized eyes, brows and mouth, and render it at a steady frame rate with smooth eased transitions between poses.

hx-hri-led-eyes.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-led-eyes.Prerequisite Codes: HRI-HRF-005, PHY-LSD-002, ELX-SAC-012, EMB-TIP-002, PHY-LSD-003, PHY-LSD-007, PHY-LSD-006
hx-hri-led-eyes.Prerequisite Names: Stylized versus realistic humanoid design; How LEDs emit light: bandgap and wavelength; LED current limiting; Generate PWM with hardware timers; LED efficacy, droop and junction heating; PWM dimming, flicker and perceived brightness; Diffusing LED light without hot spots
hx-hri-led-eyes.Skill Description: Drive LED eyes — Build LED-matrix or addressable-LED eyes and drive them from a microcontroller with brightness, color and shape patterns for blinking, looking and simple emotions.

hx-hri-blink-eyelid-brow.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-blink-eyelid-brow.Prerequisite Names: Random variables and distributions; Design and render an animated screen face
hx-hri-blink-eyelid-brow.Skill Description: Blink, eyelid and brow behavior — Generate natural blink timing from a random-interval model, link blinks to gaze shifts, and use lid and brow positions to express attention, surprise and concern.

hx-hri-look-at-target.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-look-at-target.Skill Name: Compute head pan and tilt to look at a point
hx-hri-look-at-target.Prerequisite Names: Inverse trigonometry and quadrants; Broadcast and look up transforms with tf2; Forward kinematics of a serial arm with transforms
hx-hri-look-at-target.Skill Description: Compute head pan and tilt to look at a point — Transform a 3D target point into the head frame and compute pan and tilt angles, respecting neck joint limits, so the robot's face points at the target.

hx-hri-eye-head-coordination.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-eye-head-coordination.Prerequisite Names: Easing curves and slow-in/slow-out; Compute head pan and tilt to look at a point
hx-hri-eye-head-coordination.Skill Description: Eye-head coordination — Coordinate fast eye movements with slower head turns so gaze lands quickly on a target and the head follows, keeping eyes centered and motion natural.

hx-hri-voice-design.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-voice-design.Skill Name: Select and tune a robot voice
hx-hri-voice-design.Prerequisite Names: Write a robot character bible; Moving-coil loudspeaker principles; Inverse-square spreading of sound; Loudspeaker sensitivity and required amplifier power; Text-to-speech synthesis
hx-hri-voice-design.Skill Description: Select and tune a robot voice — Select a text-to-speech voice and tune rate, pitch and prosody so the voice fits the character, stays intelligible in noise, and matches the robot's apparent size and age.

hx-hri-lip-sync-visemes.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-lip-sync-visemes.Prerequisite Names: Timestamps and clock synchronization; Design and render an animated screen face; Text-to-speech synthesis
hx-hri-lip-sync-visemes.Skill Description: Mouth sync with visemes — Map phonemes to visemes and drive mouth shapes from text-to-speech timing or audio amplitude, keeping lip motion aligned with speech audio within perceptual tolerance.

hx-hri-live-captions.Subject: Accessibility
hx-hri-live-captions.Skill Name: Live captions and visual speech feedback
hx-hri-live-captions.Prerequisite Names: Accessible interaction design principles; Speech-to-text transcription
hx-hri-live-captions.Skill Description: Live captions and visual speech feedback — Display live captions of what the robot says and what it heard, so users can verify recognition and follow speech in noisy places or with hearing loss.

hx-hri-engagement-detection.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-engagement-detection.Prerequisite Names: Proxemic zones and personal space; Classification and decision thresholds; Detect and track people and faces
hx-hri-engagement-detection.Skill Description: Detect user engagement — Estimate whether a person intends to interact from distance, approach trajectory, face orientation and dwell time, and output a calibrated engagement score.

hx-hri-expressive-face.Subject: Facial expression
hx-hri-expressive-face.Prerequisite Names: Implement an affect state with decay; Luminance of displays and surfaces; Diffusing LED light without hot spots; Blink, eyelid and brow behavior; Mouth sync with visemes
hx-hri-expressive-face.Skill Description: Expressive face display — Integrate affect-driven expressions, blinks, gaze and lip sync into one face controller that blends layers cleanly and stays readable during speech and motion.

hx-hri-gaze-behavior.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-gaze-behavior.Prerequisite Names: Functions of gaze in interaction; Eye-head coordination; Detect and track people and faces
hx-hri-gaze-behavior.Skill Description: Gaze and head-turn behavior — Implement a gaze controller that tracks the person being addressed, holds mutual gaze, averts appropriately, and shifts attention with head motion timed to look intentional.

hx-hri-pointing-gesture.Subject: Gestures and nonverbal behavior
hx-hri-pointing-gesture.Prerequisite Names: Types of nonverbal gestures; Compute head pan and tilt to look at a point; Numerical inverse kinematics
hx-hri-pointing-gesture.Skill Description: Generate a deictic pointing gesture — Compute an arm pose that points a finger or hand at a target object or location, coordinated with gaze, and check that observers identify the intended target.

hx-hri-group-formations.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-group-formations.Prerequisite Names: Proxemic zones and personal space; Detect and track people and faces
hx-hri-group-formations.Skill Description: F-formations and joining groups — Detect conversational group formations from people's positions and orientations, and choose where to stand to join or address a group without breaking its shared space.

hx-hri-failure-types.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-failure-types.Prerequisite Names: Trust and trust calibration; Speech-to-text transcription
hx-hri-failure-types.Skill Description: Types of interaction failure — Classify interaction breakdowns such as misrecognition, misunderstanding, unmet expectation and task failure, and identify the cues that reveal each during a conversation.

hx-hri-persona.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-persona.Prerequisite Names: Select and tune a robot voice; Prompt and configure a large language model
hx-hri-persona.Skill Description: Voice and personality design — Implement the robot's persona as a language-model system prompt, voice settings and expression defaults, and verify replies stay in character across typical requests.

hx-hri-joint-attention.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-joint-attention.Prerequisite Names: Detect objects with a neural network detector; Gaze and head-turn behavior
hx-hri-joint-attention.Skill Description: Joint attention and gaze following — Follow a person's gaze or pointing to the object they mean, look at it to confirm shared reference, and look back to the person to check understanding.

hx-hri-look-at-speaker.Subject: Gaze and head motion
hx-hri-look-at-speaker.Prerequisite Names: Microphone array capture and sound localization; Gaze and head-turn behavior
hx-hri-look-at-speaker.Skill Description: Orient toward the active speaker — Fuse sound direction from a microphone array with tracked faces to decide who is speaking and turn the head toward them, with hysteresis to avoid flicking.

hx-hri-trust-repair.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-trust-repair.Skill Name: Apology and trust repair after errors
hx-hri-trust-repair.Skill Description: Apology and trust repair after errors — Choose apology, explanation and corrective-action strategies after a robot mistake, and evaluate how each affects user trust and willingness to continue.

hx-hri-plain-language.Subject: Accessibility
hx-hri-plain-language.Prerequisite Names: Accessible interaction design principles; Voice and personality design
hx-hri-plain-language.Skill Description: Plain language and adjustable speech — Rewrite robot utterances in plain language, short sentences and concrete words, and let users slow speech, repeat or simplify replies on request.

hx-hri-character-consistency.Subject: Emotion and persona
hx-hri-character-consistency.Prerequisite Names: Expressive face display; Voice and personality design
hx-hri-character-consistency.Skill Description: Test consistent character across modalities — Build a test set of prompts and situations, and check that words, voice, face and gesture express the same persona and emotion without contradiction over long sessions.

hx-hri-etiquette-profile.Subject: Etiquette and protocol
hx-hri-etiquette-profile.Prerequisite Names: Greetings and gestures across cultures; Perform introductions between people; Voice and personality design
hx-hri-etiquette-profile.Skill Description: Implement configurable etiquette profiles — Encode cultural and situational etiquette rules (greeting form, address, distance, formality) as configurable profiles that the dialogue and behavior layers consult.

hx-hri-child-interaction.Subject: Special populations
hx-hri-child-interaction.Prerequisite Names: Robot height, posture and perceived dominance; Interaction data handling and minimization; Plain language and adjustable speech
hx-hri-child-interaction.Skill Description: Interaction considerations for children — Adapt robot speech, height, pacing and content for children, and apply safeguards against deception, over-attachment, data collection and unsupervised physical contact.

hx-hri-explain-intent.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-explain-intent.Prerequisite Names: Legible and predictable robot motion; LLM tool calling to robot skills
hx-hri-explain-intent.Skill Description: Announce and explain robot intentions — Generate short spoken announcements of what the robot is about to do and why, timed before motion, using the planned action from the tool-calling layer.

hx-hri-explain-limits.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-explain-limits.Prerequisite Names: Matching appearance to capability; Announce and explain robot intentions
hx-hri-explain-limits.Skill Description: Communicate capability limits and uncertainty — Tell users clearly what the robot cannot do or is unsure about, offer alternatives, and avoid overstating competence in ways that would miscalibrate trust.

hx-hri-animation-limit-check.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-animation-limit-check.Prerequisite Names: Keyframe a robot joint animation; Size an actuator from joint load, speed and duty cycle
hx-hri-animation-limit-check.Skill Description: Check animations against joint limits — Check an authored animation for position, velocity, acceleration and torque limit violations, then retime or rescale it so the physical robot can execute it safely.

hx-hri-animation-blending.Subject: Legible motion and animation
hx-hri-animation-blending.Prerequisite Names: Follow-through and secondary motion; Write a ROS 2 publisher and subscriber; Check animations against joint limits
hx-hri-animation-blending.Skill Description: Blend animations with live control — Crossfade between animation clips and layer additive gestures over live control targets such as look-at or base motion, avoiding discontinuities at transitions.

hx-hri-beat-gesture-sync.Subject: Gestures and nonverbal behavior
hx-hri-beat-gesture-sync.Prerequisite Names: Build a parameterized gesture library; Text-to-speech synthesis; Blend animations with live control
hx-hri-beat-gesture-sync.Skill Description: Synchronize beat gestures with speech — Use word or phoneme timings from text-to-speech to place gesture strokes on stressed syllables, compensating for actuator latency so motion lands on time.

hx-hri-behavior-arbitration.Subject: Interaction integration
hx-hri-behavior-arbitration.Prerequisite Names: Implement a robot behavior state machine; Blend animations with live control
hx-hri-behavior-arbitration.Skill Description: Arbitrate behaviors across modalities — Arbitrate competing requests for head, arms, face and voice by priority and resource locking, so safety, conversation and idle behaviors never fight over the same joints.

hx-hri-speech-behavior-markup.Subject: Gestures and nonverbal behavior
hx-hri-speech-behavior-markup.Prerequisite Names: Prompt and configure a large language model; Synchronize beat gestures with speech
hx-hri-speech-behavior-markup.Skill Description: Plan co-speech behavior with markup — Annotate generated utterances with behavior tags for gestures, gaze shifts and expressions, and schedule them against speech timing using a behavior markup scheme.

hx-hri-closing-interaction.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-closing-interaction.Prerequisite Names: Detect user engagement; Dialogue management and turn-taking
hx-hri-closing-interaction.Skill Description: End interactions gracefully — Recognize pre-closing cues and disengagement, summarize or confirm outcomes, offer a farewell, and release attention without abruptly turning away.

hx-hri-turn-taking-cues.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-turn-taking-cues.Prerequisite Names: Gaze and head-turn behavior; Dialogue management and turn-taking
hx-hri-turn-taking-cues.Skill Description: Multimodal turn-taking cues — Signal holding or yielding the floor with gaze, pauses, prosody and gesture, and mask processing delays with brief thinking cues so users know when to speak.

hx-hri-consent-flows.Subject: Privacy and consent
hx-hri-consent-flows.Prerequisite Names: Interaction data handling and minimization; Dialogue management and turn-taking
hx-hri-consent-flows.Skill Description: Obtain consent in conversation — Ask for, record and honor consent for recording, face enrollment or remembering personal details within a dialogue, including easy withdrawal and deletion.

hx-hri-clarification.Subject: Transparency and error repair
hx-hri-clarification.Prerequisite Names: Expectation and variance; Types of interaction failure; Dialogue management and turn-taking
hx-hri-clarification.Skill Description: Ask for clarification and confirm — Choose between acting, implicit confirmation, explicit confirmation and clarification questions based on recognition confidence and the cost of a wrong action.

hx-hri-backchannel.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-backchannel.Skill Description: Backchannel while listening — Produce nods and short vocalizations at pauses while the user speaks, timed from voice activity and prosody, so the user feels heard without being interrupted.

hx-hri-barge-in.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-barge-in.Skill Description: Handle user interruptions — Detect when a user speaks over the robot, stop or pause speech and gesture within a short latency, and resume or replan the reply appropriately.

hx-hri-multiparty.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-multiparty.Prerequisite Names: F-formations and joining groups; Orient toward the active speaker; Multimodal turn-taking cues
hx-hri-multiparty.Skill Description: Multi-party conversation and addressee selection — Track several participants, decide who is addressing the robot and whom to address, and distribute gaze and turns fairly in a group conversation.

hx-hri-handover-cues.Subject: Safety-related social behavior
hx-hri-handover-cues.Prerequisite Names: Legible and predictable robot motion; Gaze and head-turn behavior; Vision-guided pick-and-place
hx-hri-handover-cues.Skill Description: Social cues for object handover — Use reach posture, gaze to the hand and object, and timed release so a person knows when and where to take an object handed over by the robot.

hx-hri-speed-separation.Subject: Safety-related social behavior
hx-hri-speed-separation.Prerequisite Names: Proxemic zones and personal space; Kinetic energy and work-energy balance; Robot risk assessment
hx-hri-speed-separation.Skill Description: Speed and separation near people — Compute speed limits from separation distance and allowable contact energy, using power-and-force-limiting concepts, and slow or stop the robot as a person approaches.

hx-hri-warning-signals.Subject: Safety-related social behavior
hx-hri-warning-signals.Prerequisite Names: Signal robot state with light and sound; Robot risk assessment
hx-hri-warning-signals.Skill Description: Warning signals before motion — Precede potentially hazardous motion with audible and visual warnings and verbal notice, timed and scaled to the hazard identified in the risk assessment.

hx-hri-stop-on-touch.Subject: Safety-related social behavior
hx-hri-stop-on-touch.Prerequisite Names: Design an emergency stop and safe power-off circuit; Impedance control; Warning signals before motion
hx-hri-stop-on-touch.Skill Description: Stop or comply when touched — Detect unexpected contact from torque residuals or touch sensors and respond within a bounded time by stopping or becoming compliant, then explain what happened.

hx-hri-checkpoint-s5.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-hri-checkpoint-s5.Skill Description: Human-Robot Interaction checkpoint: stage 5 (mobile manipulator) — Demonstrate the 1 end-of-branch human-robot interaction skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 5 integration milestone.

hx-hri-safe-refusal.Subject: Safety-related social behavior
hx-hri-safe-refusal.Prerequisite Names: Politeness strategies for robots; Communicate capability limits and uncertainty; Guardrails on AI-commanded robot actions
hx-hri-safe-refusal.Skill Description: Politely refuse unsafe requests — Decline commands blocked by safety or policy guardrails with a polite explanation and a safe alternative, without arguing, lecturing or revealing exploitable details.

hx-hri-proxemics.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-proxemics.Prerequisite Names: Approach direction and speed; Detect and track people and faces; Autonomous navigation with Nav2
hx-hri-proxemics.Skill Description: Proxemics and approach behavior — Compute a goal pose near a tracked person from their position and facing, at a chosen social distance and angle, and drive the base there with proxemic speed limits.

hx-hri-mobility-aware.Subject: Accessibility
hx-hri-mobility-aware.Prerequisite Names: Robot height, posture and perceived dominance; Accessible interaction design principles; Proxemics and approach behavior
hx-hri-mobility-aware.Skill Description: Mobility-aware interaction — Adapt approach, height, reach and handover positions for wheelchair users and people with limited mobility, keeping interaction points within comfortable reach.

hx-hri-greeting-behavior.Subject: Engagement and conversation management
hx-hri-greeting-behavior.Prerequisite Names: Detect user engagement; Gaze and head-turn behavior; Proxemics and approach behavior
hx-hri-greeting-behavior.Skill Description: Initiate interaction with a greeting — Trigger a greeting when engagement is likely, using gaze, a gesture and a short utterance at the right distance, and back off gracefully if the person is not interested.

hx-hri-social-costmap.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-social-costmap.Prerequisite Names: Normal distributions and standard scores; Proxemics and approach behavior
hx-hri-social-costmap.Skill Description: Social costmap layer around people — Add a costmap layer that places asymmetric Gaussian costs around tracked people, larger in front than behind, so the planner keeps socially comfortable clearance.

hx-hri-social-navigation.Subject: Proxemics and social navigation
hx-hri-social-navigation.Prerequisite Names: F-formations and joining groups; Social costmap layer around people
hx-hri-social-navigation.Skill Description: Navigate socially among people — Navigate through spaces with moving people by passing on the expected side, yielding at doorways, not cutting through conversing groups, and signaling intent early.

hx-hri-elder-interaction.Subject: Special populations
hx-hri-elder-interaction.Prerequisite Names: Plain language and adjustable speech; Mobility-aware interaction
hx-hri-elder-interaction.Skill Description: Interaction considerations for older adults — Adapt for hearing and vision changes, slower pacing, mobility aids and possible cognitive decline, while respecting dignity and avoiding patronizing or deceptive behavior.

hx-hri-checkpoint-s4.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-hri-checkpoint-s4.Prerequisite Names: Hardware camera and microphone indicators; Speed and separation near people; Navigate socially among people
hx-hri-checkpoint-s4.Skill Description: Human-Robot Interaction checkpoint: stage 4 (wheeled base) — Demonstrate the 3 end-of-branch human-robot interaction skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 4 integration milestone.

hx-hri-interaction-loop.Subject: Interaction integration
hx-hri-interaction-loop.Skill Name: Full spoken interaction loop with gesture and gaze
hx-hri-interaction-loop.Prerequisite Codes: HRI-FAE-007, HRI-INI-001, SYS-TSB-008, HRI-GNB-005, HRI-TER-006, HRI-ECM-003, SYS-ADP-012
hx-hri-interaction-loop.Prerequisite Names: Expressive face display; Arbitrate behaviors across modalities; Mass, power, compute and latency budgets; Plan co-speech behavior with markup; Ask for clarification and confirm; Multimodal turn-taking cues; Design a human-facing robot interaction
hx-hri-interaction-loop.Skill Description: Full spoken interaction loop with gesture and gaze — Integrate listening, dialogue, speech, gaze, face and co-speech gesture into one real-time loop with turn-taking, repair and latency budgets measured end to end.

hx-hri-field-evaluation.Subject: Interaction integration
hx-hri-field-evaluation.Prerequisite Names: Score the Godspeed questionnaire; Code observed interactions from video; Full spoken interaction loop with gesture and gaze
hx-hri-field-evaluation.Skill Description: Evaluate a deployed protocol droid — Run an in-the-wild evaluation of the integrated robot with logged interactions, observation coding and questionnaires, and turn findings into prioritized design changes.

hx-hri-checkpoint-s6.Subject: Checkpoints
hx-hri-checkpoint-s6.Skill Name: Human-Robot Interaction checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid)
hx-hri-checkpoint-s6.Prerequisite Codes: HRI-EUS-002, HRI-EUS-004, HRI-FAE-002, HRI-FAE-004, HRI-ACC-002, HRI-GNB-003, HRI-GHM-005, HRI-TER-003, HRI-EMP-006, HRI-ETP-005, HRI-SPP-001, HRI-ECM-002, HRI-PRC-003, HRI-ECM-004, HRI-ECM-005, HRI-ECM-006, HRI-SRS-001, HRI-SRS-005, HRI-ECM-007, HRI-SPP-002, HRI-INI-003
hx-hri-checkpoint-s6.Prerequisite Names: A/B test an interaction behavior; Wizard-of-Oz prototyping; Build an animatronic eye mechanism; Drive LED eyes; Live captions and visual speech feedback; Generate a deictic pointing gesture; Joint attention and gaze following; Apology and trust repair after errors; Test consistent character across modalities; Implement configurable etiquette profiles; Interaction considerations for children; End interactions gracefully; Obtain consent in conversation; Backchannel while listening; Handle user interruptions; Multi-party conversation and addressee selection; Social cues for object handover; Politely refuse unsafe requests; Initiate interaction with a greeting; Interaction considerations for older adults; Evaluate a deployed protocol droid
hx-hri-checkpoint-s6.Skill Description: Human-Robot Interaction checkpoint: stage 6 (humanoid protocol droid) — Demonstrate the 21 end-of-branch human-robot interaction skills this checkpoint gathers, as a combined review before the stage 6 integration milestone.

rob3:B-S01.Subject: Systems practice
rob3:B-S01.Skill Name: Describe an observable task and its limits
rob3:B-S01.Skill Description: Describe an observable task and its limits — Describe an observable task and its limits

hx-sys-stakeholder-needs.Subject: Requirements engineering
hx-sys-stakeholder-needs.Skill Name: Elicit stakeholder needs for a protocol droid
hx-sys-stakeholder-needs.Prerequisite Names: Describe an observable task and its limits
hx-sys-stakeholder-needs.Skill Description: Elicit stakeholder needs for a protocol droid — Interview users, owners and bystanders to list what a helpful talking humanoid must do, and record each need with its source and priority.

rob3:B-S02.Subject: Systems practice
rob3:B-S02.Skill Name: Recognize hazards and seek appropriate controls
rob3:B-S02.Prerequisite Names: Describe an observable task and its limits
rob3:B-S02.Skill Description: Recognize hazards and seek appropriate controls — Recognize hazards and seek appropriate controls

hx-sys-conops.Subject: Concept of operations
hx-sys-conops.Skill Name: Write a concept of operations for a protocol droid
hx-sys-conops.Prerequisite Names: Elicit stakeholder needs for a protocol droid
hx-sys-conops.Skill Description: Write a concept of operations for a protocol droid — Describe who uses the droid, where, when and how, including a typical day, staffing, charging and failure handling, as a narrative that anchors all requirements.

hx-sys-build-log.Subject: Documentation
hx-sys-build-log.Skill Description: Keep an engineering build log — Keep dated build-log entries recording what was built, measured, changed and observed, with photos and values, so work can be reproduced and debugged.

hx-sys-operating-environment.Subject: Concept of operations
hx-sys-operating-environment.Skill Name: Specify the operating environment and design envelope
hx-sys-operating-environment.Prerequisite Names: Physical quantities and SI units; Write a concept of operations for a protocol droid
hx-sys-operating-environment.Skill Description: Specify the operating environment and design envelope — Specify floor types, slopes, lighting, ambient noise, crowd density, temperature and network availability the droid must tolerate, with quantified bounds.

hx-sys-use-cases.Subject: Concept of operations
hx-sys-use-cases.Skill Name: Write use cases and operational scenarios
hx-sys-use-cases.Prerequisite Names: Write a concept of operations for a protocol droid
hx-sys-use-cases.Skill Description: Write use cases and operational scenarios — Write use cases with actors, preconditions, main flow, alternate flows and failure flows for tasks such as greeting a visitor or fetching an item.

hx-sys-issue-tracking.Subject: Diagnosis and debugging
hx-sys-issue-tracking.Skill Name: Track issues with severity and closure
hx-sys-issue-tracking.Skill Description: Track issues with severity and closure — Log defects with reproduction steps, severity, owner and status, and close them only with evidence that the fix was verified.

rob3:Q01.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q01.Prerequisite Names: Describe an observable task and its limits; Physical quantities and SI units; Systems, assumptions, and models
rob3:Q01.Skill Description: Write measurable robot requirements — Write measurable robot requirements

hx-sys-need-to-requirement.Subject: Requirements engineering
hx-sys-need-to-requirement.Prerequisite Names: Elicit stakeholder needs for a protocol droid; Write measurable robot requirements
hx-sys-need-to-requirement.Skill Description: Translate needs into shall statements — Rewrite a vague stakeholder need such as 'greets visitors politely' into one or more singular shall statements with a subject, action and condition.

rob3:Q03.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q03.Prerequisite Names: Recognize hazards and seek appropriate controls; Write measurable robot requirements
rob3:Q03.Skill Description: Identify hazards and protective functions — Identify hazards and protective functions

rob3:Q05.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q05.Prerequisite Names: Record a reproducible procedure; Write measurable robot requirements
rob3:Q05.Skill Description: Plan traceable verification — Plan traceable verification

hx-sys-functional-decomposition.Subject: System architecture and interfaces
hx-sys-functional-decomposition.Skill Name: Decompose robot functions into a function tree
hx-sys-functional-decomposition.Prerequisite Names: Write use cases and operational scenarios; Trees and spanning trees
hx-sys-functional-decomposition.Skill Description: Decompose robot functions into a function tree — Break the top-level mission into a hierarchy of functions such as perceive, decide, move, manipulate and communicate down to testable leaf functions.

hx-sys-hazard-identification.Subject: Safety engineering
hx-sys-hazard-identification.Prerequisite Names: Write use cases and operational scenarios; Identify hazards and protective functions
hx-sys-hazard-identification.Skill Description: Identify robot hazards systematically — Identify mechanical, electrical, thermal, behavioral and environmental hazards across every use case and lifecycle phase from assembly to disposal.

rob3:Q04.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q04.Prerequisite Names: Write measurable robot requirements; Ratios and unit rates
rob3:Q04.Skill Description: Allocate system budgets — Allocate system budgets

hx-sys-risk-matrix.Subject: Safety engineering
hx-sys-risk-matrix.Skill Name: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix
hx-sys-risk-matrix.Prerequisite Names: Probability rules; Identify robot hazards systematically
hx-sys-risk-matrix.Skill Description: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix — Rate each hazard's severity and likelihood on defined scales, place it on a risk matrix, and decide whether the risk is acceptable.

hx-sys-standards-landscape.Subject: Safety standards awareness
hx-sys-standards-landscape.Skill Name: Navigate type A, B and C safety standards
hx-sys-standards-landscape.Skill Description: Navigate type A, B and C safety standards — Explain how basic, group and product safety standards relate and locate which ones apply to a service humanoid robot.

hx-sys-requirements.Subject: Requirements engineering
hx-sys-requirements.Prerequisite Names: Translate needs into shall statements; Measurement uncertainty
hx-sys-requirements.Skill Description: Write measurable robot requirements — Write humanoid requirements with numeric thresholds, units, tolerances and test conditions, such as response latency, reach envelope or payload, so that pass or fail is unambiguous.

rob3:Q02.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q02.Prerequisite Names: Write measurable robot requirements; Unit conversions
rob3:Q02.Skill Description: Define subsystem interfaces — Define subsystem interfaces

hx-sys-risk-reduction-hierarchy.Subject: Safety engineering
hx-sys-risk-reduction-hierarchy.Prerequisite Names: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix
hx-sys-risk-reduction-hierarchy.Skill Description: Apply the risk reduction hierarchy — Reduce risk in priority order: inherently safe design, then safeguards and protective devices, then warnings and training, and justify each choice.

hx-sys-iso-12100.Subject: Safety standards awareness
hx-sys-iso-12100.Prerequisite Names: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix; Navigate type A, B and C safety standards
hx-sys-iso-12100.Skill Description: ISO 12100 risk assessment process — Apply the ISO 12100 sequence of determining limits, identifying hazards, estimating and evaluating risk, and reducing it iteratively, for a robot.

hx-sys-operating-modes.Subject: Concept of operations
hx-sys-operating-modes.Skill Name: Define robot operating modes and transitions
hx-sys-operating-modes.Prerequisite Names: Write use cases and operational scenarios; Finite-state machines for robot behaviour
hx-sys-operating-modes.Skill Description: Define robot operating modes and transitions — Define modes such as off, standby, teleoperated, autonomous, charging, maintenance and fault, with allowed transitions, entry conditions and who may command each change.

hx-sys-verification-method.Subject: Requirements engineering
hx-sys-verification-method.Skill Name: Assign a verification method to each requirement
hx-sys-verification-method.Prerequisite Names: Plan traceable verification; Write measurable robot requirements
hx-sys-verification-method.Skill Description: Assign a verification method to each requirement — Choose test, analysis, inspection or demonstration as the verification method for each requirement and justify the choice from cost, risk and observability.

rob3:Q06.Subject: Requirements and systems practice
rob3:Q06.Prerequisite Names: Version control with Git commits; Define subsystem interfaces
rob3:Q06.Skill Description: Maintain configuration and interface changes — Maintain configuration and interface changes

hx-sys-physical-architecture.Subject: System architecture and interfaces
hx-sys-physical-architecture.Prerequisite Names: Decompose robot functions into a function tree; Define subsystem interfaces
hx-sys-physical-architecture.Skill Description: Map functions to physical subsystems — Allocate each leaf function to hardware or software subsystems, and judge alternative allocations by coupling, interface count and testability.

hx-sys-iso-13482.Subject: Safety standards awareness
hx-sys-iso-13482.Skill Description: ISO 13482 personal care robot concepts — Explain how ISO 13482 classifies personal care robots and the hazards it emphasizes, such as instability, contact and autonomous behavior errors.

hx-sys-trade-criteria.Subject: Trade studies and budgets
hx-sys-trade-criteria.Skill Name: Define weighted criteria for a trade study
hx-sys-trade-criteria.Skill Description: Define weighted criteria for a trade study — Derive trade-study criteria from requirements, assign normalized weights, and define scoring scales so that alternatives can be compared consistently.

hx-sys-test-plan.Subject: Integration and test
hx-sys-test-plan.Prerequisite Names: Assign a verification method to each requirement
hx-sys-test-plan.Skill Description: Write a test plan — Write a test plan listing objectives, requirements covered, setup, equipment, sequence, pass criteria and safety precautions for a robot subsystem.

hx-sys-wbs.Subject: Project management
hx-sys-wbs.Skill Description: Build a work breakdown structure — Decompose the robot project into deliverable-oriented work packages that cover all hardware, software, testing and documentation work.

hx-sys-traceability-matrix.Subject: Requirements engineering
hx-sys-traceability-matrix.Prerequisite Names: Assign a verification method to each requirement
hx-sys-traceability-matrix.Skill Description: Build a requirements traceability matrix — Link every stakeholder need to its requirements, design elements and verification evidence in a matrix, and find orphan requirements and unverified needs.

hx-sys-reliability-basics.Subject: Reliability and maintenance
hx-sys-reliability-basics.Skill Name: Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function
hx-sys-reliability-basics.Skill Description: Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function — Compute reliability over a mission time from a constant failure rate, and relate failure rate, MTBF and probability of surviving a given duration.

hx-sys-safety-functions.Subject: Safety engineering
hx-sys-safety-functions.Prerequisite Names: Apply the risk reduction hierarchy; Define robot operating modes and transitions
hx-sys-safety-functions.Skill Description: Specify robot safety functions — Specify safety functions such as protective stop, speed limiting, zone limiting and torque limiting, each with trigger, response, response time and safe state.

hx-sys-interface-matrix.Subject: System architecture and interfaces
hx-sys-interface-matrix.Prerequisite Names: Define subsystem interfaces; Map functions to physical subsystems
hx-sys-interface-matrix.Skill Description: Build an N-squared interface matrix — Build an N-squared matrix of subsystem interfaces to enumerate every mechanical, electrical, data and thermal interaction and spot missing or unexpected couplings.

hx-sys-trade-study.Subject: Trade studies and budgets
hx-sys-trade-study.Prerequisite Names: Define weighted criteria for a trade study
hx-sys-trade-study.Skill Description: Run a weighted trade study — Score design alternatives, such as servo versus custom BLDC joints, against weighted criteria and document the recommended option and its rationale.

hx-sys-integration-order.Subject: Integration and test
hx-sys-integration-order.Prerequisite Names: Directed acyclic graphs and ordering; Build an N-squared interface matrix
hx-sys-integration-order.Skill Description: Choose an integration order — Order subsystem integration steps from a dependency graph so each step adds one unknown, choosing between bottom-up and thread-based sequences.

hx-sys-test-procedure.Subject: Integration and test
hx-sys-test-procedure.Skill Description: Write a step-by-step test procedure — Write a repeatable test procedure with numbered steps, expected readings and record fields so another person obtains comparable results.

hx-sys-milestone-plan.Subject: Project management
hx-sys-milestone-plan.Skill Name: Define milestones with entry and exit criteria
hx-sys-milestone-plan.Prerequisite Names: Assign a verification method to each requirement; Build a work breakdown structure
hx-sys-milestone-plan.Skill Description: Define milestones with entry and exit criteria — Define project milestones with clear demonstrable exit criteria tied to requirements and tests, rather than effort spent.

hx-sys-fmea.Subject: Reliability and maintenance
hx-sys-fmea.Prerequisite Names: Identify hazards and protective functions; Map functions to physical subsystems; Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function
hx-sys-fmea.Skill Description: Failure modes and effects analysis — Perform a failure modes and effects analysis listing each component failure mode, its effects, causes and detection, and rank them by severity, occurrence and detection.

hx-sys-system-reliability.Subject: Reliability and maintenance
hx-sys-system-reliability.Skill Name: Reliability of series and redundant systems
hx-sys-system-reliability.Prerequisite Names: Conditional probability and independence; Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function
hx-sys-system-reliability.Skill Description: Reliability of series and redundant systems — Calculate system reliability from component reliabilities for series chains and parallel redundancy, and identify the weakest elements.

hx-sys-requirement-allocation.Subject: System architecture and interfaces
hx-sys-requirement-allocation.Prerequisite Names: Map functions to physical subsystems; Build a requirements traceability matrix
hx-sys-requirement-allocation.Skill Description: Allocate and derive subsystem requirements — Allocate system requirements to subsystems and derive child requirements, such as splitting an end-to-end latency limit between perception, planning and actuation.

hx-sys-margin-policy.Subject: Trade studies and budgets
hx-sys-margin-policy.Prerequisite Names: Allocate system budgets; Apply a stated design margin
hx-sys-margin-policy.Skill Description: Apply maturity-based design margins — Set contingency margins on budgeted quantities according to design maturity, from estimated through measured, and shrink them as data improves.

hx-sys-test-report.Subject: Integration and test
hx-sys-test-report.Prerequisite Names: Write a step-by-step test procedure; Create logs and replayable tests
hx-sys-test-report.Skill Description: Write a test report — Write a test report that presents measured data, deviations from procedure, anomalies and a pass or fail verdict traced to each requirement.

hx-sys-risk-register.Subject: Project management
hx-sys-risk-register.Prerequisite Names: Probability rules; Define milestones with entry and exit criteria
hx-sys-risk-register.Skill Description: Maintain a project risk register — Keep a register of technical, schedule and supply risks with likelihood, impact, owner, mitigation and trigger, and review it at each milestone.

hx-sys-fault-tree.Subject: Reliability and maintenance
hx-sys-fault-tree.Skill Name: Build and evaluate a fault tree
hx-sys-fault-tree.Prerequisite Names: Boolean algebra; Failure modes and effects analysis; Reliability of series and redundant systems
hx-sys-fault-tree.Skill Description: Build and evaluate a fault tree — Build a fault tree for an undesired top event such as an uncommanded arm motion and compute its probability from basic event probabilities.

hx-sys-burn-in.Subject: Reliability and maintenance
hx-sys-burn-in.Skill Name: Plan burn-in to remove early failures
hx-sys-burn-in.Prerequisite Names: Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function; Write a step-by-step test procedure
hx-sys-burn-in.Skill Description: Plan burn-in to remove early failures — Use the bathtub curve to plan a burn-in period for new actuators and electronics that exposes early-life failures before the robot is used with people.

hx-sys-functional-safety.Subject: Safety standards awareness
hx-sys-functional-safety.Skill Name: Functional safety: IEC 61508 SIL and ISO 13849 PL
hx-sys-functional-safety.Prerequisite Names: Specify robot safety functions; Reliability of series and redundant systems
hx-sys-functional-safety.Skill Description: Functional safety: IEC 61508 SIL and ISO 13849 PL — Explain safety integrity levels and performance levels, how architecture, diagnostics and failure rates determine them, and why software alone rarely suffices.

hx-sys-mass-budget.Subject: Trade studies and budgets
